> gained, none lost**, eleven of them D548–D558 and every one reserved and cited before its entry
> existed. The other two are **D143**, which arrived by **amendment** — the entry D551's fix amended,
> quoted at the site to say which of its claims had been falsified — and **D140**, which arrived
> because an invariant of its own had been broken: it is the entry that added `GuideDrag::left_ruler`
> precisely so a new guide could not announce a discard before it had been off the bars once, D555's
> missed half reached that state by another door, and the repair cites D140 to name the promise it
> restores. So the standing rule *"citing the entry you are extending is what makes an old number
> reach code"* has three faces — extension, amendment, and the entry whose invariant you have just
> been shown to have violated — and the third is the one no reservation habit can anticipate, because
> nobody knows which entry a bug is about until the bug is understood. `CLAUDE.md`'s census paragraph
> carries the same widening.
>
> ⚠️ **Both figures were stale again by 2026-09-07 evening — 452 against 468 and 335 against 354 —
> and this time the entries count was stale for the reason the paragraph above predicts**: sixteen
> entries (D453–D468) were written by sweeps with no shell, each adding a heading *and* an index row.
> Re-counted rather than incremented: **468 headings against 468 index rows**, the two halves
> agreeing.
>
> The **354** is the census of that evening, set-differenced against `cc5fe7f` (the previous session's
> last commit): **336 → 354, eighteen gained, none lost.** Seventeen are D454–D470, every one of them
> reserved and cited by hand before its entry existed — the eighteenth is **D22**, an old number
> reaching code for the first time on a comment about why `pick_leaf` skips an occupied frame, which
> is this list's third reason and the only one nobody can plan for. ⚠️ **Two of the eighteen,
> D469 and D470, are cited and have no entry yet** — that is the reservation habit mid-flight rather
> than a defect, and it is what the set-difference is for: it says *which* numbers are outstanding
> instead of leaving a total that looks right.
>
> The claim that **every** cited D-number resolves to a heading or an index row here is separate from
> the count and has survived every re-run of it, most recently on 2026-09-06. Worth re-running rather
> than trusting: nothing fails when one stops, and on 2026-08-25 a count reasoned forward from the old
> figure came out two low, because *which* entries are cited from code is not a function of which
> entries exist.
>
> Read `architecture.md` for the design. Read this for where the implementation departed from it,
> and why. Entries are numbered in the order they were written rather than sorted; **§15.0 is an
> index of all of them in numeric order**, which is the way to find one without scrolling.
>
> Each entry carries a verdict — *Resolved*, *Keep*, *Intentional* or *Deviation*. A *Resolved* entry
> is history: the code no longer deviates, and what survives is the rule the episode left behind.
> The other three are live and describe the code as it stands.

---

## 15.0 Index

Every entry in numeric order, with its verdict. The body below is in the order entries were
written, not sorted, so this is the map. To jump to one, search the body for its marker —
`**D42 —`. A verdict shown here is the short form; several carry a qualification the entry states.

⚠️ **A *Fix* verdict here is the one that rots, because nothing restrikes it when the fix lands.**
The entry's body gets amended by whoever does the work; the index line is a second copy of the
verdict and is a line nobody is reading at that moment. Three of them — D334, D335, D336 — were
still asking for work that had been done for a fortnight, and in every case the entry's **own body
contradicted its index line**. So the standing check is one command:
`grep -nE '^- \*\*D[0-9]{1,3}\*\*.*\*Fix\*' docs/decisions.md`, and for each hit read the body before
believing the index. **A *Fix* that has been fixed is restruck rather than deleted** — the line keeps
the deviation, states the date the fix landed, and says how long it stood open, because "this asked
for work that was already done" is itself the finding. D334's line is the model.

- **D319** — The doc gate **cannot see inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module**: `cargo doc` builds without the `test` cfg, so no test's doc comment is link-checked — and in this project that is most of the prose there is. Closes the text/points half D320 left open, which was D261's failure itself: both menu rows dimmed while `Enter` opened the mode. *(Decided by the maintainer 2026-08-23 — "a locked group means everything inside is also locked, so it's an expected behavior, not a good to have" — built and tested, four new tests and seven flips; the ancestor walk had **no** test at all, and breaking it left the whole of `ondin-core` green. `menu::LayerState` carries the own flag and the ancestors' separately and **derives** the combination, because storing it made an impossible state spellable at a `..default()` fixture. The size badge this entry left "untouched on purpose" is **D348**. ⚠️ **A second ⚠️ of this entry's went the same way**: *"there is no analogous second door on image editing, so `edited_image` needs no guard of its own"* was false too, and the two doors it missed — a locked picture's crop and its outright replacement by a drop or `Ctrl+V` — are **D463**. ⚠️ **And a *verb* has a door of its own**: `canvas::reverse_subpaths`' fallback for a selected path outside point editing asked the kind and not the lock, which is **D514**)*
- **D322** — **A skew jumped on the first frame**: the lean was `atan(offset / span)` with the offset measured from the box's **centre**, so grabbing a side anywhere but its exact midpoint leant the shape before the pointer had moved. `Drag::Skew` carries `press` now and the offset is `p − press`. The variant's own doc comment asserted the rule that was wrong — "no start reference, the dragged side tracks the pointer absolutely, the way a resize handle does" — which is true of a resize handle, since a resize handle *is* the thing you grabbed; §9.4's and D52's copies went with it. The two points travel as `tools::SideDrag { press, at }` with a private `mapped`, clippy's `too_many_arguments` having noticed the transposition trap. ⚠️ A multi-selection's frame still *inflates* as the set shears, 300 → 340 measured — chrome, not arithmetic, and in `roadmap.md`)*
- **D323** — **A lock guards against accidents on the canvas, not against deliberate edits through a panel**, so the inspector's Transform fields committing on a locked layer is a **decided non-goal**. - **D324** — **A skewing set's frame leaned by inflating**: a set's box was the upright union of world bounds with `Handles.world` the identity, so it had nothing to lean with, and re-unioning the *previewed* members grew it — 300 wide → **340** in one frame. Put to the maintainer as an open question; the answer was *make every save atomic*. `crate::atomic::write` creates the parent directory, writes `<path>.writing`, `sync_all`s it and renames over the target. *(Built and tested 2026-08-28; Keep. A top-level module rather than one under `library/`, because five modules reach it from two subtrees — `store`, `project`, `cache`, `recovery` and `prefs` — and it is a filesystem primitive. ⚠️ **The window was neither small nor rare**: every one of these files is read back and *believed*, and `write_document` truncates the document before writing a byte, so the exposure was the whole of every save, the thirty-second autosave included. **What it gives, stated precisely because this rots into "saves are safe now"**: `rename` is atomic on POSIX and on Windows (`MoveFileEx` with `REPLACE_EXISTING`), and the `sync_all` extends that from process death to power loss — ⚠️ but **the directory entry is not synced**, which POSIX asks for and Rust does not portably expose, so a cut just after the rename can leave the old name on the old data. That is the pre-write state: nothing here can produce a torn file, and the residual risk is losing the new version, not corrupting the old one. ⚠️ **The temp name is derived rather than randomised, which is what bounds the debris** — one `.writing` per file ever written, consumed by that file's next save; 🚨 **reversed by D548**, that premise being about the *process* where the file is addressed by absolute path, so two Ondin instances saving one document tore the destination and the name carries a pid and a counter now, with the self-clearing replaced by a swept-and-age-gated one; and its extension keeps it out of `scan`, which matches exactly `ondin`. The test asserts the document's **bytes** are unchanged after each refusal, "returns `Err`" and "changed nothing" being two claims. `svg_in` **degrades** rather than failing a whole import — `numbers()` gains the finite filter `parse_len` already had, both `BezPath::from_svg` sites skip and report — and ⚠️ **a singular `transform` resolves to the identity**, the reachable half: `matrix(0,0,0,0,0,0)` is finite, and `local_for_world` inverts a zero determinant into six `NaN`s on the next drag. ⚠️ **A matching refusal in `verify_integrity` was written and removed as unreachable, which is the measurement worth keeping**: no JSON input can carry a non-finite `f64` at all — `serde_json` writes one as `null`, refuses `null` for an `f64`, and refuses `1e999` — both at `from_value`, one function above the walk. What is left is the *message*, which names neither node nor field; a custom deserializer per float is a decision rather than a fix)*

Snapped **outward**, keeping §5.11's posture that a stale range is a hand-edit rather than a corrupt tree, with a collapsed span then dropped by `normalize`. ⚠️ **The loader was never the only door** — `op_set_text` and `op_set_text_style` call the same function — which is D423's two-doors finding in the one subsystem where the second door is reached by typing)*
- **D423** — **`op_insert_subtree` refuses a set holding a node nobody lists as a child.** The op walked *from each node to its listed children* and never asked the converse; `claimed` was built and thrown away. A node whose `parent` is in the set is not a root, passes the single-root check, is inserted, and is listed by nobody. ⚠️ **Reachable from the public API alone** — two `capture_subtree` snapshots of one node taken at different moments compose into exactly that set — and it panics `DeleteNode`, `Reparent` and `Reorder` at their `expect("child must be listed in its parent")` sites and saves a file whose `load` fails with *"node(s) are not reachable from the root"*. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. One comparison, `claimed.len() + 1 != nodes.len()`; the loader has enforced it since it was written — check (5) — so the two doors into the tree were held to different standards, which §5.11 says they must not be. Every production caller already satisfies it, both sites feeding `remap_subtree` output from a single fresh capture; ⚠️ **what the module's own test doc calls "malformed subtrees the public API can never produce" is a false premise**, and what reaches this is anything that *composes* captures — the MCP write surface, an importer, a multi-step builder. Flip: the guard removed leaves `apply` returning `Ok` and the `DeleteNode` assertion below **panics** rather than failing, the more legible of the two symptoms)*

Measured — `canonical(Px(1e304))` is finite, `canonical(Px(1e305))` is `inf`. ⚠️ **The `is_finite` guard two lines above does not help, being asked of the *input*.** *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. That is a document that never opens again, and it is reachable through the documented door, `Spans::set` routing every value through the canonicalizer — which makes this the one position in D421's class where the **operation-level guard would be wrong**: it would report a refused letter-spacing edit for a number the user is entitled to type. `round_to_places` returns such a magnitude unchanged, exact rather than approximate, the gap between representable neighbours being astronomically larger than `1e-4`. *A sanitizer producing the value it was written to exclude is the shape to remember; the guard was in the right function and one statement too early*)*
- **D425** — **A `Length` field's px range is derived from its `%` range, and a range no longer rewrites the document.** Two field defects with one root — *a bound stated in the wrong place acts on the wrong thing.* There was exactly **one** px cap in the Type panel, `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT_PX`, named for line height and used by all **nine** `Length` fields, so no field's two ends bounded the same quantity and the unit chip destroyed values: decoration thickness `Px(50)` at 16pt came back **32px**, letter spacing `Px(-100)` came back **−8px**, a **625×** disagreement at 8pt. And egui's `clamp_existing_to_range` defaults to `true` on every frame, so a stored value outside a range was pulled to the nearest end and `mark_changed` reported the widget's own rewrite as a **user edit** — an imported blur radius of 1200 became 1000 on the frame the panel first drew it, with nobody touching anything. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. `Bounds` loses its `px` field, `px_range_for` derives it as `Length::in_unit` does, and the constant is **deleted** rather than repaired — a px cap that is not the `%` cap in the other unit is a second quantity and wants naming as one. `.clamp_existing_to_range(false)` is one line for all **82** numeric fields, none of which opts out, which is §5.3's *"clamped where the outline is built … not on the way in"* applied to the widget. ⚠️ **`both_ends_of_every_length_field_bound_the_same_quantity` was vacuous first and its own flip said so** — the loop called `px_range_for` directly and never went through `Bounds` — so it now asserts the `Bounds` faces *are* the shared derivation; three font sizes, because at 16pt alone the old pair was only 62× apart. ⚠️ **Both clamps were on a *draft*, the third instance of that shape and the one that reached a user**: `NudgeStep::step` clamps at the reader now (D349's own ruling for the other ranged number in `prefs.json`), because the Settings field once shipped a `0.01` floor, `Prefs` has no migration, and an upgraded install painted **1** in the modal over a document where an arrow key still moved 0.1px)*

The test asserts an **empty** message returns the run count to the control's — the region absent rather than present-and-blank, which is the version that passes a presence check while saying nothing)*
- **D427** — **`deps_forbidden` read a tree nothing builds, and `ondin-mcp` was never a subject at all.** It ran `cargo tree -p ondin-core` while every gate that *compiles* core resolves the whole workspace — and with `resolver = "3"` those are different closures, measured on core's own dependencies: `smallvec` gains `union` under `--workspace`, asked for by `wgpu-hal` and reaching the build only through `ondin-render`. One member declaring `parley = { features = ["system"] }` would put a DirectWrite binding into the closure core is compiled against and this test would have stayed green. ⚠️ **§3's *"`ondin-mcp` contains no rendering or UI dependency"* was false**: the crate declared `ondin-export`, which reaches vello, wgpu and naga — on a manifest line with **zero call sites**, as had `serde` and `serde_json` beside it. *(Fixed, widened and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. The walk takes `--workspace` and cuts out the subtree under each subject, unification only ever *adding*; one invocation, not two, a second being a second chance to contend for the package-cache lock. The prefix list is enumerated rather than inferred now — `"eframe".starts_with("egui")` is **false**, and so are `emath`, `ecolor`, `epaint`, `glutin` and `raw-window-handle`, every one really in the app's tree. ⚠️ **No gate in this workspace can see an unused dependency**: `unused_crate_dependencies` is allow-by-default, no crate root enables it, clippy has no equivalent, and it fires per *target* so a test-only dep reads as unused. Flip-checked three ways, **the negative one already standing**: `"kurbo"` added fails with it named; `ondin-export` restored fails with **sixteen** crates under `ondin-mcp`, two of which the old prefixes missed; and `"egui"` is in the list while `egui` is in the tree under `ondin-app` with the test green, which is what says the walk excludes what is not under a subject. An `unseen` assertion guards the parse, or a format change leaves `violations` empty and the assertion green. **Fix with the allowlist inversion**: it was blocked on §3's own permitted list being right — it omitted `roxmltree`, `skrifa`, `read-fonts` and `flo_curves` — and §3 was corrected the same day, so the stated blocker is gone and only the test's doc comment still names it)*
- **D428** — **A transaction that changes nothing is not an undo step.** A completed interaction that turned out to change nothing committed a full one: click into a value field, type nothing, click away — undo depth 0→1, the document dirtied, autosave and the crash snapshot fired, and `Ctrl+Z` had to be pressed twice to be seen. A resize handle pressed and released without moving is the other route. `commit_inner` dropped only *empty* transactions, and a no-op transaction is not an empty one. ⚠️ **A third route was named here — *"a multi-row layers drop that lands rows where they already are, which emits one net-zero `Reorder` per row"* — and this guard never covered it** (D532): the net is zero and the operations are not, each `Reorder` moving its row to an index it is not at yet, so `changes_nothing` answers `false` for every one of them and is right to; the drop is guarded in `layers::plan_layer_move` now, and **a composition of real operations that returns to where it started is a shape no per-operation test can see**. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. Eleven sites across three routes — click, type and drag — closed at **one seam**, three per-door guards having been proposed and none of them able to cover the next door. `Operation::changes_nothing` is **exhaustive with no wildcard**, so a new variant must answer rather than inherit a guess, and `false` is the safe answer — a wrong `true` silently drops an edit. **An operation whose subject is missing answers `false`**, and so do the kind gates `apply` enforces, or the guard would swallow the error instead of the edit. The four span arms compare **what `apply` would store** rather than what the caller handed over, `SetGeometry` is asked of the **result** (`GeometryPatch::applied_to` against the node's kind), and equality is of the **value written**: `-0.0` equals `0.0`, `NaN` equals nothing, so a non-finite operation is never a no-op and still reaches `OpError::NonFinite` (D421). `Transaction::changes_nothing` is **all, not any**, which is the whole specification — *Hide* over a mixed selection is per-layer no-ops that add up to something. ⚠️ **The guard still calls `clear_gesture_preview`**: a no-op commit is the end of a gesture even though it is not an edit, and returning before that clear would trade an undo step for the stale-preview failure `commit_inner` is already annotated for (D109/D316/D317), arriving by a new door. ⚠️ *The `Reorder` "adjusted for the removal" flip failed on the **negative** half*, calling a real swap a no-op rather than missing a no-op, and the app-side test's first `!can_undo` was vacuous against its own fixture. ⚠️ **Amended 2026-09-08: it also closed `[S23.1-L1-03]` — the palette chip whose colour is already in the slot, measured at `undo_depth 0 → 1` with the brush byte-identical — and nothing said so for seven sessions.** Pinned now by `picker::grid_orphan_tests::a_palette_chip_already_in_the_slot_costs_no_undo_step`, driven at `write_slot` rather than at a chip coordinate; and **the general point is this entry's own price**: a guard at a choke point closes doors nobody enumerates, so the doors it closed are recorded nowhere and the next reader cannot tell a covered door from an uncovered one)*
- **D429** — **The open document follows a library file that moves, in memory as well as on disk.** D364's *"renaming or deleting the open document moves the session with it"* and D379's *"the open document follows its folder exactly as it follows its file through a move"* were both half true. Every one of these operations **edits the file** — `store::rename` writes a new `meta.name`, `store::move_to_project` a new `meta.project` — and the session's `Document` was never told, so **the next save undid the operation**, writing the old value back into the file the user had just moved. Measured on *Move to project*: `p-1` → `p-2` → `p-1` on disk, after which the dashboard correctly filed the card under the project the user had moved it out of, because that is what the file said. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. ⚠️ **A second and worse door**: `delete_project`'s follow was written `if session.path == Some(entry.path) && !keep_files`, so on the **transfer** branch it did nothing at all — the session went on naming a file in the deleted project's folder, the next autosave recreated it there from a document still carrying the dead project id, and the library then held **two files with one `meta.id`**, which version history, the cover cache and `recovery::pending` all key on. `OndinApp::open_document_follows` is one helper rather than the two lines copied a third time: the guard, the clone and the write-back must not diverge and only the field differs, so the patch is a closure. Four call sites; ⚠️ **one of them, `Act::Restore`, is unreachable today and is written anyway** — `trash_or_purge` clears `session.path` twenty lines up, which is a fact about a different function, and the day it stops the arm would silently become the rename bug again. Both tests assert **the file after the next save** first and the in-memory metadata second, because the loss is what the file says and the memory is the mechanism. ⚠️ *The three existing transfer tests were green throughout and always would be*: none of them opens a document, and everything about the files was always right)*
- **D430** — **_Move my library_ re-points the session through the path map, not a prefix swap.** **The last of the codebase review's seven Criticals.** `session.path` is absolute, so a migration left it naming a file in the folder the library had just abandoned: the next save recreated the document *there*, while the new root already held the copy `relocate` had carried across under the same `meta.id`. Two files, one identity — the library listed only the migrated copy and every edit made after the move went to the one nothing lists. `prefs.last_document` was the same bug one launch later. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. ⚠️ **`relocate.rs`'s own module comment stated the opposite as settled fact** — *"A library moved mid-session leaves the app writing into the new root on its next tick either way"* — which is true of the **snapshot**, `drop_recovery` re-reading `library.root` against a key that is the document id, and false of the **document**, whose path is absolute. ⚠️ **A path map and not a prefix swap, which is the part that is not obvious**: `relocate` renames into a collision (`naming::unique_stem`), so `old/kestrel/notes.ondin` can arrive as `new/kestrel/notes-1.ondin` and a caller re-joining the relative path under the new root would point the session at a file belonging to a **different document**. `Moved` carries the `(from, to)` pairs, `documents()` is derived from them rather than counted alongside — so the status line and the map cannot disagree about which files went — and `Moved` loses `Copy`. Sidecars are deliberately not in the map, nothing outside the module holding a path to a version file or a snapshot, both being found by id. Two flips, each failing at an assertion the other leaves green: deleting the re-point loop fails at the session still naming the old root; `strip_prefix(&old_root).join(&new_root)` fails with the two paths printed **identical**, which is why the test seeds a document of the same name at the destination)*
- **D431** — **A migration that cannot move a file renames it or says so.** `merge_tree` had one collision rule — skip — and it was only ever argued for `.versions`, where a path is `<document id>/<unix seconds>.ondin` and a collision really is the same document at the same instant. The same line applied to `.trash` **strands a document**: `store::trash` uniquifies within one folder and knows nothing about any other, so two libraries can each hold a `notes.ondin` that are different documents, and the source's was left in a folder the app no longer reads, **not counted in `failed`**, under a status line saying *"Moved 2 file(s)"* — and `purge_trash` only reads the current root, so it could never be swept either. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. Three policies, one per tree, each argued at its `Collision` variant: `.versions` → `Identical`, skip silently, nothing being lost; `.trash` → `Rename`, the arrival taking a suffix through the same `naming::unique_stem` `store::trash` and `store::file_document` already use within one folder; `.recovery` → `Stranded`, left where it is and **counted in `failed`** so the summary says so. ⚠️ **The renaming is what makes the third one different**: a snapshot's stem *is* the document id it belongs to, `recovery::pending` matches on it and `recovery::remove` refuses a stem that is not a minted id, so a `<id>-1.ondin` would be offered to the user and then be **undiscardable** — worse than being left behind and told about. A collision there needs two libraries holding one document id, which is a hand-copied file rather than anything the app does. ⚠️ **The flip is the interesting half**: `.trash` set back to `Identical` fails at the file assertion with the source document simply absent, and **`moved.failed` stays 0 under it** — the run that loses the file and the run that does not are indistinguishable from the status line, so a test asserting only the counters would have been green. Bodies are read as text so a failure *names* what went missing. **Fix**: `scan::collect` skips any entry whose `file_name().to_str()` is `None`, so a `.ondin` whose Windows filename is not valid Unicode is invisible to the migration too — never reproduced, not closed, and carried on the roadmap)*
- **D432** — **A read-only document's trash retention starts when it is deleted.** The Windows read-only attribute refuses exactly **one** of the three steps a delete takes, and it is the middle one. Measured: `fs::rename` into `.trash` is allowed, `fs::remove_file` is allowed too — Rust's implementation clears the attribute and retries — and the `OpenOptions::write(true).open` inside `trash_stamp` is `PermissionDenied`, and *its* result was the one being discarded. So the trashed copy kept the mtime of its last **edit**, and a document deleted after a year untouched was permanently removed by the very next sweep while the Trash screen's own heading said *"kept for 30 days"*. Nothing was reported at any point. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. ⚠️ **`trash`'s own comment argued the wrong way** — *"errs towards purging it sooner — never towards keeping something the user asked to go"* — where the architecture calls the trash the library's **only** undo, so silently permanent deletion is the one outcome this feature exists to prevent; corrected in place. The attribute is cleared for the length of the touch and the **original `Permissions` object** put back, not `set_readonly(true)`: a document is marked read-only to protect it and restoring one from the trash must give back the file the user had, and on Unix `set_readonly(true)` would mean 0o444 and drop write permission from a group that had it. `owner_may_write` is cfg-split for the mirror of that reason — `set_readonly(false)` means **0o666**, world-writable on Unix whatever the file's mode was — so the Unix arm sets `mode | 0o200` and only the Windows arm touches the single bit; clippy's `permissions_set_readonly_false` is what named this, firing on the first draft. What is still discarded is the *unmeasured* remainder, and deliberately: the delete has already succeeded, and reporting it as a failure would be a lie about a file that has moved)*
- **D433** — **The name search wraps at `u32::MAX` instead of panicking out of a duplicate.** Rename a layer to `Rectangle 4294967295` and press `Ctrl+D`: `copy_name` starts the search at `n.saturating_add(1)`, which saturates to a number **already taken** — the original's own name, which `CopyNames::rename` puts in `taken` because `child_names(parent, &[])` excludes nothing — so `free_name` found it and ran `n += 1`, an **overflow panic out of core on the UI thread during an ordinary duplicate**, taking whatever was unsaved with it. Release did not panic and answered `"Rectangle 0"`, a name `numbered` documents as impossible and refuses to parse, so the copy was mis-classified as hand-typed for the rest of its life. Both measured, in both profiles. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. A second reachable spelling needs no `u32::MAX` in the typed name: `X 4294967294` beside a sibling `X 4294967295`. ⚠️ **The doc comment's own bound argument was the drift** — *"a parent would need four billion children to exhaust it"* is true of `created_name`, whose `from` is always 1, and **false of `copy_name`**, whose `from` is parsed out of a string the user typed and whose loop needs *one* iteration. That paragraph is rewritten rather than deleted, because the reasoning it replaced is the reason nobody looked. The search wraps to 1, which is `created_name`'s own rule and produces a name in the series: a copy would rather sit just above its original, but at `u32::MAX` there is no "just above" to have. The final line — reachable only if all four billion names are taken — answers a **duplicate**, which is legal here (D127) rather than a name the parser rejects. Both flips run: `n += 1` fails in debug with *"attempt to add with overflow"* and in release at *"a name the parser can read back: \"Rectangle 0\""*, which is why the parser assertion is not decoration)*
- **D434** — **A raster size the renderer can actually take, on every axis and after the pad.** Three defects, one sentence: *an area cap cannot see a per-side limit, and the size that is capped is not the size that is rendered.* `MAX_RASTER_SIDE` was `u16::MAX`, **exactly the value `vello_common` documents as the one it panics on**, so the clamp that exists to prevent a panic handed the renderer one — `ondin export --png --width 65535` aborted, and so did a plain 1× export of a document whose one rect is `1e30` wide, no flag involved and only geometry a `.ondin` can carry. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. **This amends D274 and §7**, whose *"the pixel count is capped at the CPU rasterizer's `u16` per side"* is now wrong, and `viewport_at`'s own doc promised the opposite. The new value is `511 × 128 = 65408` and **both factors are vello's** — one depth bucket per `DEPTH_BUCKET_WIDTH = 128` pixels and `bucket_span`'s `index as u16 * DEPTH_BUCKET_WIDTH` — which also clears `snap_to_tile_coordinates`, needing a multiple of 4 at most 65532. ⚠️ **Neither vello constant is public**, so the number cannot be derived at compile time, a vello upgrade can silently invalidate it, and `a_raster_at_the_cap_renders_on_either_axis` is the only thing that would go red. Second: `padded_square` computed `side * side * 4` in **`u32`**, overflowing at `side == 32768` — a 4096×64 banner at 8× is an ordinary export set — which in debug panicked and in release wrapped to **exactly 0**, allocated `vec![0u8; 0]` and ran off the end one line later, killing a whole `--all` run before a single file was written. Now a named `square_bytes`; ⚠️ *the result is still unbounded*, which is a size decision left to `[S8.2-L5-05]` and stated in the code. Third: the Export panel's row preview reached **both**, `MAX_PREVIEW_PX` being an area cap where neither failure is about area. ⚠️ **A defect the review did not have was found by writing the first half's control and watching it crash**: a 32768×120 raster is 3.9 M pixels, under the area cap, and `ctx.load_texture` panics outright, so each side is now tested against the **device's** `max_texture_side` read off the context — inside `eframe::App::update`, with no `catch_unwind` anywhere in the app)*
- **D435** — **A font axis with a reversed or non-finite range is usable rather than fatal.** A `.ttf` whose `fvar` `opsz` record carries `minValue > maxValue` registers cleanly — `skrifa` returns the raw `AxisRecord` Fixed values with no validation of any kind and fontique's own parse is not a filter either — and the **next `text::layout` of any text node** panicked with *"min > max, or either was NaN. min = 200.0, max = 32.0"*. `f64::clamp` is an `assert!`, so this fires in **release**. The guard on that path is `optical_size_is_auto`, which is the default, so every ordinary text node was armed the moment such a family was registered; `register_fonts` is fed by the machine's own system fonts and by downloaded web faces, so this is not hostile-only, and if the *document's* family is that font it fires at every launch — including through `library/cover.rs · rasterize`, the seam D422 and D423 also land on. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-06; Keep. Closes review group G11. `FontAxis::from_fvar` is now **the one place a `FontAxis` is built from a file**: there were two, `family_axes` and `family_axes_locked`, differing only in where the name comes from — the divergence this project's own `is_paintable` comment predicts — so a guard added to one would have been missing from the other. It orders the ends, replaces a non-finite end with the other, and pulls the `default` inside the range, `fvar` promising the one no more than the other. `FontAxis::clamp` replaces `f64::clamp` at both readers (`text::axis_settings` and the typography panel's `opsz` Manual switch), the fields being `pub` and a later reader of `fvar` able to skip the constructor. ⚠️ **Both halves of `ordered` are load-bearing and they are different failures**: a reversed pair panics `clamp`, and a `NaN` end panics it too — and `f64::min`/`f64::max` **return `NaN` for a pair of them** rather than filtering it out, so ordering alone would have left the second open and looked complete. Both flips were run and **both were mis-predicted in the same direction**: each fails one line earlier than expected, inside `from_fvar` itself, with the finding's own panic verbatim, because the constructor is a second reader of its own range)*
- **D436** — **A boolean carrying an effect pops the layer it pushed.** `paint_node` pushes a node's effect layer near the top and pops it at the very **end** of the function; the `Boolean` arm returns from the middle. - **D534** — **A bare click no longer flattens a mixed corner radius.** `inspector::inspector_appearance`'s single corner-radius field shows `uniform(corners)` or, when the four disagree, `largest(corners)` — so that **dragging** it starts from the shape's own scale — and then handed `GeometryPatch::CornerRadius(r)`, which sets **all four**, to `edit_valve` unconditionally. `edit_valve` commits on the engaged→released transition a click produces and compares no value against the document, so a rect with corners `(10, 0, 0, 0)`, clicked into and clicked away from with nothing typed and nothing dragged, became `(10, 10, 10, 10)` with `undo_depth 0 → 1` — three corners the user never touched, gone. ⚠️ **The no-op family cannot see this one, which is why only the *mixed* case was ever visible**: over an *agreeing* set the write is a genuine no-op and D428's `changes_nothing` has absorbed it at `commit_inner` since it was written, and over a disagreeing one the transaction really does change the document, so D428 is right to let it through and the guard has to be at the field. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. Closes `[S14.3-L1-01]`. `if shared.is_some() || r != seed`, where `seed` is the number the field was seeded with — **`paint_row`'s `!hazy || moved` at a second field** (D465), the same accident for the same reason, and the two entries name each other. ⚠️ **What it gives up on purpose** is typing the shown number over a mixed set, which reads as *"flatten them all to this"* and now does nothing; the per-corner disclosure one button to the right is that edit's door, and `paint_row` makes the identical trade at the identical seam. **A gap rather than a contradiction**: D53 names this field only for the *readout*, and §5.7a's no-op promise is D428's, which is right about this write. ⚠️ **And it widens D465, whose paragraph reads *"every other Mixed numeric field in the inspector was safe"*** — this field is not a *Mixed* field at all, it prints a number, so the population is *fields seeded from one member of a disagreeing set* and the word is not what marks them. `inspector::mixed_corner_radius_tests`, two tests, the aim point `(200, 60)` found by sweeping and written down; ⚠️ **the harness feeds the panel from `session.display_node` and not `session.doc`**, a live drag living in the preview, so a `corners0` re-read from the committed document re-seeds `r` every frame and the release commits `r == seed` — measured, the file passes with the fix deleted. **Double-flipped**: the guard removed is red at `(10,10,10,10)` for `(10,0,0,0)`; the guard removed *and* the three claim assertions disabled leaves the drag control green, which is what says the control is a control. §5.3 and §9.4 amended, and D465 with them)*
- **D535** — **A cancelled opacity digit does not commit itself 600 ms later.** Press `4` with a layer selected: the canvas previews 40% and the document correctly still holds 1.0, the first digit being a preview by design (**D210**). The right-click cancel, the other door onto `app::cancel_gesture`, had it identically. **The cancel fired and did its job**: `set_opacity_pct_on` previews through `EditorSession::set_preview`, which sets `preview_holds_session = false`, so the opacity preview *is* a gesture preview, `has_gesture_preview()` is true and `cancel_gesture` is the rung `escape` stops on. What it never touched was `self.opacity_entry`, absent from a clearing list that names `drag`, `guide_previews`, `layer_drag`, `paint_drag`, `alt_clone`, `autopan_total`, `session_scrub`, `settings_scrub`, `grid_scrub`, `grid_paint` and `chrome_hold` — so `fold_opacity_entry`, which runs unconditionally on every editor frame, still found the entry and still ran the commit arm on the deadline. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. Closes `[S16.2-L1-01]`. One line, `self.opacity_entry = None;`, beside `self.grid_paint = None;`. **It belongs in `cancel_gesture` and not on the `escape` ladder** because the right-click is the other door, and **the digit window is a gesture even though nothing is held down**. ⚠️ **The round's first instance against a *Resolved* entry, and D210's own sentence is what made this look covered**: *"the commit happens when the window shuts, **whichever way it shuts**"* reads as covering `Escape`, while D210 and `shortcuts.md` §2 both enumerate exactly two ways it shuts — a second digit, or the deadline — and neither mentions a cancel. A cancelled gesture owes zero transactions (§9.3), so this is the third way and it shuts the window without committing; D210 amended to name it, and ⚠️ **`shortcuts.md` §2's copy of the two-way enumeration is still short and is not this entry's to fix.** `app::cancelled_opacity_digit_tests`, two. Flip A, the line removed, bites at the predicted site — the post-deadline opacity, `0.4` against `1.0` — which was easy to predict because the two earlier assertions are identical in both versions. Flip B is the *plausible* wrong fix, deleting `fold_opacity_entry`'s commit, since *"stop the deadline committing"* closes the finding and removes the feature in one line: the main test stays **green** under it and the control goes red at `1.0` against `0.4`. §9.3 amended, and D210 with it)*
- **D536** — **A `Boolean` belongs on the subtree cull's kind list.** `scene::paint_node`'s `bounds_cover_subtree` was `node.children().is_empty() || node.clip() || matches!(node.kind(), NodeKind::Group | NodeKind::Root)`. A boolean has children, does not clip, and is neither — so the predicate came out `false` and the `if` short-circuited before ever consulting `res.ink_bounds(id)`. **Every boolean in the document was walked, `paint_shape`d and encoded on every frame, wherever the view was.** Measured in release against a counting painter, viewport at `(-1000,-1000)..(-500,-500)` and the containers parked at x ≥ 10,000: 800 booleans issued **801** fills at **0.106 ms** of walk alone, where 800 groups issued **1** at 0.0116 ms. Each of those 801 fills also clones a whole `BezPath` sized by the boolean's own segment count, which is why a page of converted icon artwork is the worst case rather than a contrived one. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. Closes `[S11.1-L4-05]`. `| NodeKind::Boolean { .. }` on the `matches!`. **A boolean is the strongest member of that list, not a doubtful one**: the binding's criterion is that the bounds cover everything below, and the walk stops dead at a boolean — its children are its operands, not artwork — so its cached ink bounds cover its whole subtree *exactly*, where a group's merely happen to. **CLAUDE.md's named hazard one crate over from where it was last swept** — *"adding a `NodeKind` is a sweep the compiler only half-finds — grep the `matches!(kind` predicates after it goes quiet"* — `[S2.1-MATRIX]` having built that matrix for `ondin-core`'s six `_`-armed predicates with `ondin-render` outside its scope. ⚠️ **The flip that removes `NodeKind::Group` from the list changes nothing, and that is why this survived**: with `Group` off, a parked group is no longer culled as a subtree, but the walk descends to its children, which are leaves, and every one is culled individually — same fill count, more walking. **A group's descendants get culled leaf by leaf whatever the list says, so the list has never been observable in a fill count for a group**, and *the kind that was missing from it is the only kind whose absence it can be caught by*. The group arm is a control for the harness, not for the list, and this test's prose said otherwise until the flip was run. Two tests in `ondin-render/tests/render.rs`: `an_off_screen_boolean_is_culled_like_an_off_screen_group`, and `the_boolean_cull_does_not_grow_with_the_number_parked`, which pins the *shape* at 1 and 40 rather than asserting a time. §6.3 amended)*
- **D537** — **A zero length keeps its unit across a save.** `Length::is_zero` answers `true` for `Em(0.0)` as readily as for `Px(0.0)` and was the `skip_serializing_if` predicate on all seven optional lengths in `typography.rs` — `letter_spacing`, `word_spacing` and `baseline_shift` on `TextStyle`, `spacing`, `indent`, `indent_start` and `indent_end` on `ParagraphStyle`. `Length::default()` is `Px(0.0)`, so a field holding `Em(0.0)` was **absent from the file** and deserialized as `Px(0.0)`: set the letter-spacing field to `%`, leave it at 0, save, reopen, and the suffix reads `px`. Measured — `Em(0) reload = Px(0.0) unit=Px`. **Zero is the only value this can go wrong at**, and that is what hid it: `resolve` gives `0.0` for both, so nothing rendered ever disagrees, while the unit stays observable in the panel — and the producer is a pure model call, `Length::in_unit` mapping `Px(0.0)` straight to `Em(0.0)`, which is exactly what the `px`/`%` suffix toggle calls. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. Closes the **save half** of `[S6.1-L1-03]`. `Length::is_default_zero`, `matches!(self, Length::Px(v) if *v == 0.0)`, on all seven. Costs four bytes and only where the unit is `Em`; the common case — a field never touched, at the `Px(0.0)` default — is elided exactly as before, so no existing file grows. `Length::is_zero` stays, having two real callers in `ondin-export/src/svg.rs` that ask a genuinely different question. ⚠️ **No schema bump, and this entry says so rather than leaving it to be worked out**: the change only ever *adds* a key an older reader already understands, the fields being `#[serde(default)]` and `Em` no new variant, so a file written here loads in an older build as `Em(0.0)` and one written there loads here as `Px(0.0)` — which is what it always meant. Invisible to `io::MIGRATIONS`. ⚠️ **The other half is deliberately left open and the two halves pull opposite ways.** A zero-valued `Em` span is still kept by `normalize`, which compares structurally, and so still reports *Mixed* through `shared_in` for text whose letter spacing is zero everywhere — but **preserving the unit *requires* keeping the span**, so making `Em(0.0)` and `Px(0.0)` compare equal would fix the readout by throwing away the very thing this predicate exists to keep. The readout is a comparison on the *resolved* value and belongs at the reader; `roadmap.md`'s *Now · Text* carries it. `typography::tests::a_zero_length_keeps_its_unit_across_a_save`, asserting on the JSON text rather than on the round-tripped value, because a value that round-trips says nothing about whether the key was written, and covering a paragraph field too because the predicate is named on both types. Both flips bite: `is_zero` put back on `letter_spacing` fails on the first assertion, the key absent; `is_default_zero` made to return `false` unconditionally fails on the **control**, which is the assertion that keeps the fix from becoming *"write every field always"*. §5.4 amended)*
- **D538** — **The image adjust pipeline bounds its range, not just finiteness.** `ImageAdjust::pipeline`'s guard asked only `is_finite()`. `Adjustment::set` has clamped to `-1..=1` all along and its doc gives the reason verbatim — *"a range the model does not enforce is a range a hand-edited file ignores. The tone curve's monotonicity argument only holds inside this range"* — but `set` is the door the **panel** uses and a file does not. Two measured pictures, both from a `.ondin` that loads cleanly and survives a round trip: `"exposure": 1000.0` is a finite `f32`, so `matrix()` computes `2f32.powf(1000.0)` = `inf` and `inf * 0.0` in the compose makes **all twenty coefficients `NaN`** — every pixel of the photograph rendering `[0,0,0,255]`, a solid black rectangle, on the canvas and in the PNG, the threshold exactly `|exposure| >= 128` where `f32` overflows at `2^128`; and `"shadows": 2.0` makes `curve()` **double back at 12 of its 32 steps**, source black coming out `[204,204,204]` against source mid-grey's `[179,179,179]`, so the dark end of the picture is inverted, the threshold being the file's own algebra — the derivative of `v + 0.4s(1−v)²` at `v = 0` is `1 − 0.8s`, so anything above `1.25` is non-monotonic. ⚠️ **And it is a backend divergence, which is what makes it worse than a wrong picture**: both pixel backends quantise `NaN` to zero and agree on black, while the SVG writer passes every coefficient through `fmt` and emits `<feColorMatrix values="NaN NaN …">`, which a viewer rejects outright — one number, black in two writers and invalid markup in the third. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. Closes `[S9.1-L5-02]`. The guard is `!v.is_finite() || !(-1.0..=1.0).contains(&v)`. **Refused rather than clamped, and the reason is not stylistic**: `is_default` already reports such a value as non-neutral, so clamping would make the file *draw* something it does not *say* — the panel would read 1000 and the canvas would show the picture at 1 — where refusing draws the unadjusted picture, the one honest answer available to a reader handed a number the model forbids. ⚠️ **The operation door was already shut against the *other* half of this and the finding's brief said otherwise**: since D452, `build::image_ref_is_finite` weighs all seven sliders at `op_set_fills`, so a `NaN` exposure never reaches the model at all — which is precisely why both witnesses here are **finite**. That makes this **D492's class at a third field**, *a number that is finite is not thereby a usable one*, and the invariant list in §3 says so. New arms on `image::adjust_tests::an_impossible_value_is_refused_at_both_doors`, the test named for this guard, which had probed `NaN` only — plus in-range controls at −1.0, 1.0 and ±0.5, because a predicate written `(-1.0..1.0)` or `(0.0..=1.0)` would pass every other assertion. Both flips bite, **including the clamping one**: the assertion is on `pipeline().is_none()` and on `is_default()` rather than on a pixel, precisely so a clamping version — which draws a perfectly good picture the file does not describe — cannot pass. §5.5a amended)*
- **D539** — **Drawing the Layout grid panel does not repair the grid it draws.** **Coverage, not a behaviour change.** Three of the four grid fields carry a range the model does not — `count` is `1..=1000` where `layout.rs`'s own field doc says *"Zero draws nothing rather than being refused"*, and `margin` and `size` have floors — and egui's `DragValue` clamps a stored value into its range on **every frame, interacted with or not**. `ui::value_field_f64` took `let before = *value` around the `add` and called `mark_changed` when it moved, `grid_rows`' `changed |= r.changed()` was then true and `grid_step` returned `Commit`, so **merely selecting the frame rewrote the document and pushed an undo step**: `count: 0 → 1`, `margin: −8 → 0`, `size: 0.5 → 1.0`, each `undo_depth 0 → 1` and `is_dirty()` true, with no events of any kind. `is_dirty()` is the expensive half — autosave and the crash snapshot then write the repaired document back. **It was already closed** by `ui::value_field_f64`'s one-line `.clamp_existing_to_range(false)`, the fix `[S14.5-L1-02]`'s imported blur radius earned (D425), which covers all 82 numeric fields at once. *(Tested 2026-09-08; Test only. Closes `[S14.4-L1-03]`, and `[S14.4-L1-02]` with it — the image card's **Scale** field is the same door and the same line, its floor being `cover_scale` while the value handed in is `crop_scale`, two quantities that are equal at cover and free to part afterwards: `crop_reframed` holds the picture's scale fixed while the frame moves, so a resize that grows only the height raises `cover_scale` past a `crop_scale` that has not moved, and the field was then handed a number below its own range. ⚠️ **Read rather than driven, and this entry says which**: the *mechanism* is verified in `inspector::image_edit_card` — floor `scale.map_or(1.0, |(_, c)| (c * 100.0).max(0.01))`, value `scale.map_or(100.0, |(s, _)| s * 100.0)` — and the finding's `400%` for a crop at `200%` is not re-measured here. **What is new is the test**, `inspector::rhythm_tests::drawing_the_grid_panel_does_not_repair_the_grid_it_draws`, a symptom guard over a door fixed three panels away in a shared widget, with `ui.rs`'s `a_stored_value_outside_a_fields_range_is_shown_rather_than_rewritten` pinning the mechanism. 🚨 **The flip that must bite came back green, because the test was drawing nothing at all.** `EditorSession::adopt_document` clears the selection; the fixture adopts a second time to get a *clean* session, `is_dirty()` being half the claim and a session that has just committed its own fixture being dirty for the fixture's sake; that undid `frame_with_grids`' own `set_one`; and `inspector_layout_grids` draws nothing for an empty selection. So three frames of a panel that never ran asserted, truthfully, that nothing had been rewritten — **every assertion green, in the right order, against the right numbers, about a panel that was not on screen**, and only the flip said so. A `drawn > 20` clickable-control floor is the fixture's precondition now. Closes `[S14.1-L1-02]`. Both sides go through `pen_anchors` → `pen_path`/`pen_radii` **for the comparison only** — nothing about what is stored changes, so this is not the load-time normalisation that would be invariant 9's migration. Nothing is lost: the two forms differ only by a zero-length segment and by radii already zero, and a quad canonicalises to the cubic with the same curve, so a click on an imported quad stops rewriting it too. `pen_path`'s own doc claimed the round trip was the identity *"up to a quad elevated to a cubic and a closing duplicate folded away"* and is corrected — the third way it moves is **adding** the closing segment, and that is the common case rather than a corner one. Amends **D117**, which closed the *read* side with a fold and left the write side emitting the segment, and **D118**, whose remedy for *"a click on a point was leaving an empty undo step"* therefore held only for paths already in `pen_path`'s output shape. `tools::rewrite_no_op_tests`, three, with a fixture assertion that the round trip really does move and a control that a real radius edit still commits. - **D587** — **The I-beam is measured from the figure's middle, like the arc.** `cursor::text_on_path` builds its arc from `ccx = f64::from(w) / 2.0`, a **length**, and built the I-beam's stem and serif from `cx = w / 2`, an **index**. Closes `[S17-L1-04]`. Both marks test `(x + 0.5 − ccx).abs()`; the cost is one extra serif column on an even-width buffer, which is what symmetry means there. ⚠️ **The test named for the symmetry ran at `text_on_path(1.0)` alone** — the one scale where the parity happens to be right — while the two badge tests four hundred lines up both loop `SCALES`. Flip, the beam from `cx` again → *"at 1.5x, row 0 is lopsided at column 5"*, the site the finding predicted. Neither document changed: the *"sizes are in points and scaled"* rule lives in `cursor.rs`'s own doc comments and §9.2 rules on nothing about centring)*

So at depth 20, ordinary for imported SVG, the incremental path was **4.8×** the full reconstruction, and at depth 200 **47×**. Per commit: every arrow-key nudge (~30/s held), every undo, every redo, every released scrub. `rebuild` needs no sort at all — `resolve_subtree` is a recursion, so parents precede children structurally. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. Closes `[S4.1-L4-03]`. 🚨 **`sort_by_cached_key` is the obvious one-word fix and it is not enough**: three versions on a 200-deep chain in debug, three runs each, as a ratio against `rebuild` — `sort_by_key` over a depth walk **42.9×**, `sort_by_cached_key` over a depth walk **3.2×**, depth recorded on the way down **1.2×**. The middle row is the one worth carrying, since it takes 93% of the cost out and still leaves the incremental path three times the price of the thing it exists to avoid, the walk still running once per node. So `collect_subtree` records each node's depth as it descends (a child's is its parent's plus one, free there), `affected` is an `FxHashMap<NodeId, usize>`, and the sort is `sort_by_cached_key` over a lookup. ⚠️ **The review's own attribution had to be corrected before it was believed**: its first replica of this line read *10% of update* and would have sent the finding to Rejected, because it sorted ids in *creation* order, which is already sorted by depth, so the adaptive sort called the key O(n) times instead of O(n log n). Composes with **D590** without either helping the other — the sort still runs over the *expanded* set, and D590 changed only what `op_set_transform` puts in the dirty set. §5.9 amended)*
- **D595** — **One picture on many shapes is written once.** Every def was keyed per node **per slot** — `image_id(id, slot)` — and `Defs::add` dedupes on that string, so nothing was keyed on `ImageRef`'s `ImageId` and two shapes showing one photograph were two defs, each carrying a full base64 copy. **Measured in release, one embedded 200 KB image shared by N rectangles**: 1 shape → 0.27 MB document, 0.27 MB SVG (1.0×); 2 → 0.27 / 0.53 (2.0×); 10 → 0.28 / 2.67 (9.6×); **30 → 0.30 / 8.01 (26.6×)**. The document side is the control and it is flat, because `ImageId` is a content hash and the table holds the blob once — **the export threw that away exactly**. A moodboard, a photo grid and a repeated logo are ordinary documents, and *Export SVG* is not an exotic path. `ImageEntry::href` also returns a fresh `String` of 4/3 × the blob per call and `escape_xml` copies it again, so the transient cost per shape was ~2.7× the blob on top of the ~1.33× that landed in the file. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix. One `<image id="pix-<hash>">` per distinct `ImageId` in `<defs>`, and each `<pattern>` holding a `<use href="#pix-…">`. **The per-node `<pattern>` is not the duplication and stays** — its `patternTransform` carries that node's own `ImageRef::framing`, which genuinely differs per node. Measured on an otherwise-valid save: `8589934592` (2³³) truncated to **0**, passed the guard, ran the whole v0→v4 chain and **opened**, reported as v4; `4294967300` truncated to `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` and returned early, the failure then arriving from the DTO as a serde error about a `u32`; `u64::MAX` was refused as *"unsupported schema version: 4294967295"*, a version the file does not claim. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep. Closes `[S1.1-L1-05]`. Both comparisons are against `u64::from(CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION)` now and the `match` runs on the same value the guard read. 🚨 **`IoError::UnsupportedVersion` carries a `u64` where it carried a `u32`, and that is the load-bearing half**: with the payload narrow, casting at the read was free everywhere; with it wide, re-introducing the cast **does not compile** — rustc rejects the `match`'s `other` arm — so widening the error is the only mechanical objection anywhere to half of the old shape. `tests/io.rs · load_rejects_a_schema_version_wider_than_u32_without_truncating_it` asserts the **number inside** the error rather than the variant, `UnsupportedVersion(_)` alone being satisfied by a widened comparison over a re-narrowed payload. ⚠️ **The predicted failure site was wrong**: it is the `Ok` arm and not the `assert_eq!`, because the 2³³ header does not merely get reported under the wrong number, it opens the file. `load_rejects_future_version` (9999) is deliberately left alone — 9999 fits a `u32`, so it was green before and says nothing about this. §5.11 gains a bullet; nothing struck from `roadmap.md`)*

Closes `[S2.2-L1-06]`. ⚠️ **The arithmetic downstream was already safe and that was never the question** — `geometry::pivot_for` falls back below `MIN_EXTENT` and `canvas::origin_pivot` has `ORIGIN_MIN_EXTENT`, so nothing divides by a zero extent; what neither guards is a coordinate that was never finite, which arrives from a singular world transform through `canvas::pivot_at`'s `.inverse()` and from any hand-authored or MCP write. `Pivot::is_finite` is the predicate and it lives **on the enum**, because `Normalized` holds a `Vec2` and `Local` a `Point` and a guard written against one compiles happily while missing the other. The sharpest of three flips blinds only `Pivot::is_finite`'s `Local` arm and leaves the `Normalized` assertion **green**. §2's invariant 8 and §5.3's pivot bullet amended; nothing struck from `roadmap.md`)*
- **D640** — **A `NaN` corner radius was the *largest* radius, not none.** `geometry::round_corners`' fast path was `radii.iter().all(|r| *r <= 0.0)` and `round_run`'s per-corner guard `if radius <= 0.0 { continue }`; every comparison against `NaN` is false, so both let it through, and what it reached is `fillet`'s `.min(la * 0.5).min(lb * 0.5)` — where `f64::min` returns the **non-`NaN`** operand, i.e. the largest trim the clamp allows. - **D641** — **An infinite escape became *no* escape, and the fix is one level out.** `effect::escaped` splits its insets back into an offset and a radius — `off = (x1 − x0) * 0.5` — so `x0 = x1 = inf` gives `inf − inf`, which is `NaN`, and `NaN.min(0.0)` resolves to the **non-`NaN`** operand. Since `escaped`'s signature has no room for absence, the honest place for the check is the operation — which is where invariant 8 puts it anyway. ⚠️ **The contrast is the entry's other half**: `reach(f64::NAN)` is `0.0` by the same `max`-against-zero convention, so a `NaN` radius was always a benign no-op while an infinite one was a bounds *lie* — two non-finite inputs, two silent answers, from one idiom. ⚠️ **The preview path does not come through an operation and is bounded by the panel's ranges** — a scrubbed blur reaches the renderer through `RenderOverrides` — and *"`MAX_BLUR` is what covers it"* is **half of it**: `stack_escape` reads a shadow's offset and spread too, and those are bounded by `MAX_OFFSET` (10,000), while `Filters` escape nothing at all. `svg_in::deviation_of` is the third bound, on the import side. - **D643** — **`normalize`'s overlap arm depended on the file's array order and ate bytes outside the overlap.** `typography::Spans::normalize` merged with a three-way `Join` under a comment claiming *"equal values join, unequal ones let the **later** span keep the shared bytes (it is the one a caller set most recently)"*. Both halves were false: the list has just been sorted by `(kind, start)`, so *later* meant "starts further right" and had nothing to do with recency, and for two spans sharing a start `sort_by_key` is stable, so the winner was whatever order the file's array happened to be in. *(Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep. Closes `[S6.1-L1-06]`. Measured on a stock `TextStyle`: `[{0..10, W700}, {0..5, W300}]` → `[{0..5, W300}]` and `[{0..5, W300}, {0..10, W700}]` → `[{0..10, W700}]` — **two documents from one set**, and in the first, bytes 5..10 lost their 700 to the node default because `Join::Truncate` set `prev.end = span.start` and then popped `prev`, discarding its **whole** range including the part beyond `span.end`. The straddling control behaved exactly as documented, which is what localised the defect to *containment*. **Painting, not truncating**: spans of one kind are laid down in sorted order, each byte takes the value of the last one covering it, and a span painted over keeps whatever lies outside the shared bytes on both sides. ⚠️ **`std::cmp::Reverse(end)` joins the sort key and is the only reason two spans sharing a start have a defined winner** — widest first, so the narrower paints over it — and it is what makes the answer order-independent. The equal-value merge is a pass of its own now, because painting can split a run around one of equal value. ⚠️ **The `(kind, start)` save order is unaffected** (§5.11, invariant 9): after `normalize` runs one kind's spans do not overlap, so no two share a start and the third key never breaks a tie in the output. ⚠️ **Two spans with an *identical* range and different values are still decided by array order**, nothing here comparing values — a case with no defensible answer that this crate cannot produce. 🚨 **No §15 entry and no architecture passage had ever ruled on this**, §5.4 stating only the postcondition, so this is the first record of the rule. Reachability is IO only and that is the honest bound: `set` splits the old span around the new range, `edited`'s maps are monotonic, `clamped`/`restated`/`scaled` preserve ranges — so the producer is a hand-edited or foreign file, which `io/schema.rs` chooses to normalize on the stated grounds that clamping *"loses nothing a designer would notice"*. Here it lost styling, and which styling depended on array order. `an_overlap_resolves_the_same_way_whichever_order_the_file_lists_it_in`, built with `from_parts` rather than `set` on purpose; two flips, **each red at exactly one assertion with the other green**. §5.4's span bullet gains the rule; nothing struck from `roadmap.md`)*

Closes `[S9.2-L1-01]`, an open **High**. **The maintainer's decision is full resolution until it stops fitting, then shrink.** `ImageStore::prepare` computes one integer factor from the store's own decoded population rather than from what a frame happens to draw, **deliberately**: a factor derived from visibility would change as the canvas is panned, so a photograph would visibly resharpen when its neighbour scrolled off. `images::atlas_downscale` searches upward from 1, so a page with two photographs is handed both at their own size exactly as before. **One factor for all of them rather than one each**, because per-picture factors make the page's photographs disagree about sharpness — which reads as one of them being wrong rather than as a budget — and make the answer depend on placement order. 🚨 **The fit test is a *shelf* packing where vello uses a guillotine allocator (`guillotiere`), and the direction of that difference is the licence to have written it at all.** Shelf packing is strictly the worse of the two, so **"the shelf fits" implies "the guillotine fits"** — the one-way guarantee this needs. The converse does not hold, so it refuses some sets vello would have taken and the cost is a photograph shrunk when it need not have been; the alternative was depending on `guillotiere` directly and hoping our copy matched vello's, trading a conservative answer for a version-skew bug that draws nothing. 🚨 **The two backends now deliberately differ, and this is the first place they do.** `color::Resolution { Source, Atlas }`: the GPU painter asks for `Atlas` (`ImageStore::atlas_pixels`), the CPU painter for `Source`. `color.rs`'s whole purpose is that they cannot disagree — one conversion, one monotonic-stops repair, one framing composition — so **a canvas that softens a photograph and an export that does not are both correct**, and a reader finding them different should reach for this rather than for a bug. ⚠️ **The reduction is applied to whatever buffer `pixels` returns, not to the decode**, so a picture under a moving slider — already a preview — is reduced once more: one step softer than it needs to be, for the duration of a scrub, on a page already over budget. Accepted rather than hidden. ⚠️ **The atlas cache is keyed on the *blob's* id and not the picture's**, which is what makes it correct for an adjusted picture: the buffer may be the decode, a preview, or a derived copy carrying somebody's exposure slider, three sets of pixels under one `ImageId` — and it is the key vello itself uses for residency. ⚠️ **A residual**: `MAX_ATLAS_DOWNSCALE` is 64 and past it `atlas_downscale` gives up, so the silent drop returns. And flipping `atlas_downscale` to return 1 fails on the *factor* assertion four lines before the pixels, so it says nothing about the drawing: the flip that reaches the picture is `atlas_pixels` returning `pixels` unchanged, which comes back **`left: 1250, right: 1875`**, the finding's own measurement to the pixel. **A test with a cheap assertion in front of an expensive one is only as good as the flip that gets past it.** §5.5a gains the atlas-budget bullet, §6.2 the one deliberate disagreement, and §6.3's *"the pixels come from `ImageStore::pixels`"* sentence is corrected; nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose *Now · Images* list is closed but for linked sources)*

- **D819** — **Linked images are a decided non-goal for v1, and `is_linked` stays with no production caller.** The three Asset entries — *Embed*/*Link*, *Relink…* and the document-wide *Embed all* — all wait on the same missing thing: a gesture that **authors** a linked source. `ImageSource::Linked` is constructed in exactly one place, `io/schema.rs`'s deserializer, and every app path onto a picture funnels through `app::load_image_bytes`, which builds `Embedded` unconditionally — **so a foreign `.ondin` can carry a link and the app will open it, and nothing can make one.** §15 **D191** is the out-of-v1 image list this joins, and §15 **D305** already withdrew *Export original…* the same way. 🚨 **`is_linked` and the preserved reasoning stay**, which is the half a future editor would tidy: the subject exists in the model, a foreign document can put one in front of the app, and `tools::original_refusal`'s three-state answer is kept as comments where that function stood — fine, linked, or an id the table does not hold. **Rebuild from those rather than re-deriving**, and *do not infer linked from absent bytes*, which is the bug §15 **D280** is about and which two hand-rolled `bytes().is_some()` doors had already committed once. *(Ruled by the maintainer 2026-09-19; **Resolved — a decided non-goal.** Record-only, no production line changed; **the citation is planted by hand** on `ondin_core::image`'s `is_linked`, which is where the question *why does nothing call this* is met — and `dead_code` cannot ask it there, core being a library where a `pub` item is API. **The three rows move into `roadmap.md` §0** and the *Now · Images* open bullet is struck, leaving that section as the record of the v1 image build with nothing open)*
- **D820** — **A dashboard cover is rendered on a thread of its own, and the budget is deleted with what it bounded.** `Covers::get` → `render` → `io::load` → `png::png` → `ImageStore::prepare` ran the whole document→pixels path **inside the egui pass**, where a picture's decode alone was measured at **433 ms** for an 8000² image (§15 **D449**). `roadmap.md` said which thread it goes on was undecided. 🚨 **It is a second worker of its own and not a job on `library::writer::Writer`'s queue**, and the reason is that module's own contract — *"one background writer of anything, in **FIFO** order"* — with the FIFO load-bearing twice: a `Forget` must not be overtaken by the `Snapshot` it cancels, and a save must not be overtaken by anything. A cover render is hundreds of milliseconds nothing is waiting on, so putting one in front of an autosave makes the feature that protects work wait behind the feature that decorates a card. ⚠️ **Nothing the renderer does is a record**: it may write a PNG into the cover cache, which `crate::atomic` deliberately **exempts** as derived data, so this is not a second writer of anything that module protects. 🚨 **`FRAME_BUDGET` is deleted rather than retuned, and that is a removal and not a regression**: the 8 ms never bounded the felt cost, because the **progress guarantee** under it rendered one document per pass *whatever the budget said* — so a library of slow documents cost one stall per pass rather than none. Both were consequences of rendering **inside** the pass, and neither has anything to bound now. `thumbs::ImageThumbs` keeps its 2 ms and is no longer the same shape: its decode really does happen in the frame. *(Ruled by the maintainer, built and tested 2026-09-19; **Resolved.** `Covers` gains `queued` — so a card drawn every frame enqueues **once** rather than sixty times a second, which is a queue that outruns its drain and a thread that never reaches the second document — plus `Renderer`, spawned lazily on the first miss for `Writer::spawn`'s reason and **joined** on drop rather than detached, and a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) settle`. ⚠️ **`settle` is `cfg(test)` and not `pub`, which is §15 D672's answer rather than D699's**: nothing in production waits for a cover, and `ondin-app` has no lib target, so `dead_code` does analyse a `pub` item there and it warned. **Test** `library::cover::tests::covers_are_rendered_off_the_pass_and_all_of_them_arrive`, **replacing** `one_cover_a_pass_arrives_however_spent_the_budget_is` — the rule that one pinned is **gone rather than changed**, which is why the test goes with it; `a_document_with_no_cover_is_not_retried_every_pass` survives with a new tell, the budget having been how it measured a re-render and the queue being it now. 🚨 **The thread introduced a flake in *another module's* test, and finding it is the most useful thing in this entry.** `panels::dashboard::tests::a_document_this_build_cannot_open_wears_the_mark_and_a_healthy_one_does_not` asserts the red `UNREADABLE` chip, which `mark_of` reads through `Covers::unreadable` — and a cover only learns a document is unloadable when it **renders** it. The test pumped one extra pass and asserted on the next, and **its own doc said those two passes were *"the cover cache's laziness rather than a flake"***. ⚠️ **That sentence was accurate when it was written and this change made it exactly wrong**: the laziness is still there and the *timing* it promised is gone, because "the next pass" was a fact while the render was inline and is a **race** once it is on a thread. It is struck in place in the test's doc rather than deleted, the stale half being the point. **The fix is one line** — `app.covers.settle(&ctx)` before the assertion, which is what that method exists for — and 25 paired runs afterwards failed none. 🚨 **What found it was running the filter twenty times.** The whole suite was green throughout, both full `--workspace` runs were green in debug *and* release, and a verification run of the same two filters **three times each** was green: **2 of 20** paired runs failed, and only under a filtered run, which packs the related tests onto every core at once. *Six clean runs is not evidence.* That is `CLAUDE.md`'s thirteenth gate hole and §15 **D796**'s lesson arriving from a second direction — there a shared OS resource, here a shared worker — and neither is visible to any gate. ⚠️ **It is also what earns `settle` its `pub(crate)`**: the argument for the method was that the app stays asynchronous and a probe asks for an answer, and this is a *second* module's test needing it, which is the case that says it must not be private to `cover.rs`. 🚨 **The doc gate caught two dangling links this change created** — `[`FRAME_BUDGET`]` after the constant was deleted, and `[`Covers::settle`]` after that method became `cfg(test)`, the second being D319's mechanism from the direction where a production doc may not name a test-only item. *That gate is the one that reads doc comments, and this is it working.* §5.11a's cover-cache paragraph and §9.5's `Covers::unreadable` sentence are amended, and §5.3a's `MAX_SHADOW_BLOCK` paragraph, whose *"a hang at launch"* is now a stuck cover thread and a library that renders nothing past the first bad file. **The bullet is struck from `roadmap.md`** with the clause in the table row that named it)*

A new rung in `OndinApp::escape` answers it. 🚨 **Below `cancel_gesture` and not above it, which is the whole of the placement**: a numeric field's cancel has to go on reaching that function, because it is what sets `gesture_cancelled` and stops the release committing after all (D317). It reads a new field, `OndinApp::chrome_focus`, written at the **end** of each frame after the `Tab` surrender. ⚠️ **Recorded rather than asked, because egui has no global question for it**: `Memory::had_focus_last_frame` takes an `Id` and the ladder has none. ⚠️ **"Anything focused", not "a text field"** — `egui_wants_keyboard_input`'s own definition (§15 **D123**), deliberately not narrowed. *(Found and fixed 2026-09-19; **Keep.** This closes nothing on `roadmap.md`: it is a defect D808's probe turned up and the maintainer ruled on in the same round. - **D823** — **A layer copied in one `ondin` window pastes as a layer in another, and the wire form is the document schema.** §15 **D17** closed by prescribing the fix — *"give core a serializable subtree; that would also buy paste between two Ondin windows"* — and until now a copy put only the layer **names** on the OS clipboard, so a second window's `Ctrl+V` saw text and pasted the names as a text layer. `ondin_core::io::clip` is that subtree: the names, then `FENCE`, then JSON, found with `rsplit_once` so a layer *named* like the fence cannot truncate the heading. **Not a second format** — `NodeDto::from_node`/`into_node` and `ImageDto` were lifted out of `DocumentDto` so the clipboard reaches the same projection a file does, which is what keeps D663's out-bound `clip` normalization and every rule like it in one place. 🚨 **The version is compared for equality, not migrated**, the one deliberate divergence from `io::load`. 🚨 **`read` answers `Option<Result<…>>` and the third state is the point**: ours-and-unreadable must be *said*, or the payload falls through to `paste_text_as_layer` and the user gets a text layer holding megabytes of their own JSON. *(Built and tested 2026-09-22; **Resolved.** All four paste doors call `OndinApp::take_clipboard` where they called `owns_the_clipboard`, and `adopt_clip_text` is its decision with the OS read lifted off it, **D805**'s split for **D798**'s reason. 🚨 **`roadmap.md`'s cost estimate was wrong twice, both times in the cheap direction**: the id minting *did not exist as work* — `build::insert_subtrees` already remaps through `document::remap_subtree` — and the serialization it said must **not** be `NodeDto` **is** `NodeDto`. - **D824** — **The Escape context-menu rule gets its wider fixture, and it had to be a *second* test.** §15 **D795** closed on one clause of `context-menus.md` §10 it could not write: that file's Escape bullet asks for the menu opened with a layer selected **inside an entered group and the node tool active**, and for `entered_group` and the tool to be untouched as well as the selection. 🚨 **§10 asked for the existing test to be widened and that would have been wrong.** `OndinApp::escape` pays out **one** rung per press and reaches `entered_group` *before* the tool and before the selection clear that is its final `else` — so under the narrow fixture the fall-through's extra rung is the **selection**, which is why that test bites, and under the wide one it is `entered_group`, leaving the selection and the tool untouched **under the very flip the test exists for**. - **D826** — **Rejoining a multi-line paragraph on SVG import is a decided non-goal for v1.** A multi-line text layer of ours exports as one `<text>` per line and comes back as one layer per line, because nothing in the markup says they were one node — and the rejoin would have to **invent the line height** that decides where every line after the first sits. 🚨 **The refusal is about what the only available signal identifies**: same `x`, a constant `y` step and a matching resolved style is *also* exactly what a stack of separate labels in a foreign file looks like, so the heuristic welds unrelated layers together and the user has no way to say which reading was meant. ⚠️ **And the case it would have been worth most for is answered elsewhere** — a copy crossing between two `ondin` windows carries real nodes now, paragraph and all (§15 **D823**) — so what is left here is the foreign file, which never had the structure to lose. *(Ruled by the maintainer 2026-09-22; **Resolved — a decided non-goal**, no production line changed. **Record-only, so the citation is planted by hand** on `svg_in`'s `text_node`, in the run that already argued the loss was real — that paragraph is now the end of the argument rather than the start of one. `a_positioned_tspan_starts_a_new_layer_and_a_bare_one_does_not` already pins what *is* read, so nothing about the element is left open. **It moves into `roadmap.md` §0** and is struck from *Now · SVG import*, where it was the last item — §15 **D813** having left that section with this alone)*
