which `CLAUDE.md` records; this time the code is at `HEAD` and the entry says which occasion is
which, so the history does not read as a second slip. §9.5's copy of the same list and the same
sentence amended. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`. Closes `[S16.3-L2-06]`.)*

**D769 — `skip_ink`'s cost sentence was measured on the wrong fixture. *Ruling by the maintainer;
recorded 2026-09-15; Keep — the code is unchanged and the sentence is gone.***

`[S5.2-L4-06]`, on the maintainer's ruling: **leave the code, delete the false sentence.**
`core::text::skip_ink`'s doc closed with *"what is left is under a third of the layout it rides on"*,
measured on the 816-glyph / 24-band table directly above it and **quoted as a property of the
function**. At **22,528 glyphs over 366 bands** it is **6.6 ms of a 12.7 ms layout — 52%**.

**The mechanism is the per-*run* reject, which tests against `reach` — the *union* of every band's
extent.** On a multi-line underlined paragraph that union spans the whole node, so the reject rejects
nothing and `raw_crossings` walks the full glyph list once per band. The four-comparison per-glyph box
test makes each step cheap; it does not remove the product. **The doc now carries the complexity class
and no number**, because the next fixture will be bigger again and a corrected figure would be the
same mistake one size up.

🚨 **And it is not paid twice per keystroke, which both the finding and `review/index.md` say.** That
cites `[A4-L4-01]`, **fixed by D592** — a keystroke shapes the edited node once, `canvas.rs` says so
at the site, and `TextEdit::reshape` calls `shape()` rather than `extract`. The cost is 6.6 ms, not
13.2. **A stale multiplier in a cost argument is a severity error**, which is `[S4.1-L4-08]`'s shape
from the other direction.

**Not fixed, and the reason is the guard rather than the fix.** Bucketing `placed` by line is about
twenty lines. The existing test asserts *properties* — `!gaps.is_empty()`, `total < width * 0.6` —
and would stay green through a float-level drift, so the honest guard for that change is a
byte-identical snapshot of `gaps` before and after. *Revisit when somebody has a document that
reaches it*: the trigger is roughly 4,500 words underlined end to end in a **single** node.

*(No production line changed. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`. Closes `[S5.2-L4-06]`.)*

**D770 — Escape discards a staged Settings form, and that is decided. *Ruling by the maintainer;
recorded 2026-09-15; Keep.***

`[S18.3-L1-07]`, on the maintainer's *"leave the behaviour"*. The rule is written into `settings.rs`'s
module doc rather than left to be rediscovered by the next reader of that card.

⚠️ **Measured, and it corrects the finding's framing.** The card closes **identically with and without
field focus**: `egui::ModalResponse::should_close` gates only on `is_top_modal` and `!any_popup_open`,
egui's `TextEdit` handles **no** Escape at all, and the app's own modal arm is empty — it suppresses
`input::resolve` and nothing else. So *"while a field owns the keyboard"* describes the situation and
is **not a condition on the behaviour**. What the focused case adds is that `DragValue` *reads* Escape
one layer down, to abandon a typed number, so the user's expectation is narrower than what actually
happens.

**Three grounds for keeping it.** What is lost is five staged preference values, not artwork. The
module doc already said Escape discards, so the behaviour was documented rather than accidental. And
the obvious guard is a bad trade: `should_close()` is **one expression covering Escape, the ✕ and the
backdrop click**, so gating it also breaks backdrop-dismiss while a field has focus — and
`ctx.egui_wants_keyboard_input()` is true whenever *anything* has focus, including a button reached by
Tab.

⚠️ **Confirm-on-dirty is the principled alternative and it is blocked, which is the useful part of
this entry.** `draft != saved` is already computed every frame for the footer, so the comparison costs
nothing. But `[S18.3-L1-02]` records `nudge_field`'s clamp moving the draft on the card's **first
frame**, so the confirmation would fire on a card nobody edited — the most annoying possible failure
of a confirmation. *Fix that first; this question is not worth re-opening until a clean card reads
clean.*

*(No production line changed. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose Escape row is about the ladder
and the type popovers rather than about this card. Closes `[S18.3-L1-07]`.)*

**D771 — The release suite is a session-close step, and its cost was misstated in three places.
*Ruling by the maintainer; recorded 2026-09-15; Resolved — D597's open half is closed.***

`cargo test --workspace --release` is a written step in `CLAUDE.md`'s **Build / test** section now,
run once at the close of a session, **not** a per-edit gate.

🚨 ***"It roughly doubles the test time"* was false, and it appeared in three places** — D597's body,
D597's index row and `CLAUDE.md` — which is how a cost figure comes to decide a question nobody
re-measured. Measured 2026-09-15, warm, on this machine: the release **run** is **6 s** against the
debug run's **20 s**, three times *faster*, partly because
`[profile.dev.package.ondin-render] opt-level = 3` already optimises the hot crate in debug.

**The cost is the build, not the run**: 26 s of fingerprinting on a warm no-op, **96 s cold** over 280
crates, and **2.4 GB** of a second profile's artifacts — against the
`[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = false` that exists because `target/debug` once reached 46 GB.
🚨 **The phrase landed near the right *total* for entirely the wrong reason, and the reason is what
the decision turns on**: the number a maintainer actually feels is the **marginal release recompile**
after each edit, which *"doubles the test time"* does not describe at all. Had it been true as
written, a gate would have been the right answer.

⚠️ **`-p ondin-app --release` costs 1 s and covers all three known instances, and was rejected.**
Adopting `-p` as a gate spelling buys back the feature-unification hazard `CLAUDE.md` records twice —
`peniko::Gradient` at 168 bytes under one spelling and 160 under the other — and **D600** records that
same spelling deciding whether a *test can fail*, its BMP decoder arriving only under `--workspace`.
A cheap gate that compiles different code is not the cheap version of this gate.

⚠️ **The class it catches is a test whose *meaning* changes with the profile**, and every instance
that has bitten was a **dependency** reading `debug_assertions` on our behalf rather than us reading
it — egui defaulting `warn_on_id_clash` to `cfg!(debug_assertions)` twice over. `check --release` is
scoped `-p ondin-app`, so it does not compile the other four crates' test targets under the release
cfg at all, and no other gate runs anything under it.

*(D597 amended in body and index: its cost figure corrected, and its *"one further instance is open …
fix with the same one line"* **closed** — `the_dashboard_draws_without_egui_complaining` carries the
fix. `CLAUDE.md`'s gate block was edited by the maintainer, an agent's message not being authorization
to change the project's instructions. ⚠️ **The step is a habit and not a gate, so nothing keeps it**;
sessions 19 and 23 had already run it by hand, and writing it into the closing checklist is what stops
that depending on somebody remembering. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, which carries no row on the
gate list.)*

**D772 — The dashboard's drop door had D759's hole too. *Fixed 2026-09-15; Keep — and no test, which
is recorded rather than glossed.***

⚠️ **Out of numeric sequence on purpose.** This is the tail of **D759**, found by re-reading that
entry's own call graph while writing it up, and it belongs with that story; D767–D771 had already
been reserved for other work by the time it landed. The index is still in strict numeric order, and
the gap this sentence was written against — D767 to D771 — is **filled**: those five were the batch
that followed. ⚠️ **This sentence read *"the block closes at D772 with D773–D775 reserved"* and was
overtaken the same day** — D773 was spent on a defect D767 turned out to have introduced. It was then
rewritten to say *"the block closes at D773 with D774 and D775 reserved and unspent"* and **overtaken
again inside the same session**, those two going to D774 and D775. The block closes at **D775**.
*A claim about which number is free is stale the moment the next one is typed into a comment*, and
this paragraph has now been the demonstration of its own sentence twice.

In no finding. `OndinApp::take_dropped_documents` runs **first** in `dashboard_ui`, above every card
that screen draws, with no modal guard at all — and `raw.dropped_files` is filled from winit before
any widget runs, so an `egui::Modal` backdrop does not stop a drop. A `.ondin` dragged onto the
library while *Move to project*, a delete confirmation, *New project*, *Edit project*, the library
settings, a rename or the recovery card was up **was filed anyway**, and then announced itself into a
status line behind the backdrop, where the user cannot read it.

🚨 **The guard is `library_keys_are_free`, and choosing it is the whole decision.** That predicate is
this screen's own enumeration of *"a card is up"* — written for the keyboard by §15 D383 and lifted
into one place by D542, precisely because the screen had two readers of the context and only one of
them had the list. The pointer asking a **second** list would be the shape D759 had just removed from
the editor: *a rule with one statement and several implementations*, which is the thing this codebase
keeps finding broken. So the library has one list with two askers now, exactly as the editor has one
predicate with two.

⚠️ **Not `modal_is_up`, which is the editor's, and the check was made rather than assumed.**
`settings_ui` is drawn below `dashboard_ui`'s own `return` and never runs on this screen, and

🚨 **No test, and that is a gap rather than an omission worth hiding.** D759's equivalent was

which is a different and much larger fixture than a revision counter. The guard is one conjunction in
front of one call and was read against the call graph; it is not measured on the machine.

⚠️ **D759's closing ⚠️ predicted this would *"want a third list or a second predicate"*, and both
halves were wrong.** The second predicate already existed and had been read by exactly one caller
since D542. That is the ordinary way an un-enumerated remainder closes — **by asking the list the
screen already keeps** — and it is worth knowing before the next one is put to the maintainer as a
decision.

well as the editor's. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, which carries no row on drop routing.)*

**D773 — A faded gradient's chips show it; the stop bar stays raw. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-15;
Resolved for the gradient arm — and the image arm, put to the maintainer on the strength of the
paragraph below, is closed by §15 D784 the same day.***

**A live defect D767 introduced, and the mechanism is worth more than the fix.** `picker::ramp`
returned `paint::stops_of(brush)` — the stop list as stored — and `GradientBrush::opacity` was folded
in nowhere on that path. It *is* multiplied in at `color::brush_to_backend` for both backends and
written as `fill-opacity` by `svg::paint_attr`, so **the chrome was the third multiplication nobody
added**: a gradient fill dropped to 30% drew the inspector's paint-row chip, the picker's 34×34
preview and the Type panel's text swatch at **full** alpha, over a canvas drawing it faint.

🚨 **This is D564's sentence word for word — *one document drawn two ways in one frame* — and it had
been right for free until D767.** While the opacity *was* the stops, `stops_of` was what the paint
looked like, so every chip in the app was correct without anybody arranging it. **A derived value
that becomes a stored one turns every reader of the old derivation into a bug**, silently: the types
do not change, every caller still compiles, and the picture is wrong. **The entire suite stayed
green.** Nothing in this project can see that class — not the compiler, not clippy, not the doc gate,
not the tests — which is the generalisable half, and it is the reason this entry is longer than the
change it records.

**The fix is caller-side and the defaulting is the decision.** `ramp` folds the opacity in and a new
`stop_colours` is the named exception. Three of the four callers are **chips** — `inspector`'s paint
row, `picker`'s preview, `typography::text_ramp` — and have to look like the canvas. The fourth is
the **stop bar**, which is the editing surface for those very stops and sits directly under the
opacity slider: a bar that faded as the slider moved would be dimming the handles being dragged.
**The common case is the default so that a chip written next year is right by doing nothing**, and
the exception opts out by name.

⚠️ **The image arm has had the identical gap since D185 and is deliberately not fixed here.**
`ImageSampler::alpha` is folded into neither function, so a half-faded photograph has always had an
opaque thumbnail. It is real, it is older and wider than this, and it is not this change's — **which
is why it is written down rather than left implicit: fixing the gradient alone is exactly what makes
the image arm read as a decision somebody took.** ***Fix — but not asked for.*** The maintainer has
never been put the question, and D767's own paragraph asked for both arms together; this entry
declines that only because the gradient is the arm D767 broke, where the image arm has been this way
since the image brush had an alpha at all.
🚨 **Amended: it was put, and it is closed — §15 D784, the same day.** The paragraph above is kept
exactly as written because **it is the reason the arm got fixed**: a defect recorded as *deliberately
not taken* is one somebody can rule on, where a defect left implicit is one nobody knows is there.
*Writing down the half you are not doing is what got it done.* ⚠️ **And it was two surfaces, not the
one this entry names**: beside the chips above, `panels::layers` draws the same picture on every image
layer's row through a `picture_of` that returned `&ImageRef` and dropped the sampler on the floor —
**the entry that decided the rule was written against the surface its author was looking at**, which
is this project's most-recorded shape arriving inside a paragraph about a missed door.

**Test** `panels::picker::grid_orphan_tests::a_faded_gradient_dims_its_chip_and_not_its_stop_bar`.
⚠️ **It asserts both halves because the defaulting is the decision** — an assertion that only checked
the chip is satisfied by folding the opacity into `stop_colours` too, which is the version that dims
the handles, so a one-sided test would have been green for the wrong fix. Flip: restoring `ramp`'s
pre-D773 body fails at the chip assertion, predicted correctly. ⚠️ **The flip was written up as
*"`255` against `76`"* and that is a failure message the run does not print** — the assertion is an
`assert!` on `faded < opaque`, so it names what the chip *did* read and never the value it should
have, and the `76` is a post-fix number that appears nowhere in the failure. Corrected in place.
**A flip's colour and site were right and its *reported output* was invented**, which is a thinner
version of this file's standing warning about a verdict that outlives its argument, and reads
exactly like a measurement because the shape of an `assert_eq!` message is so familiar.

🚨 **The number was spent in code comments before this entry existed, and that is the D727/D728 hole
rather than a tidiness complaint.** The defect was found by `arch-scribe` checking D767's brief
against §5.5a — *after* this session's second block had been reserved and its batch-3 numbers
allocated — so the fix was written, committed and cited while `D773` resolved to nothing anywhere in
`docs/`, with every gate green throughout. It was caught by the citation census at the batch
boundary. **`CLAUDE.md` records that hole as what a batch that *dies* leaves behind; this is the same
hole left by a batch that *succeeded*** — the work simply arrived after the brief that would have
carried it. A number is owed from the moment it is typed into a comment, not from the moment a batch
fails.

**D784 — An image brush's alpha reaches its chips, and D773's one surface was two. *Fixed and tested
2026-09-15; Resolved — D773's image arm is closed.***

D773 closes by recording the picture arm as a real defect it was deliberately **not** taking: *"`Fix` —
but never put to the maintainer"*, written down *"so that fixing the gradient alone does not make the
image arm read as a decision somebody took"*. It was put, and taken. **Writing down the half you are
not doing is what got it done**, which is the argument for that paragraph rather than for the silence.

`peniko::ImageSampler::alpha` is folded in at `color::brush_to_backend` for both backends and written
by the SVG writer, and by **nothing in the chrome** — so a fill dropped to 30% drew a fully opaque
chip beside a canvas drawing it faint. That is §15 **D564**'s *one document drawn two ways in one
frame*, and unlike the gradient arm it was never right for free: it has been this way since §15
**D185**, i.e. since an image brush had an alpha at all. The gradient half had the excuse that
`stops_of` *was* what the paint looked like until D767 moved the opacity off the stops; this half had
none.

🚨 **D773 named one surface and there are two.** Besides the inspector's paint-row chip
(`ui::Swatch::Picture`), `panels::layers` draws the same picture on every image layer's row, through
its own `picture_of` — **which returned `&ImageRef`**, taking the picture out of the brush and
dropping the sampler on the floor. *A helper that returns half of a brush is how the other half gets
forgotten by every caller at once*, and the way the omission happened is the ordinary one: the entry
that decided the rule was written against the surface its author was looking at. `picture_of` answers
with the whole `ImageBrush` now.

**The row's two multipliers compose rather than one winning**, which is `layers::thumb_tint`'s whole
subject. The row's dimming says *this layer is out of play*; the brush's alpha says *this paint is
faint*. They are facts about different things, so a hidden layer holding a 30% picture is fainter than
either alone — and a rule that picked a winner would make one of the two invisible exactly when the
other was also true. ⚠️ **It is a named function so that it can be asserted at all**: the drawn
thumbnail needs a decoded picture in the store *and* a texture the frame budget did not defer, which
is two pieces of machinery between a test and the decision. The decision is the expression; the rest
is the thumbnail cache, which has its own tests.

**One clamp and two entry points**, because the two chips reach the brush by different roads: the
inspector has a `&Brush` and the layers row an `&ImageBrush` out of its own `picture_of`.
`panels::paint::image_brush_alpha` is the rule and `image_alpha` is the arm that answers `1.0` for a
brush that is not a picture at all — the alternative was the same `clamp` written twice, which is the
shape this entry exists to stop. ⚠️ **And the clamp is not decoration.** `build::brush_is_finite` asks
only that `alpha` is *finite*, so a hand-edited or third-party `.ondin` reaches this with `-3.0` or
`1e30`, and `Color32::gamma_multiply` outside `0..=1` is not a fade. ⚠️ **Not folded into
`stops_of`'s picture arm**, which is a flat grey placeholder for a picture that could not be decoded
rather than a picture — fading it would say something about a photograph nobody can see.

🚨 **`picker::ramp`'s doc asserted the opposite of the function under it, and had since D773's own
commit (`efc1072`).** It read *"it does not fold in `GradientBrush::opacity`, and since §15 D767 that
is a gap"* — written as the **statement of the defect**, with D773 then fixing the gap by folding the
multiplier in three lines below and the paragraph not following. **A comment that describes the bug
you are fixing is the one a fix leaves standing**, because its author reads it as the problem
statement rather than as a claim about the code, and the more precisely it describes the defect the
more invisible it becomes once the defect is gone. It also proposed the design that was **not** taken
— *"that is what makes this a caller-side fix rather than a change here"* — where the fix is not
caller-side at all: `ramp` folds and `stop_colours` is the named opt-out, so the common case is the
default and the one surface that edits the stops opts out by name. **The sentence describing the
rejected alternative outlived the decision to reject it.** Nothing gates either half: it compiles, it
lints, its links resolve.

*(Seven tests across `layers`, `ui` and `paint`, flipped both ways at both surfaces with the predicted
sites holding — ignoring the picture fails `a_faded_picture_fades_its_row_thumbnail` at its **first**
assertion, which is the reported symptom rather than the mechanism, and folding the alpha into the
**undimmed arm only** is green everywhere except
`dimming_and_a_faded_picture_compose_rather_than_one_winning`: one flip, one assertion, which is what
says that test carries the composition rule on its own. ⚠️ **One flip result is recorded rather than
left to be rediscovered**: `an_out_of_range_alpha_is_clamped_at_both_ends` is **green against the
pre-fix code**, both sides of each assertion collapsing to `WHITE`, so it has teeth only once

**that one is green under the flip the first catches**, so the two pin different halves — *is it

chips paragraph amended in the same place D773 left it open; §9.2's dimmed-thumbnail sentence gains
the second multiplier; §9.4's *"untinted"* is corrected. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, which
carries no row on the chips.)*

**D787 — `paint.rs`'s head and §9.2's claim say what is true. *Record fixed 2026-09-15; Resolved for
the record half — the code half is `[S23.1-L1-05]`'s and is not done.***

`[S23.2-L3-04]`. `panels::paint`'s module head promised two things: *"no egui"*, and *"**every** rule
about how an edit rewrites a brush lives here so the two cannot drift"* — the two being the
inspector's fill and stroke lists and the detached picker. 🚨 **`architecture.md` §9.2 said the same
in the document's own voice**, which is what makes this a record defect rather than a stale comment:
*"`paint.rs` owns every rule about how an edit rewrites a brush"*, and *"it is the reason the
inspector's paint rows and the picker cannot disagree about what an edit means"*. **Both halves were
false.**

**egui.** `paint::CharWrite` is `Valve(&egui::Response)`. The module also holds `PaintDrag` and
`Slots`, which carry `f32` screen spans off last frame's layout. Neither is *"pure `Brush` in,
`Brush` out"*.

**Every rule.** The hex edit is the counter-example, and `[S23.1-L1-05]` had already enumerated the
four ways its two copies — `inspector::paint_hex_field` and `picker::hex_row` — differ. **Three of
those four are rules about how an edit rewrites a brush**, which is exactly what §9.2 puts in this
module, and `paint.rs` holds **none** of them: what alpha goes out with a typed colour over a set
that disagrees; whether an unchanged colour is written at all; and whether an unrepresentable colour
is quantised before it is stored. What the module *does* offer that path is `with_stops`, which takes
the alpha decision as an **argument** — i.e. it is the mechanism for applying a rule that lives
somewhere else.

🚨 **A promise that is load-bearing while untrue is worse than no promise at all.** A reviewer who
reads *"the two cannot drift"* concludes the drift is impossible and stops looking — and
`[S23.1-L1-02]` is the measurement of those two panels doing precisely that, with the sentence
guaranteeing they could not sitting in the source of truth the whole time. **The guarantee was doing
work, and the work it was doing was stopping somebody checking.**

⚠️ **The code half is not this entry, and saying so is the point of the verdict line.**
`[S23.1-L1-05]` owns it — delete `hex_row`'s field, call `paint_hex_field`, and lift the three rules
into `paint.rs` as one function — and it moves a shipped control, so it is its own change with its
own risk. What is closed here is the pair of documents that claimed it had already happened.

*(Record fixed 2026-09-15; no production line changed — a module head and two §9.2 sentences.
🚨 **§9.2 had to be amended and not only the comment**, which is the half a code edit cannot reach:
correcting the head alone leaves `architecture.md` asserting the guarantee, and the next careful
reader holding both in view repairs the **code** to match the document — **D666**'s direction, where
§9.4 stated `menu_place`'s order backwards and agreeing with it would have introduced the bug. ⚠️
**The §9.2 tree entry at the head of the section is left alone deliberately**: *"pure `Brush` algebra
shared by the two + the list-generic reorder"* already names the reorder pieces, so it admits the
half that is not pure. ⚠️ **No test, and none is possible for this one** — the defect was a sentence,
and nothing in this project can see a conflict between a claim and the code it is about. What catches
the next instance is somebody reading the head against the module, which is how this one was found.
Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose hex row is about routing the field's **commit timing** through
`edit_valve` and is a different open question.)*

**D774 — §3's wgpu rule could not be obeyed by anybody. *Record fixed 2026-09-15; Resolved — and the
half of it that was true is tested now.***

`[A2-L7-04]`. §3 read *"Only `ondin-render` may depend on `vello`, `vello_cpu`, `wgpu`"*. **The wgpu
third is not a rule the code has drifted from; it is a rule no arrangement of this workspace can
satisfy.** `VelloGpuRenderer::new` takes `&Device`, and `render` takes `&Device`, `&Queue` and
`&TextureView` — all wgpu types — so nothing can call the GPU backend at all without naming them.
That seam is deliberate: **`ondin-render` does not own the device.** eframe owns it, vello renders
the canvas into a texture and `egui-wgpu` composites that texture, so the two must draw onto one
wgpu, which is what the workspace manifest's `INTEROP PINS` header has said all along — `=29.0.4`,
*"dictated by them, never chosen freely"*. `ondin-app` declares `wgpu.workspace = true` today and is
right to.

🚨 **A rule nobody can obey is a false statement rather than an aspiration.** That is the whole
entry, and where it was sitting is what makes it worth one: in the document `CLAUDE.md` calls the
source of truth, in the section whose entire job is to say what may depend on what, three bullets
above the sentence that names the test enforcing its neighbours. The amended bullet is
*stronger* than the one it replaces, because it carries the reason — a reader who knows why the two
share a wgpu cannot accidentally "tidy" the sharing away.

⚠️ **The app names those types through eframe's re-export, and that is worth knowing before anybody
narrows the rule back on the strength of it.** `canvas.rs` has `use eframe::wgpu;`, and there is no
`use wgpu::` anywhere in `crates/ondin-app/src` — nor `use egui::`, nor `use egui_wgpu::`, all three
crates arriving by the same door. So the direct manifest line is an **interop pin** rather than the
thing that makes the source compile. **It does not rescue the old rule**: eframe puts wgpu in the
app's tree whatever any manifest says, and the transitive reading is the one `deps_forbidden` uses
for every other rule in §3. It does mean those three declarations are a question worth asking one
day — D427's shape exactly, a manifest line with no `use` behind it — and this entry records it
rather than asking it, because a pin that asserts a version is not the same as a dependency nobody
uses.

*(§3's bullet amended, and the enforcement bullet under it; both `ondin-render`'s and `ondin-app`'s
manifest head comments carry the citation. ⚠️ **`canvas.rs`'s count of `wgpu::` mentions was written
into that comment as *"thirteen"* and is **twelve** — the thirteenth line a naive grep returns is
`use eframe::egui_wgpu::RenderState`, which `wgpu::` matches inside `egui_wgpu::`. **Replaced with
the command rather than with a corrected number**, per this file's standing lesson that a count in
prose is a gate nobody built:
`grep -cE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])wgpu::' crates/ondin-app/src/canvas.rs`. **The vello half is tested now
and has its own entry — D775.** Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose only wgpu rows are about the
version pins and the blocked egui bump, which this does not touch. Closes `[A2-L7-04]`.)*

**D775 — §3 states four layering rules and exactly one of them had a test. *Fixed and tested
2026-09-15; Resolved.***

`[A2-L7-05]`. `ondin-core/tests/deps_forbidden.rs` enforced one rule — core is headless — against a
hard-coded pair of subjects. 🚨 **Two of the other three were already false with every gate green**,
and neither had left any trace of when it stopped being true: `ondin-mcp` reached vello through an
`ondin-export` edge no line of its source used (D427), and §3's wgpu clause could not be obeyed at
all (D774). **An unenforced layering rule in this repository does not stay true**, which is the
argument for a table rather than for a crate.

`RULES` is that table, one row per rule a dependency tree can express: `ondin-core` → `HEADLESS`
(invariant 1), `ondin-mcp` → `HEADLESS` (§3), and `ondin-render` and `ondin-export` → `NO_UI`, which
is §3's *"only `ondin-app` may depend on egui/winit"* read against the two crates that sit between
core and the app and could quietly acquire chrome.

🚨 **`NO_UI` is a second list and not a filter over `HEADLESS`, and collapsing them is what a later
editor will try.** `glutin_wgl_sys` really is under both `ondin-render` and `ondin-export` —
`wgpu-hal` 29.0.4 pulls it for the GL backend, readable in `Cargo.lock` — so a row reusing the
headless list would fail a crate doing nothing whatever wrong. `ash`, `metal`, `naga` and
`raw-window-handle` are absent for the same reason: every one of them arrives legitimately under
wgpu. Core is forbidden them because core may have **no GPU at all**, which is a different rule with
a different reason, and merging the two lists is precisely what makes the stricter one unstatable.

⚠️ **One walk per rule rather than one walk carrying a stack**, and the reason is that the rows no
longer share a list. `ondin-core` sits *inside* `ondin-render`'s subtree, and core's forbidden list
contains `vello`, which render is allowed. A single walk that re-rooted on the inner subject would
report render's own vello against core; one that did not would check core against render's looser
list. Neither is the rule. The tree is parsed once and walked four times, which costs nothing beside
the one `cargo tree` call — and it stays **one** call, because running cargo inside `cargo test` is
the riskiest thing the file does and a second invocation is a second chance to contend for the
package-cache lock (D427).

🚨 **The vello rule is a second *test*, `only_ondin_render_declares_vello`, and it reads the
manifests — which is the part most worth carrying.** §3's rule is about what a crate may **declare**,
not about what a tree may contain: `ondin-app` and `ondin-export` both reach vello through
`ondin-render` by construction, so there is no subtree anywhere in which its absence could be
asserted. **That is *why* this rule went untested while the other three did**, and it is the trap a
reader generalising `RULES` walks into — the row cannot be made green as a tree row, so it reads as
unenforceable and gets dropped. The finding's own words: *"each row that cannot be made green today
is a decision to record, not a row to omit."* It is enforceable; it is simply a different question.
**Who declares it**, not **who can reach it**, and **neither test can express the other's rule.**

**Flip-checked.** Adding `"kurbo"` to `NO_UI` fails naming `kurbo (under ondin-export)` and
`kurbo (under ondin-render)` **separately**, so the per-rule walk really does find what is under each
subject rather than reporting one subtree twice. Adding `vello.workspace = true` to
`crates/ondin-export/Cargo.toml` fails the manifest test with `["ondin-export", "ondin-render"]`
against `["ondin-render"]` **while the tree test stays green** — which demonstrates the
two-tests-for-two-questions point rather than arguing it, and is the flip to re-run if anybody
proposes folding them. Both tests carry a vacuity guard, `unseen` and `manifests >= 4`, because a
parse that matched nothing would read as compliance in either of them.

⚠️ **Reverting the second flip left a `vello` edge in `Cargo.lock` that reverting the manifest alone
did not remove**; only a re-resolve took it out, and `git diff` is what caught it. That is
`CLAUDE.md`'s *"`git diff` after a hand revert"* rule firing for real, in a shape its own list does
not yet name: **the artefact a flip leaves behind need not be in the file the flip edited.**

*(§3's enforcement bullet amended, and a bullet added for the manifest test. **D427 is extended
rather than corrected** — its subject count of two was true when it was written and this widens it to
four. ⚠️ **`HEADLESS`'s doc still says the right shape is an allowlist and that §3's list is correct
enough to build one from**; that inversion is still unwritten and is not this change. Nothing struck
from `roadmap.md`, which carries no row on the layering gate. Closes `[A2-L7-05]`.)*

**D776 — The sibling half of the pass count, and it is the half nothing bounds. *Measured and
recorded 2026-09-15; the case D763 left unmeasured is the unbounded one. `[S11.2-L4-05]` stayed open
on this entry and is **closed by §15 D779**, which declines the pool on this arithmetic.***

§15 D763 measured the `K` in `[S11.2-L4-05]`'s `K × ~5.7 ms` — the per-renderer half of which is
**6–8 ms** measured on an idle adapter, §15 D777 — on a *nested* document and found it to
be the nesting **depth** — one blur → 1 pass, three deep → 3 — which de-ranked the finding to about
17 ms of pipeline build paid once in the life of the process. It closed by saying in as many words
that the case `pack`'s budget rule is actually about was still unmeasured: *"Depth is bounded by how
deeply a designer nests groups; area is not."* **This is that measurement, and the two answers are
not alike.**

`gpu_effects.rs`'s new `siblings(n, size)` fixture puts `n` blurred 45×45 squares at **one** level,
all of them on the page, staggered by two points so no two resolve to the identical box — a packer
that deduplicated would otherwise read as a packer that packed.
`how_many_effect_passes_a_level_of_siblings_demands` counts the passes on an RTX 4070 Ti:

```text
               n=1   n=4   n=8   n=16   n=32
  100×100       1     2     3      6     11   passes
  200×200       1     1     1      2      3
  400×400       1     1     1      1      1
```

🚨 **`K` grows with the sibling count and nothing caps it.** D763's figure and this one are both true
and they answer different questions, which is the whole trap: **a reader who has only the first
concludes `K ≤ 3`**, and the first is the one that reads like the answer to the finding, because it
is the one that de-ranked it.

**The divisor is the page, and that is what makes a 100×100 fixture honest.** Four times the page
area is four times the per-chunk capacity and so a quarter of the passes, the counts being that ratio
taken to a ceiling — so the quantity is a **ratio**, total effect-buffer area ÷ page area, rather
than a property of a small drawing.

⚠️ **The table is exactly what `pack` computes, and that agreement is worth keeping**:
`effect::reach(3.0)` is 4.5, so each square's buffer is about 54 px on a side, three of them fit
inside the 100×100 page's 10,000-pixel budget and four do not, and ⌈32/3⌉ = 11, ⌈16/3⌉ = 6,
⌈8/3⌉ = 3, ⌈4/3⌉ = 2. Thirteen fit at 200×200 and fifty-four at 400×400, which is the other two
rows. **The measurement and the arithmetic agree, so the number is the budget rule and not something
else about the device** — and the agreement survives a pixel either way in the outward rounding.

⚠️ **What this does not say is that a real document reaches those numbers, and the arithmetic for one
is reasoned from `pack` rather than measured at that size.** At 1920×1080 the budget is 2,073,600
pixels and a 200×200 square blurred at radius 3 has a 209×209 buffer — about 44k — so it takes
forty-odd *overlapping* on-screen effect layers to demand a second pass. That is a busy file rather
than a casual one, and it is the arithmetic the severity should be argued from.

🚨 **But at that size the binding constraint is not the one the fixture measures, so a reader
re-deriving the figure from the ratio alone gets the right order for the wrong reason.** `pack`
weighs the packed texture's **bounding box** and not the ink in it, and the shelf wraps at the device
limit — 8192, because the app requests `wgpu::Limits::default()` and `effects::MAX_EFFECT_BUFFER_SIDE`
is that number for the same reason. Thirty-nine 209-pixel layers fill one row at 8151×209, which is
1.70M and inside the budget; the fortieth wraps, the box becomes 8151×418 = 3.4M, and it is over at a
stroke. So the break lands at **39** where the ink ratio says 47. The two agree on *about forty* by
coincidence. **The fixture's break is area-driven and a full-page document's is row-driven**, which
is the thing to know before anybody widens the fixture, or its page, and concludes the rule changed.

⚠️ **It is a measurement and not a licence to bound the pool.** §15 **D344** is why there is one
renderer per pass — a **correctness** rule rather than a saving, whose symptom was a pasted image
drawing nothing from the second frame onwards, because vello's atlas evicts a picture that has not
been drawn for two resolve passes. D763 already put the burden on any bound-and-reuse scheme to argue
against that entry directly, and what this changes is only that the severity can now be argued from a
number instead of from a guess. ⚠️ **D777 has since taken D344's *other* number away without
touching that argument** — the 84 ms does not reproduce and the build is 6–8 ms on an idle adapter,
seven times that when the test suite is contending for it — which cuts the
`11 × ` above to about **77 ms on one frame**, and **a cheaper renderer is an argument for building
them rather than for sharing one.**

**Flip-checked against the plausible wrong version rather than against nothing** — `budget` set to
`u64::MAX`, i.e. the pre-D402 packer that had no page rule at all. Predicted to fail on the first
assertion, and it does: 32 siblings come back as **1** pass. ⚠️ **The second assertion is the one the
first cannot make.** `roomy == 1` says the divisor is the *page* and not a constant, so a budget
pinned to any fixed number leaves it red — and it needs a **fresh** renderer, because
`pass_high_water` is a high-water mark and reusing the crowded page's would report that page's number
for the roomy one.

*(Measured and recorded 2026-09-15; `[S11.2-L4-05]` stayed open on this entry and **§15 D779 closes
it**, the pool declined on the arithmetic above. No production line changed — a
fixture, a test, and a correction to the neighbouring test's doc, which said *"`K` is the nesting
depth, not a function of how many effect layers a document has"* without saying for which case.
**D763 amended**: its ⚠️ said the sibling case *"is still unmeasured"*, which is false now, and it
points here instead — the distinction that paragraph draws is the valuable part and is kept, and its
heading and index row now say *"for a nested document"*. §6.3's pass bullet carried the same sentence
and is amended with it. 🚨 **And grepping for the claim rather than for the entry turned up an older
copy of it, twice**: §6.3 and **D344** both still said *"the layer count no longer changes the pass
count"*, which **D402 falsified in 2026-09-01** when it gave `pack` the page budget — D402's own
index row says so in as many words, and the two passages it contradicts were never amended. Both
carry the proviso now. **The measurement they rest on stands**; those 20 layers packed into one
texture. The test is `#[ignore]`d and needs a GPU adapter. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose
effect-pass rows are struck already.)*

**D777 — A vello `Renderer` costs 6–8 ms to build, not 84, and this file held both figures at once.
*Measured 2026-09-15; D344's figure is amended rather than struck. `[S11.2-L4-05]` stayed open on
this entry and is **closed by §15 D779**, which declines the pool on this band and D776's `K`.***

§15 **D344** says *"A vello `Renderer` costs 84 ms to build (49 with area-only antialiasing)"*;
`[S11.2-L4-05]`, **D763** and **D776** all say *"~5.7 ms"*. Both are in this file, both are live,
neither cites the other, and the finding that is still open is ranked on `K ×` the smaller one.
🚨 **A record that disagrees with itself about a number is worse than one that is silent**, because
each half reads as settled on its own and nothing in this project can see the pair — the doc gate
resolves links, the citation census counts D-numbers, the tests assert outcomes, and a figure in
prose passes all three. It survived three weeks and two entries that quoted one half of it.

`gpu_effects.rs`'s `a_vello_renderer_costs_about_six_milliseconds_to_build` times six consecutive
`vello::Renderer::new(&device, RendererOptions::default())` calls against one device. RTX 4070 Ti,
vello 0.9.0, `--release`, **run twice minutes apart**:

```text
         run 1      run 2
  #0   15.05 ms   15.04 ms   <- first in the process
  #1    6.46 ms    7.49 ms
  #2    6.24 ms    7.33 ms
  #3    5.99 ms    7.65 ms
  #4    5.96 ms    7.86 ms
  #5    5.62 ms    7.51 ms
```

⚠️ **Twice deliberately, because one run reads as a precision this has not got**: the marginal build
is a **6–8 ms band** and the two runs do not overlap in it, while the cold one is 15 ms to within a
hundredth both times. **Quote the band, not a figure** — which is what the `~5.7 ms` in three places
already gets slightly wrong in the other direction.

🚨 **And quote the *condition* with it, which is the half this entry nearly shipped without.** Both
runs above are of an **otherwise-idle adapter**. Run inside the whole on-device suite, which the
harness runs in parallel with thirteen other tests sharing the one adapter, the same six calls come
back **121.72 / 65.27 / 49.25 / 49.69 / 49.88 / 48.31 ms** — about seven times the idle figure.
⚠️ **`--test-threads=1` over that same suite gives 15.50 / 7.19 / 7.48 / 6.86 / 6.89 / 7.26,
reproducing the isolated numbers exactly, and that is the control that makes this *contention* and
not drift** — without it the parallel run reads as a measurement that has moved, which is the reading
a machine three weeks from now would have taken. **6–8 ms is still the figure `[S11.2-L4-05]` wants**,
the app not building renderers from thirteen threads; what the contended number is for is the reader
who measures this the easy way and gets fifty.

**So ~5.7 ms is the right order and D344's 84 ms does not reproduce, not as a marginal build and not
as the cold one, under either condition above.**
And it is the *same option set*: `RendererOptions::default()` is `AaSupport::all()`
(`vello-0.9.0/src/lib.rs:408`), which is precisely the arm D344 priced at 84 rather than the
area-only one it priced at 49. Both `VelloGpuRenderer::new` and the per-pass builds in
`render_to_texture_with_effects` take that default, so the thing measured here is the thing the app
builds.

🚨 **What the measurement cannot say is *why*, and the obvious explanation does not survive being
checked.** A figure that old invites *"vello has moved"* — it has not. **D337** (2026-08-24) and
**D339** (2026-08-25) both name `vello` **0.9**, D337 in the same breath as the `vello_cpu` 0.0.9
that **D414** later replaced, and the workspace has pinned `=0.9.0` ever since; D344 is 2026-08-25.
**The renderer D344 timed is this renderer.** What D344 does *not* record is the **profile**, the
machine or the version, and this measurement is `--release` — that was the only difference the record
could see until the contention figures below added a second, and it is a candidate rather than a
finding. So this entry says the figure **does not
reproduce**, not that it was wrong: nothing available now can tell a stale measurement from a
mismeasured one, and the reason the disagreement lived three weeks is exactly that absence.
**Write the profile, the machine and the version beside a timing, or the next reader can do nothing
with it but doubt it.**

⚠️ **Contention is now a third candidate, it is the most interesting of the three, and it does not
close either.** Under load this build is 48–65 ms and the first is 121.72, so **84 stops being
fifteen-fold away from anything reachable and starts sitting inside an ordinary spread** — and D344
was written on the day the GPU effect passes landed, which is a session running on-device tests.
🚨 **But it does not reconstruct D344's *pair*, and that is what stops it being an answer**: seven
times our measured `AaSupport::all()` build is **49**, which is D344's *area-only* figure rather than
its 84, so making both halves fit needs two different multipliers on two configurations. **The
numbers land in the same region and the arithmetic does not land at all.** So the list is profile,
machine and machine *load*, none of them established — and **the verdict is unchanged, because 84
reproduces under neither condition**, as a marginal build or as a cold one. It is recorded here as a
candidate the record could not previously offer, and **not** as the explanation; a plausible cause
written down as a fact is worse than no cause at all, since the next reader inherits it as settled.

⚠️ **What it changes for the open finding.** The marginal renderer is what `[S11.2-L4-05]` needs and
it is the 6–8 ms one. `VelloGpuRenderer` builds one `Renderer` up front and one more per effect
pass, so a document that first demands `K` passes pays about `(K − high-water) × 7 ms` on that frame
and nothing on any frame after it, `layers` only ever growing. **At D776's worst measured `K` of 11
that is about 77 ms on one frame** — a visible hitch, once, and then nothing.

🚨 **This shipped with a wall-clock drift guard at 40 ms, it had to come out within the hour, and the
way it failed is worth more than the number it asserted.** The bound was chosen as *"about seven
times the measurement"*, to be generous against ordinary machine-to-machine variation — **and seven
is exactly what contention turns out to be worth here**, so it was guaranteed to pass every time the
test ran alone and to fail the first time the whole suite ran, which is what happened. *A margin
picked to be generous was picked at the size of the effect it needed to survive*, and nothing about
choosing it could have revealed that, because the effect had not been measured yet.

⚠️ **It is also D776's own trap committed into the test that cites D776, one hour after that entry
was written.** *"A number measured for the wrong case reads exactly like a number measured for the
right one"* — and the wrong case here was not a fixture or a page size, it was **the machine the
assertion runs on**, which is a dimension neither entry had thought to name. **A wall-clock bound
cannot be a gate in a parallel harness**: loose enough to survive contention is loose enough to catch
nothing, and tight enough to catch drift fails on a busy machine. There is no setting of that
constant that is both.

**What replaces it asserts that the loop timed five marginal builds and nothing about the clock** —
*the numbers above are of nothing* if it did not — so the test still cannot pass vacuously while
making no claim it cannot keep. ⚠️ **The removal is a result rather than a retraction**, and it
sharpens D434 rather than contradicting it: *assert against a dependency's behaviour and not against
its number* is right, and **a duration is not a behaviour**. `png::MAX_RASTER_SIDE` works because
rendering at the cap either succeeds or does not; a build time has no such answer. The behavioural
question here — *is a renderer built per pass at all* — is already `pass_high_water`'s, and D763
asserts it. ⚠️ **There is nothing of ours to flip either way**: this times a dependency, so the six
figures and their conditions are the deliverable and the pass never was.

*(Measured 2026-09-15; **no production line changed** — a fixture-free test and three amendments.
**D344 amended**: its 84/49 sentence keeps its figure and gains the note that it does not reproduce,
because deleting it would take the *reason* renderers are built on demand with it. 🚨 **D344's
correctness argument is untouched and is still the thing any bound-and-reuse scheme has to answer** —
one renderer per pass exists because vello's atlas evicts a picture not *drawn* for two resolve
passes, and the symptom was a pasted image going blank from the second frame onwards. **A cheaper
renderer is an argument for building them, not for sharing one.** **D763 and D776 amended** where
they quote `~5.7 ms`, and §6.3's `3 × 5.7 ms` with them; D763's index row too. ⚠️ **The comment
shipped with the test said vello had moved several versions and that is corrected in place**, which
is the same *"grep the claim, not the entry"* that D776 was written out of. The test is `#[ignore]`d
and needs a GPU adapter. **`[S11.2-L4-05]` stayed open on this entry and §15 D779 closes it.**
Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose effect-pass rows are struck already.
⚠️ **Five `crates/` comments carried `~5.7 ms` and all five have the band and this number now** —

makes it stop matching the thing it cites. 🚨 **The population was found by grepping the claim and

and the two this entry's own test carries, and **no sixth** — which is the check D754 asks for, run
on a list of five that was handed over rather than derived. **The `gpu.rs` field doc is the one that
needed more than a number**: *"the per-renderer cost is measured"* is a true sentence resting on a
contested premise, so a reader who looks D344 up finds 84 and discredits it. It now names both
figures and says which one was timed. ⚠️ **It gained the ruling the same day**: §15 **D779** declines
the pool, so that doc now carries the measurement and the decision taken on it.
⚠️ **Two neighbouring sentences at those sites were stale in a way this entry did not create and
are corrected while open**: `pass_high_water`'s *"nothing in the suite answers it"* — D763's and
D776's tests answer it for **fixtures**, and what is unread is a real drawing — and the loop's
*"the per-renderer cost is measured; **K is not**"*, which those same two entries falsified. **What
the case rests on is no longer that `K` is unknown but that nothing bounds it.**
🚨 **Amended the same day, and the sweep had to be run twice for it.** The band was written into
those five sites and §6.3 *without its condition*, an hour before the condition was known — so the
population this entry had just corrected became the population that needed correcting again, by the
same phrase-grep, and **every quotation of 6–8 ms in the tree now carries *"idle adapter"* with
it**. That is this entry's own *"quote the band, not a figure"* needing one more clause, and it is
the cheapest possible demonstration of why: a figure with no condition reads as unconditional, and
five copies of it are five places a reader learns the wrong thing.)*

**D779 — The bound-and-reuse renderer pool is declined: after D776 and D777 the bill is a one-off
hitch, and the pool has to argue with a correctness rule rather than with a cost. *Ruling by the
maintainer; recorded 2026-09-15; Resolved — `[S11.2-L4-05]` is closed and the pool is a decided
non-goal.***

`[S11.2-L4-05]` asks for the effect passes' renderers to be bounded and reused instead of built one
per pass. **No** — and the two entries above are the reason, because between them they turn the
finding's `K × ~5.7 ms` into a quantity with a shape.

**D776 says what `K` is**: a ratio of total effect-buffer area to page area, not a count of effect
layers. Thirty-two blurred siblings are **11** passes on a 100×100 page, **3** on a 200×200 one and
**1** at 400×400, and at 1920×1080 it takes on the order of **forty overlapping on-screen effect
layers** to demand a second pass at all. **D777 says what a pass costs**: a **6–8 ms** band on an
idle adapter, 15 ms for the first in the process — not D344's 84. So the worst `K` this project has
ever measured, 11 on a fixture page a fraction of a window's area, is about **77 ms, once**, on the
frame that first demands it; every frame after it holds the renderers already built. **A bill that
is paid once is not a pool.**

🚨 **And a pool is not a cost question at the end of it, which is the half the finding does not
reach.** §15 **D344** is why there is one renderer per pass and it is a **correctness** rule:
vello's image atlas evicts a resident image that has not been *drawn* for two resolve passes, so a
renderer doing N passes in a frame loses any picture appearing in only one of them. The symptom it
was written for was **a pasted image going blank from the second frame onwards** — not a stutter, a
missing photograph. Trading a one-off hitch for a re-run of that is the wrong way round, and D777
sharpens the direction rather than softening it: **a cheaper renderer is an argument for building
more of them, not for sharing one.**

⚠️ **The next step is written down rather than left to taste, and it is not the finding's.** If the
hitch is ever *felt* — a real drawing, a visible stall on the frame an effect stack first appears —
the thing to try is building renderers **off the critical frame**, ahead of the pass that will want
one, which leaves D344's rule untouched because each still does a single pass per frame. Reuse is
the last resort rather than the first, and it wants an on-device test reproducing D344's symptom
**before** anything is shared, not after: that bug is invisible on frame one and arrives on frame
two, which is exactly the shape a test written to a regression report is tuned not to see.

*(Ruling by the maintainer; recorded 2026-09-15; no production line changed. **Closes
`[S11.2-L4-05]`.** ⚠️ **The citation sits on `pass_high_water`'s accessor doc**, beside the two
measurements, so the next reader to meet the number meets the ruling taken on it — this being a
record-only entry, which is D735's shape and D741's fix for it. **D776 and D777 amended** where
each says *"`[S11.2-L4-05]` stays open"*, which was true when it was written and is the sentence a
reader consults to find out whether a decision has been made — the failure D782 is about, met the
same day in the same file. §6.3's pass bullet gains the ruling beside the figures it already
carries. ⚠️ **What is *not* declined is the measurement D776 asks for** — `pass_high_water` read on
a real drawing rather than on a fixture — which stands, since a trigger nobody can observe is not a
trigger. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`, whose effect-pass rows are struck already.)*

**D780 — The SVG writer gets the reader's fidelity channel, and the finding's flat list of four is two
lists. *Built and tested 2026-09-15; Resolved — this closes the round's last open High.***

🚨 **`[S8.1-L7-05]` is the last open High and had been open unnoticed since 2026-09-04**, which is
worth carrying because the mechanism is one this project has no other instance of. The maintainer
promoted it **Debt → High at T3** on an instruction given at T2; `review/index.md`'s `Sev` cell read
*"Debt → promote at T3"* — **the record of the promotion sitting in the column that holds the
severity** — so every tally that folded that cell to its first word filed an open High under Debt. The
nine findings T2 said were blocked behind it have all since closed anyway, so the anchor sat open with
nothing queued behind it, which is why nobody noticed.

⚠️ **The cell was corrected to `High` at the close of the same session, on the maintainer's
instruction, and it is the one row in that generated table edited on purpose.** Nothing was lost —
the promotion note was already in that row's *Claim* column, two sentences along, which is where a
note *about* a severity belongs. **The general rule is worth more than the repair**: a column a
census reads is an **input**, not prose, and a value and a note about the value must not share one.
Left uncorrected it would have gone on mis-filing this finding **after** it closed, in the other
direction.

**The asymmetry is the whole finding.** `svg_in::Import` carries `skipped` and `approximated`
precisely so a lossy **read** can tell the user; `svg_of` returned a bare `String`, so a lossy
**write** could not. The four losses the writer knew about were each written down in a doc comment
only a developer would ever read, and the export UI had nothing to show because the function it called
could not tell it anything. `svg::svg_of_reported -> Export { svg, approximated, round_trip }` is the
function now and **`svg_of` is the shim** — that way round rather than the other because the report is
the *new* thing and every existing caller wants the markup: `plan::bytes`, the CLI, the round-trip
suites and thirty-odd assertions take a `String`. The two callers that face a user ask for the report:
the export card, which is what somebody reads *before* exporting and so the one moment a note can
still change what they do, and *Copy as SVG*, which is the one export with no file to inspect
afterwards. Both word it through one `panels::fidelity_clauses`, in the **same two-clause shape as the
paste message** on the reader's side, because the two ends of a round trip are read by the same person
and a second vocabulary for one idea is a second thing to learn.

🚨 **Two lists and not one, and that is a correction to the finding.** Two of its four are a different
kind of loss, by this writer's own argument, and it says so at both sites. A flipped rail is written
as a **reversed path** and `text::PathWarp::flip` *is* traversing the rail backwards — §15 **D406**
decides it in as many words, *"it is **not an approximation**, because our own flip *is* traversing
the rail backwards, so the reversed path is the identical drawing rather than a stand-in"*, and *"the
cost is that the round trip loses which of two spellings the flip was in, not the flip"*. The image
fill's `<pattern>` was measured in Chrome over HTTP **by `[S8.1-L7-05]` itself**, which reports the
picture landing exactly where the document puts it and concludes that *"the entire loss belongs to
`svg_in`, not to this writer"*. So `Export::approximated` means **the picture differs** and
`Export::round_trip` means **the picture is right and the document will not come back**. Telling a
user their image fill was *approximated*, over an export that is correct in a real renderer, sends
them after a bug that is not there — which is `Import`'s own argument for splitting `skipped` from
`approximated`, one step along.

🚨 **The report is read off the node at emit time, under the visibility guard, and deliberately not in
`collect_defs`.** That pass is where it belongs by every other measure: it already walks every origin,
already carries a `&mut` and already sees all five features. **It has no visibility guard** — it
recurses into hidden children on purpose, because an unreferenced def is harmless and skipping one
would mean a second visibility rule to keep in step with `emit_node`'s. A report built there announces
a sweep gradient on a layer the file does not contain, and there is a test for exactly that.

⚠️ **Three conditions on the shadow arm, two of which the first draft was missing.** A spread of zero
emits no `feMorphology` at all; an effect with `visible: false` is skipped by `effect_def`'s own loop;
and the whole `<filter>` is absent unless `effect_region` could answer, which is what `filter_written`
carries in from the caller. **Each of the three is a way to warn a user about markup that is not in
the file** — the exact failure mode of a report that restates a rule instead of observing one.

*(Eight tests in a new `crates/ondin-export/tests/fidelity.rs`, **each pairing a reported claim with
the markup that caused it** — *it says sweep* / *there is a `<radialGradient>` in the file* — so the
report cannot drift from the writer, which is the only way a list like this stays worth reading. ⚠️
**The brief for this entry said nine and the file has eight**; the figure is the count of `#[test]`
attributes in that file and is best re-run rather than carried. ⚠️ **The hidden-layer test asserts its
own fixture is in the state it is about**, by un-hiding the node and watching the report appear —
without that, *"nothing is reported"* is green if the hidden sibling is missing, visible, or carries
no sweep. `emit_node` gains an eighth parameter and an `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` carrying
its reason: the alternative was folding `defs` and `report` into one struct purely to get under the
counter, and they are an immutable lookup table and a mutable sink, related only by both being
pass-wide — **a type that exists to please a lint is worse code than the lint**. §7's opening
signature now names the reported form, and its model-completeness paragraph — *"anything it can only
approximate must say so out loud"* — records that it now says so to the **user** rather than only in
this writer's prose. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`: its *Now · SVG import* row's *"nothing here is
lost silently"* is a claim about the **reader**, and no row has ever carried the writer's side. Closes
`[S8.1-L7-05]`.)*

**D781 — A differential between the two document walks, and it answers the question the finding said
it could not. *Built and tested 2026-09-15; Resolved.***

`[A1-L7-07]` says `svg::emit_node` re-decides eleven things `scene::build` also decides — visibility,
opacity, clip, mask and mask mode, effects, fill rule, paint order, the stroke-alignment clip, the
missing-image placeholder and image framing — without going through `scene::build` or `ScenePainter`,
and that the agreement is held by convention plus one golden. 🚨 **It has diverged twice on record.**
§15 **D179**'s frame background reached the placeholder rule a step late, so *"a frame whose picture
had gone drew the cross on canvas and exported a hole"*; and a `fill="none"` was written on the same
path. **Both were found by a human reading two files against each other**, which is not a gate.

`crates/ondin-export/tests/two_walks.rs` is the gate. **Its scope is the ink set**: for each node, did
this walk decide to put paint down for it at all. Read on both sides by giving every fixture node a
**unique solid colour** and collecting the colours each walk emits — a recording `ScenePainter` on
one side and the `fill="#rrggbb"` attributes on the other — so the comparison is a set of node
identities arrived at **without either walk being asked to report on itself**.

⚠️ **Deliberately one of the eleven and not all eleven**, and the reason is the finding's own: the two
legitimately differ elsewhere. SVG has no viewport cull. Geometry is a `BezPath` on one side and a `d`
attribute on the other. Element ordering is not call ordering. A comparison reaching for those needs a
scope argument per decision, and **an unscoped one gets switched off the first time it cries wolf**.
*Both recorded divergences were ink-set bugs* — each was a node one walk drew and the other did not —
which is why this is the one worth having rather than the one that is easiest to argue for.

🚨 **And it answers the finding's own open question, which the finding says it could not.**
`[A1-L7-07]` is explicit that it is *"not a claim that they disagree right now"* and that establishing
that by reading was not possible. **They agree**, on this tree, today. That is the second thing the
file is for: a negative result somebody can re-run, rather than a structural worry nobody can close.

**A third test asserts the agreement is about decisions and not about appearance**, and it is the one
worth reading twice. A hidden node is in neither walk; **a zero-opacity node is in both**. Zero opacity
is not invisibility — the node is drawn and composited away — so a reader "optimising" either walk to
skip it would make the two disagree **in a way no picture would show**, because the ink is invisible
either way. That is precisely the shape of the two recorded divergences: a difference of *decision*
with no difference of appearance, until something downstream reads the file.

*(Flipped with exactly that — `|| node.opacity() == 0.0` on `emit_node`'s visibility guard, the
plausible optimisation and one that changes no picture at all: all three tests fail at their predicted
sites, the first naming the one colour that went missing. ⚠️ **The fixture is asserted before the
comparison**, because two empty sets are equal and a fixture that painted nothing would be green for
ever. ⚠️ **The recording painter draws nothing below `fill_path`** — the layer stack, strokes and text
are all no-ops — deliberately, because implementing them would invite a reader to think they were
checked. §4's invariant 11 gains the boundary note: the rule is about **renderers behind one walk**
and says *document→scene* in as many words, so the SVG writer is outside it rather than in violation
of it, and that boundary now has a differential where it had a convention. §7's `fill="none"`
paragraph — which records one of the two divergences — names the test. Nothing struck from
`roadmap.md`, which carries no row on the second walk. Closes `[A1-L7-07]`.)*

**D766 — The two hand-rolled sliders bound different axes, so D673 was not a question with a side to
take. *Ruling on §15 D673; fixed and tested 2026-09-15. Resolved — the pair is described now rather
than reconciled.***

§15 D673 closes by asking the maintainer which of the app's two hand-rolled sliders is right about
whether a row owes its knob any room: `ui::slider`, whose shadow leaves its row by a point, or
`panels::picker`'s track, which allocates `+ 6.0` for exactly that reason. **Measured, the two do not
disagree.** The picker's bounds its knob **vertically** — `slider_knob` draws to radius 7.0, a 6.5
disc under a 1pt stroke at 6.5, against a half-row of 7.5, so half a point of slack top and bottom —
and lets it hang **7pt past each horizontal end, unclamped**, the centre being
`track.min.x + track.width() * t` with no inset. `ui::slider` does the reverse: it bleeds 1pt below
the row and **clamps travel to `half..width − half`**, so its knob cannot leave the rail at all.

🚨 **D673's sentence is true of one axis and silent about the one where the answers are reversed.**
It reads *"its knob is given room where `ui::slider`'s overhangs"*; on the horizontal axis it is the
picker's that overhangs and `ui::slider`'s that is bounded. Corrected there, and the ruling is that
there was nothing to rule: **neither is *the* answer, because they are not answering one question.**
⚠️ **And D673 cites *"§9.2's `ui::slider` paragraph"* three times, where the paragraph is in §9.4** —
§9.2 is *Layout*. All three corrected. A section reference that names the wrong neighbourhood reads
as having read it, which is why this is worth the three edits.

**`picker::SLIDER_H` is renamed `TRACK_H`**, and the rename is the substance rather than tidying: it
is the **rail's** thickness, 9, where `ui::SLIDER_H` is the **knob diameter**, 11, with
`SLIDER_RAIL_H` of 3 under it. Two constants of one name and two quantities, in a module that also
imports `ui::`. ⚠️ **Unifying the values would have been a category error**, which is the thing D673
half-proposed: setting the picker's to 11 thickens the two gradient strips, re-corners them
(`mask_corners` reads `TRACK_H * 0.5`), and leaves the knob exactly where it was, because this
module's knob is a fixed 6.5/7.0 the constant does not derive.

🚨 **Nothing in `picker.rs` asserted a single slider dimension.** Eleven tests covering chips,
placement, hex fields, radial centres and palettes, and not one touching `slider_track` or
`slider_knob` — which is how a live §15 entry could describe this geometry wrongly for six days with
every gate green and nothing to disagree.
`picker::tests::the_alpha_knob_stays_inside_the_cards_padding_at_both_ends` measures the knob's
**ink** out of the painter at both ends of its travel. It asserts the vertical clearance, that the
overhang still exists at all — if somebody clamps it, this test and `slider_track`'s doc both want
rewriting rather than deleting — and that it is within `PAD`. ⚠️ **That last one is a fact about the
*card* and not about the slider**: `PAD` is 11 against a 7pt overhang, which is exactly the kind of
accidental clearance a later layout change spends without noticing. Flips: dropping `PAD` to 6 fails
the horizontal assertion, growing the knob's outer stroke radius to 8.0 fails the vertical one, both
predicted correctly.

⚠️ **A first draft asserted constants against constants and clippy reported it under
`assertions_on_constants`, correctly.** It recomputed the knob's reach as a literal and compared it
to `TRACK_H + 6.0` and `PAD` — restating arithmetic rather than measuring the drawing, so it would
have passed against any `slider_knob` at all. The ink is read out of the frame now, which is
`ui.rs`'s own slider test's method and the reason that one has teeth.

⚠️ **`ui::SLIDER_H`'s own doc overstated its reach and is corrected in both copies.** It said the
constant is *"the number every caller reserves"*; **no production code outside `ui.rs` reads it.**
`slider` reserves it on its callers' behalf, which is a different claim and the true one — and the
difference matters, because the first version is the sentence somebody packs a row against.

*(**D673 amended** — its geometry sentence, and its three §9.2 citations. §9.4's `ui::slider`
paragraph amended: its open ruling is struck, the two sliders are described as bounding different
axes, and its own copy of the *"what every caller reserves"* overstatement is corrected. Nothing
struck from `roadmap.md`, which carries no row on the sliders.)*

**D765 — One release-frame rule for the `Length` fields, and the argument for the divergence cited a
method that does not exist. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-15; Keep — unification of the four copies was
declined, and the reason is recorded.***

`[S6.2-L3-09]`'s standing ruling, and the last of the three divergences that finding measured across
this file's `Length` fields. `optional_length_field` reported a value on **every** frame it held one,
idle frames included, where `length_field` reports on a frame the value **changed** and again on the
frame the drag **ends**. It follows `length_field`'s rule now. ⚠️ **The second half is the one that
cannot be dropped**: the release is the frame `edit_valve` commits on, and it is the one frame a
changed-only field has nothing to say, `value_field` having already settled the number on every
dragged frame — which is §15 **D109**'s shape, so a plain `shown != before` withholds the value on
exactly the frame that owes one.

🚨 **The argument for the divergence cited a method that does not exist.** The doc read *"the shape
`OndinApp::char_length` uses for the other character-scope `Length` fields, and the house rule for
anything that ends at a valve"*. There is no `char_length` anywhere in the tree — the function is
`OndinApp::length_char_field` — and **the link reference under that doc redirected the name to the
`OndinApp` *type***, so `cargo doc` resolved it and the invented method never surfaced.
***A citation that resolves to the wrong item is worse than one that dangles***, because a dangling
one is a gate away from being found and this one had passed every gate for months while being the
whole of the argument the finding was filed about.

⚠️ **The two `char_valve` callers are not a third answer, and the finding's *"three functions give
three answers"* framing is corrected.** `length_char_field` and `type_line_height_field` hand
`char_valve` a value unconditionally because that function takes a `CharAttr` rather than an
`Option` — and `char_valve`'s own comment records **D109 being caused by a guard in exactly that
position**. That is a different **contract**, not a different opinion, and reading it as a third
opinion is what makes the family look more inconsistent than it is. ⚠️ **And there are four copies of
this control, not three**: `type_line_height_field` is a fourth, which `[S6.2-L1-01]`'s own index row
already counted — **so the review's two findings about this family disagreed with each other.**

**Unification was declined, deliberately.** The finding's cost argument is spent: `[S6.2-L1-01]`,
`[S6.2-L1-03]` and the `%`-cap root cause `[S6.3-L1-03]` all landed separately, so what a merged
helper would buy is no longer the three bugs it was proposed against. And the merge is not small —
about twelve parameters across functions that genuinely differ, the sharpest difference being that
`type_line_height_field`'s `auto` face shows a **resolved px value** where the others show a
placeholder, which wants a formatter strategy rather than a flag.

**Test** `a_decoration_field_reports_on_a_change_and_on_the_release_and_not_when_idle`.
🚨 **The idle frame is the load-bearing assertion and the other two are not.** Release and changed
frames report under *either* rule — the old every-frame gate is a **superset** of the new one — so a
test that drove a scrub and stopped there is green for both, which is the vacuous shape
`CLAUDE.md`'s *"what would also pass this"* rule is about. The frame that tells them apart is a
settled one with the value untouched. Both flips bite where predicted: restoring
`current.is_some().then(…)` fails at the idle assertion, dropping the `|| resp.drag_stopped()` term
fails at the release one.

**Also, and found while reading the three fields rather than by the finding: they had no hover text
at all.** `length_field` gives the argument for having one in as many words — *"the field is labelled
by a 14pt glyph and nothing else, so the tooltip is the whole of what says which number this is"* —
and `length_char_field` wears the same argument at three fields and had the tooltip at none of them,
while the unit chip beside them had its own text the whole time. Two of the three, word spacing and
baseline shift, sit **side by side in one row** behind two icons a reader has to already know. They
have one now.

⚠️ **D359 carries a copy of the phantom name and is corrected too.** Its *"four call sites, not the
two the fields are named for"* paragraph names `OndinApp::char_length` as one of them. It was found
by grepping the **phrase** rather than re-reading the list of sites already fixed, which is
`CLAUDE.md`'s own *a list of the places you corrected is not a sweep* arriving one entry later.

*(§9.4's `Length`-field passage gains the shared release-frame rule and the tooltip; nothing struck
from `roadmap.md`, which carries no row on this family. Closes `[S6.2-L3-09]`.)*

**D764 — `selection_handles` walked the same subtree twice in one call. *Fixed and tested
2026-09-15; Keep — and D741's "there is no single caller to hoist" was false.***

This is Decision A of `[S4.1-L4-08]`'s options, and **it needed no cache, no new map on `Resolved`
and no autopan ruling**, because the doubling was *inside* one function. `selection_handles` asks
`self.session.preview_local_box(*id)` for its own `box_` and then asked
`self.session.preview_pivot(*id)` — which asks `preview_local_box(*id)` **again**, for the box that
is on the line above it. And `previewed_pivot` answers `Some` for any node that exists, so the `?` in
`preview_pivot` never short-circuits ahead of the second walk: **it always happened.** Four
production call sites, two walks each, which is **eight of the fourteen `query::local_box` asks a
frame** that §15 D741 counted. `canvas::origin_fields` had the same shape one function away and is
fixed too.

`EditorSession::preview_pivot_in(id, box_)` is the new spelling, and `preview_pivot` is written in
terms of it. ⚠️ **Passing the box in is not an optimisation shortcut, it is the honest signature** —
the pivot is a fraction *of* a box — and writing the convenience in terms of it is what stops the two
disagreeing about what `pivot_point` is applied to.

🚨 **D741 says the fourteen asks are *"fourteen different functions across four files … there is no
single caller to hoist"*, and that is false. It is amended.** ⚠️ **The arithmetic had said so all
along, in two findings that each held half of it**: `[S12.1-L4-03]` measured **0.6431 ms** per
selection-box build and `[S4.1-L4-08]` measured **0.3490 ms** per `local_box` call — a factor of
**1.84**. ***Two findings measured the same work and neither divided.*** That is worth more than the
saving: a ratio between two numbers in two documents is a thing no gate, census or test can notice,
and the only reader who can is somebody holding both.

**Test** `session::tests::the_two_pivot_spellings_agree_and_preview_pivot_always_walked`. The first
assertion is that the two spellings answer alike, or the eight asks removed were not the same work;
**the second is the one that matters**, and says the duplication was *unconditional* rather than
occasional, by asserting `previewed_pivot` answers `Some` for a node that exists. ⚠️ **The saving
itself is established by reading the call site and the test says so** — flipping `preview_pivot_in`
to ignore its argument and walk for itself keeps the first assertion green, because it is the same
box.

⚠️ **Two further D741 claims are corrected while there, and both are the same kind of error.** It
calls `assert_resolved_matches_rebuild` a comparison *"field by field through the public API"*: it
compares **four of six** maps — `world`, `world_bounds`, `ink_bounds`, `text` — where `boolean` has
only a fixed-fixture differential over four named nodes and **`inner_ink` is compared by nothing
anywhere in the workspace**. And its *"a fourth map on `Resolved`"* collides with D510's and
`roadmap.md`'s *"a fifth map"* for the rounded-outline cache: **`Resolved` holds six maps today**
— `world`, `world_bounds`, `ink_bounds`, `inner_ink`, `text`, `boolean` — so those two would be the
seventh and eighth, and as written the two documents read as describing one slot. **Both ordinals are
deleted rather than corrected**, because a count in prose is a gate nobody built and the next map
added makes any number here wrong again.

⚠️ **`[S4.1-L4-08]` stays open, and what is gone is only the claim that there was no cheaper
interim.** The map is still a real question for the other six asks, and for the **preview door**:
`session::preview_local_box` re-walks the children itself whenever an override is live — in another
crate, on the frames of a live gesture, which are the frames the handles are moving — and there is no
differential of any kind against it. ⚠️ **`[S12.1-L4-03]`'s `multi` row also survives this**:
`selection_frame_extent` loops the selection and `local_box` returns O(1) per leaf, so a local-box
map buys that row nothing, which the finding's own body already says.

*(**D741 amended** in three places. §5.10's `bounds`/`local_box` bullet amended, which carried both
the no-hoist claim and the ordinal; `roadmap.md`'s rounded-outline row keeps its reading and loses
its ordinal, that row being D510's open half and **not** closed by this. Nothing else struck.)*

**D763 — The `K` in `K × ~5.7 ms` had never been observed, and for a *nested* document it is the
nesting depth. *Measured and recorded 2026-09-15; `[S11.2-L4-05]` stays open, with its severity now
