payload wide, re-introducing the cast **does not compile**: rustc rejects the `match`'s `other` arm,
handing a `u32` to a variant that wants a `u64`, and names the line. That is the only mechanical
objection anywhere in this workspace to half of the old shape, and it exists only because the error
type moved. **Widening the payload is not tidying; it is the check.**

`tests/io.rs · load_rejects_a_schema_version_wider_than_u32_without_truncating_it` runs one row per
measured header and asserts **the number inside the error**, not the variant: `UnsupportedVersion(_)`
alone is satisfied by a comparison that is widened and a payload that is re-narrowed, which is
exactly the half of this fix a later reader is likeliest to undo. ⚠️ **`load_rejects_future_version`
(9999) is deliberately left alone** — 9999 fits a `u32`, so it was green before this change and says
nothing about it.

⚠️ **The flip is the shipped code before this entry, not a deletion** — the cast put back on the read
and both comparisons narrowed, with the payload widened again at the two `Err` sites so it still
compiles. Red on the 2³³ row. **The predicted failure site was wrong**: it is the `Ok` arm and not
the `assert_eq!`, because that header does not merely get reported under a number the file never
claimed, it **opens the file**, so the loop never reaches a comparison at all. The row that fails on
the *number* is `u64::MAX`, and it never runs, the first row having already panicked.

*(§5.11 gains a bullet for the comparison's denomination. Nothing struck from `roadmap.md`.)*

**D637 — Four sentences that describe something the code does not do, and one dead line that is
holding two items alive. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; **Resolved 2026-09-19** — five Low findings in
one pass, four of them prose and the fifth a deliberate stop the maintainer has since ruled on.***

Four of the five are one defect, and it is the one nothing in this project can gate: **a sentence
that describes something the code does not do.** A return value's doc, a condition's doc, a sweep's
count, and a twin with no doc at all. `cargo doc` resolves links, clippy reads code, the tests assert
outcomes, and a sentence that is merely *false* passes all three — so the only detector this project
has for them is somebody reading the sentence against the thing it describes, which is what a review
pass is and is why the Low tail is not tidying. The fifth is what happens when one of the four is
fixed properly: the sentence comes off and the line under it turns out to be holding something up.

**`preview_slot` now answers the question its own doc asks.** Its second line has always read
*"Returns whether it had anything to preview"*, and only the character-scoped route computed it —
`write_char_slot`'s `Preview` verb genuinely answers `false` when no session owns the range, which is
the case the sentence was written about (§15 D129, D155). Every other slot fell through to a bare
`true`. **The consumer is written as though it were not**: `picker::pointer_slot` spells the press
arm `if resp.is_pointer_button_down_on() && !resp.dragged() && self.preview_slot(…) {
note_live_edit(true); return; }` and falls through to `valve_slot` otherwise, so the `else` was
unreachable and a press whose write had been **refused** armed the selection-chrome retreat (§15
D128) as though the colour on screen had changed. `!tx.0.is_empty()` now, which is the answer the
transaction already holds. ⚠️ **`slot_transaction` refuses far more often than the finding's summary
suggests** — thirteen explicit `Transaction(Vec::new())` returns, before the arms that merely collect
nothing: no `display_node`, an index past the end of either paint list *or* of either shared list,
`Canvas` and `Guide` and `Effect` and `Grid` handed a brush with no stop, `GroupColor` handed a
gradient, `GroupGradient` whose `PaintAt` no longer holds paint, an `Effect(i)` retyped out from
under the picker, and the two character slots that never arrive here at all.

`inspector::paint_write_tests::previewing_a_slot_that_has_nothing_to_write_says_so` pins it with
**the same slot at two indices** — `Fill(0)` on a layer that has one fill, `Fill(9)` on the same
layer — which is the cheapest reachable pair; two different *kinds* of slot would be asserting
something about `slot_transaction`'s arms instead. Flip-checked with the bare `true` put back: red at
the second assertion and green at the first, which is what says the first is not a copy of it.

**`interacting`'s doc named the condition its subject was superseded by.** It read *"The same set of
responses `OndinApp::edit_valve` acts on"*, and the expression under it — `dragged() ||
drag_stopped() || lost_focus() || changed()` — is D316's **superseded** commit condition quoted
verbatim. `edit_valve` asks whether the control is *engaged*, `dragged() || has_focus()`, and commits
on the falling edge; §9.3 states that supersession in as many words. ⚠️ **The two sets differ on
exactly one state and it is the load-bearing one**: a control that is **focused and idle** is engaged
and is not interacting, so a field gated on this is withheld from the valve on precisely the frames
the latch would be armed. The old sentence made the sites that gate with `if !interacting(…) {
return/continue }` read as belt-and-braces over a valve that already agreed, when the gate is the
only thing deciding the outcome, and made the ones that build with `if interacting(…)` read as
equivalent when they are not. Prose only — the name is right, the expression is right, and this is
the older, wider question that is the correct one for deciding whether to *build* a transaction.
🚨 **The shipped comment says *"eleven call sites, all in this file"* and there are **ten**, three
negative and seven positive; the eleventh site is `canvas.rs`'s inline copy, which is not in this
file and is not a call.** Corrected here rather than in a second pass, because a count in a comment
is exactly the thing this entry is about.

**Two rows survived §15 D386's sweep, and D386 claims completeness.** `stroke_properties` and
`mixed_stroke_properties` both sized the weight field `available_width() - 28.0 * 2.0 - 6.0 * 2.0`,
where `ui::CARD_COL_GAP` is **7** — and the same row's combo arithmetic four lines above reads the
constant. So one row computed its width from three gaps of 7 and handed the field two gaps of 6, and
its last button sat **two points right of every other control in the column**: on a 280pt card the
stroke unit's colour row ran to 285 and its properties row to 287. That is `CARD_COL_GAP`'s own
warning happening — *"spelled **twice per row** and both have to move together … so grep the
constant, not the number"* — and D386's *"Fifteen rows had been written at 6 and twenty-four at 7;
all thirty-nine read the constant now"* is **a counted claim in a live entry that a grep refutes**,
with these two in the very row that entry singles out as having been at 6. Amended there; the sweep
was right about the rule and wrong about the count.

`inspector::stroke_card_geometry_tests::a_stroke_units_two_rows_end_on_the_same_x` asserts a
**relation** rather than a number — every row of one stroke unit ends on the same x — so the card's
width, its padding and the button sizes stay free to change. ⚠️ **It needs each row's *rightmost*
control and not every control**: a row holds a combo, a field and two buttons side by side, so an
ungrouped census reports four different edges and fails for the wrong reason, which is what the first
draft did. Flip-checked with either `6.0` put back: red at the equality with `[265.0, 267.0]` in the
message — the finding's own two points at this fixture's own numbers rather than at its 285/287,
which is the second half of why the assertion is a relation. ⚠️ **And two stale mirrors of the same
literal survive in this file's own test fixtures**, where a sweep of *rows* would not have looked:
`the_settings_popup_fits_four_tabs_and_a_close_button` recomputes `inner - 18.0 - 6.0` against a
production line that reads `inner - 18.0 - ui::CARD_COL_GAP`, and a dash-popover test halves
`menu_inner_w(POPOVER_W, 11.0) - 6.0`. Both are one point *optimistic* — the fixture believes the
control has more room than it has — so neither can fail for the right reason. *Fix with the constant
in both; recorded here rather than swept, because a fixture that mirrors production arithmetic is a
third population D386 never counted.*

**`write_strokes` was `write_fill_list` re-typed, and only the fill half carried the reasoning.**
Eleven lines each, differing in four tokens, and the surviving doc — *"Whole `Fill`s rather than bare
brushes: the panel edits `visible` and the order, and neither survives a round trip through a list of
brushes"* — is the **weaker** half of its own argument, the stroke side having `width`, `sides`,
`dashes`, `align`, `cap` and `join` to lose as well. ⚠️ **And that doc is itself a note about a
*deleted* twin** — *"one of the two had to go"* — sitting one line above the twin that stayed. The
review's seventh instance of this family in this one file, and the first where the copies differ in
**documentation** rather than in code, which is the direction neither the length ranking nor the
neighbour grep can see: two correct functions, each with the doc it deserves, and one of them has
none. One `write_paint_list<P>` now, generic over the `Operation` constructor and the `*_all`
builder, carrying the doc once.

⚠️ **Unified only because D635's item-7 test already asserts both scopes of both lists against each
other** — `[S14.5-L6-05]` asks for that order in as many words, and without it this is a refactor of
two functions neither of which anything ran; the flip still bites through the shared body. ⚠️ **No
`!tx.0.is_empty()` guard, unlike `write_effects`, and the absence is deliberate**: `commit_inner`
drops an empty transaction on its first line, and that guard is not what `[S14.3-L1-04]` wants
either, since a **no-op** transaction is not an empty one. The comparison `strokes_tx` has and
documents is what is missing, and there is now one place to put it for both lists.

🚨 **`delete_points`' last two lines were a truncation followed by an unconditional wipe, and the
line is left in place.** The tail read `self.points.retain_valid(&tools::subpath_lengths(&left));
self.points.clear();` under a comment describing the truncation; `PointSet::clear` unconditionally
empties `points`, `segments` and the id, so the filter — and the allocation built solely to feed it —
has no observable effect. **The cost is the drift and not the cycles**: a reader who deleted the
`clear()` on the strength of that sentence would have shipped `retain_valid`'s behaviour, a *partial*
set carried across a structural edit, which is the silent near-miss that function's own doc exists to
refuse.

**Finding out why the line stays is the result.** Removing it makes `PointSet::retain_valid` and
`tools::subpath_lengths` **production-dead** — clippy says so at once, on the bin target — because
this is their only non-test caller; the remaining callers are two tests and one assertion. So *the
dead call has been the only thing keeping `dead_code` quiet about a pair that doc comments in four
modules cite as the statement of a rule.* Deleting them, moving them behind `#[cfg(test)]` — which
breaks two real intra-doc links in `preview.rs`, on production items where the gate does read them —
or keeping them under an `allow` are three different answers, and the choice was the maintainer's:
`roadmap.md`'s *Now · Path editing* carried it until the ruling below. **What was wrong here was
the sentence, and the sentence is what was fixed.**

🚨 **Ruled 2026-09-19: the `allow`, and the no-effect call goes with it.** Both items carry a narrow
`#[allow(dead_code)]`, and `delete_points`' `retain_valid` / `subpath_lengths` line is **removed** —
it was the misleading thing this entry found, and with the `allow` in place there is no longer a
reason to keep it. `#[cfg(test)]` is the stronger tool and is wrong here: it costs `preview.rs` a
real intra-doc link on a **production** item, which is **D699**'s case rather than **D672**'s, those
two entries bracketing the same attribute from opposite sides. Deleting the pair outright takes out
the statement of a rule that doc comments in four modules cite and two tests assert, and a whole-path
geometry patch is the work that will want them back. ⚠️ **What the `allow` gives up is named on both
items**: nothing now fails if the pair's last *test* caller goes too — `dead_code` has stopped being
the thing that would say so, and these sentences are what is left. `[S12.3-L3-07]` is closed by it,
and the *Now · Path editing* bullet is **struck from `roadmap.md`**; the whole-path-geometry decision
beside it, parked with MCP, is untouched.

⚠️ **Worth generalising, because it is a hole neither of `CLAUDE.md`'s two dead-code paragraphs
covers.** The `pub`-in-core case and the derived-`PartialEq` case are both about the lint failing to
*fire*; this is the lint firing correctly on **a caller that does nothing**, so the item reads as
live to every gate and to every reader. **`dead_code` can be satisfied by a call with no effect**,
and the only thing that distinguishes such a call from a live one is reading what the next line does.

*(§9.3's picker bullet amended: the press arm claims the frame only where there was something to
preview, which is what the `&&` now means. §9.4's paint-write sentence amended: `write_fill_list` is
still the fill door and still carries whole `Fill`s, and it and `write_strokes` are one generic since
this entry. `roadmap.md` gained one bullet under *Now · Path editing* for the `retain_valid` pair and
nothing was struck — none of the five was an item that file was carrying. **That bullet is itself
struck as of 2026-09-19**, the ruling above having spent it.)*

**D636 — Two silences: a folder export that replaces without saying so, and an axis field that names
one run's number. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — two findings under one entry, because they are
the same defect at opposite ends of the app.***

**A control that answers a question it has no answer to**, twice — and in both cases the project
already had the word for the honest answer. The export's word is the status line it was already
writing; the axis field's is `mixed_text`'s dash, which four other fields in its own file were already
using. Neither repair needed a new mechanism, and both silences had shipped for months, because the
honest answer is one clause longer than the confident one and nothing anywhere objects to a control
that sounds sure.

**Half one: the folder export replaced files nobody had been shown.** `export_all` reads
`prefs.export_dir` — *"One folder, not one per document"*, the field's own doc, and set by **any**
previous export including a single-file save dialog's *parent*, since `write_export` stores
`path.parent()` for a `Destination::File`. `export_destination`'s `(Some(dir), _)` arm answers
`Write(dir)` for **both** values of `how`, so the write happens with no dialog at all; and
*Re-export on save* runs the whole thing off a save that succeeded, which since D393 includes an
**autosave landing from a background thread** (`app.rs`'s `Done::Saved`). The `Folder` arm was a bare
`fs::write` per file with no existence check. So: export one PNG into a folder of hand-made assets,
open a different document with a layer called `logo`, and every save of *that* document replaces
`logo.png` in the first folder. **The status line said `Exported 1 file` and named nothing.** What was
documented was the folder-sharing and the autosave trigger, both plainly, in `prefs.rs`; what was
documented nowhere is that the write *replaces* rather than adds, and that the destination is never
shown.

The repair is the finding's own *"cheap honest version"* — one `Path::exists` per file **before** the
write, and the folder on the end of the message: `Exported 4 files (2 replaced) — 1 had no size →
C:\…\assets`. ⚠️ **Only the folder arm gains it, and the asymmetry is the decision.** A *File* or an
*Archive* was named in a save dialog a moment earlier, so the user has been shown the path and warned
by the OS; a folder export can arrive with no dialog at all, which is the feature `export_all`'s own
doc states — *"No dialog when there is somewhere to put it"* — and is exactly what makes the report
the whole of the promise. ⚠️ **The order in the message is decided by `app::status_label`, which
draws it with `.truncate()`**: count first, loss next, path last, so what falls off the end is what
the reader can most afford to lose — *Show in folder* can re-derive a folder, and nothing can
re-derive a replacement count.

🚨 **The flip is red one run earlier than predicted, and that is the whole argument for where the
read sits.** Moving the `path.exists()` call to *after* the write was predicted green on the first
run and red on the second. It is red on the **first**, at `"Exported 1 file (1 replaced)"` for a file
that was not there a moment before: every path exists once `fs::write` has returned, so the count
comes back as the *file* count and the report is wrong from the very first export rather than
drifting into wrongness. That one line is the one a reader could move without noticing, which is why
the test carries a `!contains("replaced")` assertion on the first run at all.

`export_all_scope_tests::a_folder_export_says_what_it_replaced_and_where` writes the same plan into
one directory three times — twice through the folder arm, then once as a *File* — **because the count
is a difference and not a property**: asserting only the second run would pass for a message that
always says "replaced", and only the first for one that never does, while the *File* run is the
control that says the other two arms are unchanged. ⚠️ **The test's own doc calls that *"three runs
into one folder"*, and only two of the three go through the folder arm**; the third is the control,
and the sentence reads as though it were a fourth write.

**Half two: the Axes readout named the first run's number.** `[S6.2-L1-05]` measured `subject.mixed`
called **zero** times across `axes_section`, `features_section` and the row helpers under them, while
`subject.ragged` is called **exactly once** — at the reset slot in `axis_field`, a few lines *below*
the readout it sits beside. So the code asked the raggedness question within one screen of the field
and spent the answer somewhere else. Over a selection whose first word is `wght 300` and whose second
is `wght 800`, the field read **300** with no mark, which is `mixed_text`'s own objection: *"showing
one of the several values reads as a claim that it is **the** value — which the next drag would then
make true for all of them"*. The repair is one call to `mixed_text`. **A consistency repair rather
than a new visual**, which is why it did not need the maintainer.

⚠️ **The slider under it keeps its knob and that is deliberate** — the same fork `multi_number` makes.
A control has to operate from something real while the field beside it says it does not know, and a
knob has nowhere to be that means "mixed"; the drag is relative either way. What the dash buys is
that the *number* stops making a claim.

🚨 **`TypeSubject::partial`'s doc was wrong, and it nearly cost the test its fixture.** It read
*"whether `range` is a sub-range rather than the whole node. **The only case in which a character
control can read mixed.**"*, so a select-all predicted `partial == false` and was written in as the
control. `TypeSubject::read` sets the field from `!sel.is_empty()`: **any** non-empty selection is
partial, a select-all included, and the two states that are *not* are the bare caret and no session
at all. The finding was right and the doc was not — and what caught it is `assert!(one_run.partial)`
on the **fixture** rather than any assertion about the claim. Corrected at the field.

🚨 **The OpenType half is deliberately left, and the reason is the difference between the two
sections.** A *number* already had a mixed spelling in this panel; a **switch** does not, and
inventing a third knob state is a visual decision rather than a consistency repair — `ui::switch_row`
and `ui::paint_switch` both take `on: bool` and would have to grow it. Over a mixed selection every
switch draws **off**, because `set` resolves at the range's start, so a selection half of which has
`tnum` on reads as a column of dead switches. Named at `features_section` and left. Its **write** half
is a separate ruling and stays one: a toggle over a disagreeing range writes `set.clone()` — the first
run's whole list — plus the change, over the entire selection, so the other runs' features are
dropped.

⚠️ **Both halves were ruled on and closed on 2026-09-10 — D752**, and the ruling on the readout is
the one this paragraph could not have guessed: **not a third knob state, but the word**. The
maintainer refused the knob for the reason above stated as a picture — *"a three way switch would be
visually weird (thumb in the middle?)"* — and `ui::switch_row_mixed` paints "Mixed" where the switch
would be, which is D130's rule rather than the new visual this paragraph priced. **So the split it
draws between a *consistency repair* and a *visual decision* held, and the answer landed on the
consistency side after all.** The write half is *"only the tag you named"*, through `Spans::runs_of`
and `TextEdit::style_selection_per_run`.

🚨 **And the dash this repair reuses is itself a departure from D130, so widening it is not this
entry's to authorise.** D130 resolved the two live conventions the other way round and says so in
terms: a control says **"Mixed"**, a dash only where five letters will not fit, *"and there are
exactly two: `ui::segment_mixed` … and `ui::Swatch::Mixed`"*. §9.4 repeats that pair. The Type panel
keeps neither — `typography::mixed_text` paints `–` into a `DragValue`'s digits at four call sites
before this change (the Size field, the list *Level* field, `length_char_field`'s three character
lengths and `length_field`'s five paragraph ones) and the line-height field carries its own copy of
the same formatter, while `inspector.rs`'s numeric fields spell the word at three. **This change adds
a fifth caller and answers nothing.** Whether a 74pt field behind a two-letter prefix is *"too small
to hold five letters"* is precisely the size question D130 leaves to be asked, and it has not been
asked here; the consistency this repair was for is the *panel's*, which is real, and the app-wide
rule it is measured against says something else. **Recorded rather than resolved, and not a
precedent** — *Fix by asking that size question once, then amending either D130's "exactly two" or
the panel; do not cite this entry as the argument for a sixth dash.*

⚠️ **Two counts in the code comments this change shipped are wrong in the same direction and are
corrected here.** *"Three sibling fields"* — at `features_section`, at `axis_field` and in the test's
doc — is four `mixed_text` call sites serving about ten fields, plus the line-height copy; the
undercount is the same shape as a grep that misses the module owning the function. And
*"`subject.mixed` is asked **zero** times across the whole of `axes_section` and `features_section`"*
is a measurement of the tree **before** this change, written in the present tense two lines above the
call that falsifies it.

*(§7 amended: *"Nothing is silently overwritten"* is a rule about names inside one **plan** — which is
why it sits in the bullet that opens *"Nothing here touches the filesystem"* — and it read as a rule
about the disk. §9.4's mixed-spelling paragraph gains one ⚠️ naming the panel that does not keep it,
with the rule itself untouched and D130 not amended, per the paragraph above. Nothing struck from
`roadmap.md`: its Type-panel bullet named `list_section`'s gutter default, `wrap_section`'s gate and
`write_axis`'s `clear_at_default` (all three closed since, D804), none of which this reaches — the new test asserts galleys and
writes nothing — and the letter-spacing *Mixed* bullet is the structural-comparison question, which
is a different one.)*

**D635 — The other five of `[S14.5-L6-05]`, and the one of the ten that was never a decision.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — five tests, four of which close an item and the fifth of which
closes a claim.***

D634 closed items 3, 5, 6, 9 and 10 and recorded the remaining five as belonging in **one** change,
because they are *"`&mut self` write paths"* wanting D269's lift. 🚨 **That was wrong twice over and
writing the tests is what says so.** Item 4 is `slot_transaction`, which has been `&self` returning a
`Transaction` all along; item 8 is `template_cell`, a **free function** over a `&mut egui::Ui` with no
`self` anywhere near it. The three that genuinely are `&mut self` — `write_slot`,
`retarget_mixed_paint` and `write_fill_list` — are reachable on a headless app with a `selection.set`,
and needed no seam cut for them either. This is D630's *"check whether the seam is already there
before cutting one"* a second time in the same file in the same week, and what the mistake cost was a
paragraph in §15 telling the next reader five findings were blocked when none of them was.

**Item 4's two rules pull in opposite directions, and a test of either alone misses the other.** D340
is the widening: the Effects card takes a selection without a slot of its own, so `PaintSlot::Effect(i)`
writes a shadow's colour to **every** selected layer. The repair `[S14.5-L1-01]` earned is that each
subject's list is read **from that subject** rather than cloned from the anchor, because the second
door is the detached picker, which outlives the card. One fixture holds both: layer A with one drop
shadow, layer B with a shadow **plus** a layer blur, both selected. A write that fails to widen leaves
B's shadow alone; a write that clones the anchor's stack takes B's blur with it, which is that
finding's measured data loss reproduced from the write side. Both flips are red at their own
assertion. ⚠️ **The citation the code carries for the second half is `D476`, which was one of the two
numbers reserved and cited from `crates/` with no entry here** — a reader following it landed nowhere,
and between this entry and D553 the argument was the only place it lived. **D476 has an entry since
2026-09-19**, reconstructed from its citation sites and this passage among them; it is the one to read
for the repair itself.

⚠️ **The third case in that test is about `anchor_ok` and not the `filter_map` beside it**, which is
the fixture's load-bearing detail: the anchor's row is retyped from a shadow into a blur and **B's row
is still a shadow**, so without the guard the transaction comes back with one operation rather than
none. A fixture that had retyped both layers would be green with the guard deleted and would look
exactly as convincing.

**Item 1 is the click door, and it says something about coverage that a covered helper cannot.**
`retarget_mixed_paint` has its own test now (item 2's) — and with it green, deleting `retarget_after`'s
`SelectionAll` branch left the whole workspace green. *A tested helper says nothing about whether
anybody calls it.* So this one is driven end to end through `write_slot`, the door D580 enumerates as
the picker's ordinary press plus the kind tabs, four places in the stop bar and the hex field, rather
than at the helper. ⚠️ **Two flips, and they are the pair D580 was for**: the `SelectionAll` branch
removed is red **here alone**, with D580's `frame_fill_tests::a_click_over_a_group_colors_row_takes_the_picker_with_it`
green, which is what says the two arms are separately pinned now; `write_slot`'s whole `retarget_after`
call removed is red at **both**, which is what says neither arm has quietly acquired a route of its
own.

**Item 7's two scopes are asserted against each other, which is the point of one test rather than
two.** The finding handed `write_fill_list`'s `Selection` arm `&[]` — a bulk fill write reaching
nobody — and the workspace stayed green. A `Node` write that quietly fanned out and a `Selection`
write that quietly did not each satisfy half the contract, and neither is visible from its own side.
`write_strokes` is the same function re-typed (`[S14.5-L3-07]`), so both are asserted here rather than
one standing in for the other, which is that finding's whole point. Four flips, one per arm: the two
`Selection` arms handed `&[]`, and the two `Node` arms pointed at the selection's first member instead
of `id`.

**Item 8 is `TEMPLATE_BOX_MIN` — four sentences of measured argument with nothing checking them**, the
finding having removed **both** `.max` calls with the workspace green. A 40 : 1 strip fits the 20 × 28
slot at 20 × 0.5 and a 1 : 40 tower at 0.7 × 28; both come back at the 5pt floor, with a 16 : 9
template at 20 × 11.25 as the control that needs no floor at all and stops *"clamped"* being satisfied
by a cell that draws the same box for everything. ⚠️ **Both extremes are there because a floor on one
axis is invisible from the other** — the flip is red at the strip's *height* and green at its width.
⚠️ **The picture is identified by being the only thing painted**: a cell that is neither lit nor
hovered has no ground and no stroke, so its single `rect_filled` *is* the fitted picture, and the
helper asserts that count before reading the size. That is what makes this a measurement rather than a
search through the output, and it is the line to keep if anyone gives a resting cell a ground.

🚨 **Item 2 is a no-op, and finding that out is the result.** The mutation deletes `shown ||` from
`retarget_mixed_paint`'s `if shown || rows == 0`, which the finding describes as *"the picker is
dragged off a row that is still mixed"*. Three fixtures were written for exactly that case and the
flip is **still green**, because `PaintShown::Mixed`'s `list()` returns an empty slice and `rows` is
therefore `0` on precisely the frames `shown` is `true`. The two clauses name two situations and select
one branch. **A flip that stays green after a test is written for the very case it names is a finding
about the code, not about the tests** — D340 reached the same conclusion from the same direction, on a
`+` whose `if mixed { Vec::new() }` was a no-op dressed as a decision — and here the code is right;
what was misleading is the guard's own comment, which reads as two independent cases. Corrected in
place. ⚠️ **The clause is kept rather than simplified**, because it states an intent that `rows` only
happens to imply: if `PaintShown::Mixed` ever carried a row, that is the clause that would still be
right.

🚨 **So a flip list is evidence about coverage only when every one of its mutations actually changes
behaviour, and nothing in the review's method checks that.** This is the second distinct way a flip
list has misled this session. The first is the **expired** flip — D628's item 1, D630's flips 3 and 4,
D633's flip 2, four instances — where the mutation does change behaviour and something written after
the finding was ranked already catches it; a re-run finds those. This one no re-run can find, because
the flip is green before the test and green after it, and the only thing that tells *"nothing reaches
this"* from *"there is nothing here to reach"* is reading the two clauses against each other.

⚠️ **Three fixtures stay on the item-2 test even so**, because the *function's* contract is
three-valued where its guard is two-valued — still mixed, agreed, and nothing at all — so two of the
three take the same branch by arithmetic rather than by design. The middle one is the only assertion
with teeth and is flip-checked separately: removing `p.slot = to` turns it red while the other two stay
green.

*(§9.4's Effects paragraph amended. It carried D340's premise alone — *"`PaintSlot::Effect(i)` writes
to every selected layer, which is sound because the card's subject **is** the selection"* — and said
nothing of the per-subject read the picker door forced, which is the half this test pins and the half
no §15 entry carries. §9.4's mixed-row paragraph is unmoved and was exact already: *"`write_slot` and
`valve_slot` call `retarget_mixed_paint`"*, both of them through `retarget_after` since D580. Nothing
in `roadmap.md` — D634 recorded these five in §15 rather than there, which is where a decided item
belongs.)*

**D634 — Five of the ten decisions `[S14.5-L6-05]` broke, and why the other five belong in one
change. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — four tests, and a fixture that never reached the state
it was named for.***

That finding mutated **ten** documented rules in two batches of five, and `cargo test -p ondin-app`
came back **973 / 0 both times**, against a control run separately that failed at its predicted
assertion carrying the reported symptom in its message. Every one of the ten has a paragraph of doc
saying why it is the way it is. `inspector::slot_decision_tests` closes five of them — items 3, 5, 6,
9 and 10, which are the ones reachable without a driver: three `&self` methods and two arms of a free
function that already had a test module next door.

`align_target`'s `.filter(|k| ids.contains(k))` is item 3, and its own comment spends a paragraph on
it: *"The key has to survive `outermost` to be usable: one nested inside another selected layer is not
an operand of this align at all, and aligning a set to a box **inside** one of its own members reads
as the ancestor jumping for no visible reason."* `crop_seed`'s selection guard is item 5 — *"the whole
of why the slot is a parameter"*, because a seed is a rectangle computed for **one** frame while a
selection write sends one brush to every node in it (§15 D181). `slot_brush`'s `_ => None` is item 6,
the answer that closes a picker left open on a row retyped from a shadow into a blur underneath it;
the out-of-range index is asserted beside it as a third case through a different door — `get(i)`
finding nothing rather than the kind having no colour to give. Items 9 and 10 are `pattern_for`'s
Dashed and Custom arms.

🚨 **`Selection::set_key` ignores an id outside the selection, so the first draft's fixture never
reached the state it was named for.** Its doc gives the reason — the key is one *of* the selection,
and one sitting outside it *"would align the others to a layer the user cannot see is involved"* —
which means the only reachable spelling of *"a key that `outermost` drops"* is a layer selected
**alongside its own ancestor**: in `ids()` and not in `outermost(ids())`. The draft selected a group
and a loose rect and then set the key to a layer inside the group; `set_key` returned without doing
anything, and the test then asserted the union fallback against a selection that had no key at all —
**green, and for the wrong reason.** What caught it was asserting the fixture,
`selection.key() == Some(..)` and `outermost(..).len() == 2`, rather than the claim failing.
`CLAUDE.md`'s third vacuity shape, met again.

⚠️ **Item 10's failure message is more informative than the finding's description of it.** The
finding says a three-number custom list is *"rebuilt from two numbers instead of preserved"*;
measured, `[8, 4, 2]` comes back as **`[8, 4, 4, 4]`** — its first two, padded out by the
`vec![length, spacing, unit, spacing]` arm below it — so the third number is **replaced** rather than
dropped, and the list comes back *longer* than it went in. A test asserting only that the list is no
longer two numbers would be green on it.

⚠️ **Items 9 and 10 answer the coverage half of a question D515 answered in shape.** That entry
measured the Dotted arm's `spacing.max(unit)` as the lossy one and left its two siblings alone,
rightly: Dashed floors at `0.0`, which is the edge of the legal domain — `parse_dash_list` refuses
only negatives — and Custom does not clamp at all. **Safe in shape and unpinned in fact are different
statements**, and this test is about the second. Both flips bite: Dashed's two floors raised to `1.0`
turn a legal zero gap into a gap of 1, and `s.dashes.len() > 2` → `> 3` gives the `[8, 4, 4, 4]`
above.

⚠️ **The other five are `&mut self` write paths and the finding's own sketch is right about them** —
they want D269's lift, and `[S14.5-L1-03]`'s fix is that same lift, so they belong in **one** change
rather than in five tests taken around the outside. That is recorded here as the reason they are open
rather than as an omission, which is the distinction between *writable now and unwritten* and
impossible.

🚨 **Corrected the same day at D635, which closed all five without cutting a seam.** Two of the five
are not `&mut self` write paths at all — `slot_transaction` is `&self` returning a `Transaction`, and
`template_cell` is a free function over a `&mut egui::Ui` — and the three that are were reachable on a
headless app with a `selection.set`. **This paragraph is what a wrong shape argument costs**: it told
the next reader five findings were blocked on a refactor when none of them was, and the only thing
that falsified it was somebody trying to write the tests anyway.

*(Neither document changed. §9.2 states which box align works against — the key layer's, the
selection's union or the container's (§15 D113) — and the `outermost` filter is a refinement below the
level the design states; §9.4's dash tab row and D181's selection decline are unmoved. The gap was
coverage throughout.)*

**D633 — What the mixed paint row *says*, and the one guard nothing in this project can read.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — four tests, the fifth flip named, and one flip somebody else had
already closed.***

`[S14.4-L6-05]` broke **five** documented rules at once and `cargo test -p ondin-app` came back
**974 / 0**, against a control flip that bit at its predicted assertion; sixteen functions in that
range had no test caller anywhere in the workspace. `inspector::mixed_spread_tests` has four tests,
one per testable rule.

**Four of the five are `&self` methods over the selection, and saying so is half the point.** The
finding's own sketch reaches for *"one driver test over `mixed_paint_row`"* — pointer events at swept
coordinates, several frames, the whole instrument D632 needed. What these four rules want is a
headless app and a `selection.set`: no `Ui`, no events, no sweep. **A driver is what the row's
*buttons* need and not what its *reports* need**, and the two halves of one function do not have to be
tested the same way.

`mixed_visible` reads `any`, not `all`, and all three states are asserted because the finding's flip —
`!= Some(false)` → `== Some(true)` — is **green at both agreeing cases** and red only at the
disagreeing one; the two spellings differ on exactly the input nobody types into a test by reflex.
`mixed_row` compares the alpha **as a byte**, the precision the hex field and the save format both
work in, so the fixture is `0.5` against `0.5 + 1/2048` — distinct `f32`s that both round to 128 —
with a real difference beside it as the control. `image_pixels` declines over a selection (§15 D181),
with the `Fill(0)` row as the control, because *"declines"* is otherwise satisfied by a function that
always answers `None`.

🚨 **The `Spread::bare` test closes a flip that was already closed, and nothing anywhere said so.**
Flip 2 is `spread.bare |= fills.is_empty()` deleted, and **D607**'s
`a_layer_with_no_fill_disagrees_with_every_colour` records that exact mutation as run and red at its
third assertion — written for a different finding, in a module four hundred lines above. So the
finding's *"five at once, 974 / 0"* is a measurement of a tree that no longer holds for one of the
five. **That is the fourth time this session**, after D628's flip 1 and D630's flips 3 and 4, and the
reason the test is kept anyway is that it pins a different consumer: D607 asserts the *spread*, this
asserts what the **row** reports, `mixed_row`'s `brush` flag. ⚠️ Both halves are asserted here for
`[S14.4-L3-06]`'s reason — the rule is written twice, in `shown_over_fills` and in
`shown_over_strokes`, and the fill flip leaves every stroke assertion in the workspace green.

🚨 **The fifth is a *message* guard, and this project has no instrument that can read one.** Flip 3
drops `!locked_layer` from `paint_row`'s `let door = …`, and the finding is right that only the
promise changes: the click arm reads `picture`, and the entry at `inspector.rs:7782` re-tests
`row_edits_the_mode_s_picture` and **not** the lock, `begin_image_edit` refusing on its own. So
`door`'s whole remaining job is choosing an `on_hover_text` string — **and a tooltip's ink never
reaches `FullOutput`**: `on_hover_text` defers an `Area` whose galley is absent however many frames
are pumped, measured with time past the 0.5 s delay. The assertion would have to be one step back on a
`Response`, which says nothing about *which* sentence. This is `[S14.2-L6-05]`'s shape from session 14
— redundant for correctness, load-bearing for the message — and the same answer applies: **an
`is_err()`-style test cannot tell a message guard from a dead one.** The other half of the same `let`,
`row_edits_the_mode_s_picture`, has its own module and is pinned.

⚠️ **`door` has two readers and only one of them can change, which the note at the module does not
say.** The chip's chain tests `else if picture && locked_layer` **before** `else if door`, so on a
locked layer it reaches the lock sentence whatever `door` holds and the flip moves nothing there at
all. The one site that changes is the *Image* label at `:7594`, whose chain tests `door` **first**, so
a locked layer would be told *"Edit this picture"* instead of *"This layer is locked"*. **The guard is
redundant twice over at the chip and load-bearing at exactly one site**, and the arm order is what
carries the guarantee at the chip — worth knowing before anyone reorders either chain.

*(Neither document changed, and both rules the first two tests pin were already in §9.4 with nothing
checking them: *"Its eye reads whether **any** paint in scope is on rather than all of them"*, and the
stand-in row being `paint_row` *"told only which of its two values it may not state"*, where an
unpainted target among painted ones counts as disagreement (§5.7a).)*

**D632 — The mixed paint row's two verbs, and the alignment dropdown that needed the popup driven.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — the last two of `[S14.3-L6-05]`'s six flips, and with them the
whole finding.***

D630 pinned four of that finding's six and named the other two as needing a click driven at a swept
coordinate rather than a lift. These are those two. `mixed_paint_row`'s `out.remove` arm is what its
own doc calls *"the one destructive act on the row and the deliberate one"* and *"the only way back to
an empty panel"* — §9.4 says the same, *"the row's `x` is therefore the only destructive control on
it, and deliberately so"* — and it had no assertion of any kind. Nor did the eye beside it, whose
`any`-not-`all` rule §9.4 states in the same paragraph. `mixed_stroke_properties`' `picked` commit is
the alignment dropdown, and it is the one flip of the six that needed the **popup** driven rather than
a function called, because `picked` is set inside `ComboBox::show_ui`'s closure.

⚠️ **The `x` and the eye are asserted in one test on purpose, and the reason is arithmetic.** The
sweep `mixed_opacity_tests` already carried for D465 gives, in a 320-wide row, the opacity field at
x = 200…255, the `x` at 260…285 and the eye at 290…315 — **five points apart** — so a test of one that
silently hit the other would be a passing assertion about the wrong button, and its failure would read
as a claim about the code. Running both from one fixture is what says the aim is right. The eye is
clicked **first**, because the `x` takes the fills the eye needs to be asserted on. A reader splitting
this into two tests loses the only thing that tells the two buttons apart.

⚠️ **The `x` drops the picker too, and that is the half no document assertion can see.** A picker left
on `SelectionAll(Fill)` after the fills have gone is editing nothing, so `self.picker.is_none()` is
asserted beside the two empty fill lists. Both verbs commit through `commit_edit`, so both are
asserted at **one** undo step rather than one per layer.

⚠️ **The dropdown's coordinates came out of a throwaway probe and are written down at the test so the
next one does not need one.** In a 320-wide row at `screen_rect` (0,0)–(320,600) a click at (60, 14)
opens the combo, and the popup's three rows then draw their labels at y = 38.5, 66.5 and 94.5, x = 15.
**The popup appears on the frame after the release**, so the second click cannot land before the
fourth frame. That is the expensive half of this instrument and the half that does not survive in
anybody's head.

🚨 **`Mixed` is asserted absent from the list, and §9.4 had been asserting it with nothing to check
it.** The design says *"the position dropdown shows 'Mixed' as its selected text but **never lists it
as an option** — it is a report, not a value, so offering it would be offering a no-op"*, and the loop
says the same in place. The popup's contents are asserted **exactly** — three rows, `Centre`, `Inside`
and `Outside` — so a fourth added later fails here rather than shipping.

⚠️ **The dropdown test carries a control for its own aim**: the same click at y = 100 with the popup
shut writes nothing, so a first click that missed the combo cannot pass the test above by landing on
something else. Flip-checked by neutering the `if let Some(a) = picked` commit — red at the first
assertion, both strokes left as the fixture made them — and the two verbs flip-checked separately,
each red at its own assertion and green at the other's.

*(Neither document changed. §9.4 describes the mixed stroke row, its two inert controls, the row's `x`
and its eye exactly as they behave, and `roadmap.md` holds nothing this closes.)*

**D631 — `remap_slots` had a third copy three thousand lines above it, and its own doc said there
were two. *Fixed 2026-09-09; Keep — the duplicate is gone and the rule the helper states is now
true.***

`inspector::remap_paint_indices` carried `remap_slots`' entire body **verbatim, comment for
comment** — the picker's drop-or-move, the hex buffer's other-node guard, and both of the comments
arguing them: *"Read, then written, because both halves want `self` and the picker may have to be
dropped rather than moved"* and *"A buffer hanging off another node is not in this list at all."*
`remap_slots` was extracted **later**, for the effect and grid lists, and its own doc read *"What
both of those do"* and *"One function taking the mapper rather than two copies of this body, because
… the half that is easy to get wrong is the picker's drop-or-move, which is the half they share"* —
while the copy it was describing sat three thousand lines above it, written first and so never
converted when the extraction happened. Found while writing D630's tests, which needed an anchor
unique enough to flip.

`remap_paint_indices` calls `remap_slots` now, and its doc is corrected to **three** callers with a
⚠️ saying what it used to claim. The stroke half — the options popup, the open sides rows and the
dash buffer — stays where it is, because that is the part no other caller has and it does not go
through the mapper the shared body takes. **The flip still bites through the shared body**: dropping
`.filter(|p| p.node == anchor)` turns D630's
`paint_chrome_belonging_to_another_layer_is_left_where_it_is` red, which is what says the refactor
kept the behaviour under test rather than merely compiling.

🚨 **A rule stated in the place that keeps it says nothing about the place that does not.** That is
the whole finding, and it is worth an entry because this file states the same rule twice more and
both statements were equally unable to see this: `paint_unit`'s *"One function rather than two call
sites because they have already drifted"* and `PaintScope`'s *"The Fill and Stroke panels are one
implementation, not two."* The review found three further duplicate pairs in this same module
(`[S14.1-L3-06]`, `[S14.2-L3-08]`, `[S14.3-L3-07]`), and **this is the first of them where the
deduplicated helper already existed** — so the ordinary reading of a duplicate, *nobody has got
round to factoring it out*, was false here and the factored-out version was one search away.

⚠️ **Nothing in this project can detect it.** `cargo doc` is happy, the length ranking measures a
run against the item beneath it and both runs described their own function correctly, and the
neighbour grep asks whether an item *lost* its comment — where here nothing lost anything. Two
correct functions that happen to be the same function is the shape all three detectors are blind to,
which is the same hole `CLAUDE.md` records for a *duplicated* doc comment, arrived at from the code
side.

*(Neither document changed. §9.4 names `inspector::remap_paint_indices` as what carries the five
index-keyed pieces of chrome across a reorder or a removal, and that is still exactly what it does —
the entry point, the five pieces and the `paint::reordered_index` / `paint::removed_index` mappers
are all unmoved. What changed is which function holds the shared half, which is below the level the
design states.)*

**D630 — The paint panels' write half, and a readout nothing could see.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — four of the finding's six flips are pinned, and two of the four
were pinned by somebody else.***

`[S14.3-L6-05]` measured nineteen functions under `inspector_paint_panels` with one production call
site each and **no test caller anywhere in the workspace** — the single exception, `inspector_stroke`,
being reached by a test that measures the card's *height*. It then broke **six documented decisions
at once** and ran the whole `ondin-app` suite green against a control that bit, so the absence was
coverage rather than a dead harness. Four tests close the testable core of it: `strokes_tx`' equality
guard, the reorder/removal remap in both directions, the other-layer guard beside it, and the mixed
corner-radius readout.

**Neither of the two needed the lift the finding's sketch proposed, and saying so is half the point.**
`strokes_tx` is already `&self` and returns a `Transaction`. `remap_paint_indices` is `&mut self`
only in that it reads and writes five fields on `OndinApp`, every one of them `pub(crate)` — so a
headless app with those fields set is the whole fixture, and lifting the `moved` closure would have
moved code to make testable something that already was. D269's move is the right instrument often
enough that reaching for it is the reflex; **check whether the seam is already there before cutting
one.**

🚨 **Two of the four flips were closed by tests written after the finding was ranked, and neither
leaves a row anywhere.** Flip 4, `pattern_for`'s `spacing.max(unit)`, is caught by **D515**'s
`dash_list_tests::a_dotted_spacing_under_the_stroke_width_survives_a_mode_round_trip` — re-run to
confirm rather than reasoned. Flip 3, `largest(corners)` → `0.0`, is red **twice**: at the new
readout test, and at **D534**'s own drag control, at `(15,15,15,15)` against `(25,25,25,25)`. The
second is the interesting one — the seed is what a drag *counts from*, so a wrong seed lands ten
short, and D534's control catches this **by arithmetic rather than on purpose**. A finding's flip
list is a claim about the tree at the moment it was ranked, and this round has now hit that three
times.

⚠️ **The readout is a claim about pixels, and that is why nothing saw it.** The existing corner-radius
tests drive the field and read the *document*, and are green whatever the field displays, because a
bare click writes nothing either way. Only a galley can see the number, so the test reads one —
recursively, `FullOutput::shapes` being layer-flattened while its entries are not. ⚠️ And a
prediction is corrected: `largest` → `corners.top_right` was predicted **green**, on the ground that
the first fixture's radius is on the top *left*. It is **red at that very assertion**, because
`top_right` is `0` there; the second fixture puts its radius on `bottom_right`, so no single-corner
spelling satisfies both, which is the reason there are two.

⚠️ **Flips 5 and 6 remain unpinned and the module says so** rather than reading as coverage of the
six: `mixed_paint_row`'s `out.remove` arm and `mixed_stroke_properties`' `picked` commit both need a
click driven at a swept coordinate, which is a fixture rather than a lift. **The `stroke_menu` /
`stroke_sides_open` / `stroke_dash_text` block does not go through `moved` at all** — it calls the
mapper directly — so the finding's own flip 2 leaves those three green and they are asserted against
a second flip of their own. That is the load-bearing detail in the reorder test: a reader
simplifying it to one flip would leave three of the five pieces of chrome unasserted.

*(Neither document changed. §9.4 describes the reorder and removal remap exactly as it behaves, and
the mixed readout's *"largest of the four"* is the panel's own rule rather than a design statement —
the gap was coverage throughout.)*

**D629 — Three of the inspector's four subjects had never been entered by a fixture.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — nine tests through `inspector_ui`, and the finding's central
claim disproved by its own flip.***

`inspector_ui` dispatches to four subjects — selected guides, point editing, one layer, several
layers — and every fixture in the file selected one painted `Rect`, so **three of the four arms were
entered by no test in the module**. Twelve functions had exactly one production call site and no test
caller: the guide panel and its four rows, the free `shared_guide_colour`, the empty-canvas panel and
its ground row, and the point-editing panel with its header, transform and handle rows.
`[S14.1-L6-03]`.

**Driven through `inspector_ui` rather than through the leaf**, which is `a_line_trades_w_and_h…`'s
own argument: the dispatch is itself a decision, and a test that calls `inspector_guide` directly
asserts nothing about whether a selected guide ever reaches it. The two exceptions say why they are
exceptions — `shared_guide_colour` is a free function of one slice, and the stranded-target drop is a
field on `OndinApp` that has to be set before the frame that clears it.

🚨 **The finding calls the `if !interacting(&resp) { continue; }` gate *"the only thing stopping a
bare click committing an undo step"*. Flipped three ways, it is not.** Deleting the gate alone is
**green** at the bare-click test — and **red** at the stranded-target one, because the
`if !resp.dragged()` at the foot of the loop then runs on every idle frame and clears the target the
gate was skipping past. Making `Operation::SetGuidePosition` never a no-op in `changes_nothing`
(**D428**'s absorber, in `ondin-core`) is **also green** alone. **Only both together turn the
bare-click test red**, at 1 against 0. So there are two independent sufficient guards; the gate's
live job today is the **drag target** rather than the commit, and D428's absorber is what makes the
click free. **No single-line flip proves that assertion has teeth**, which is recorded at the test
because the next reader tempted to simplify either guard will flip it, see green, and conclude it is
dead.

⚠️ **Two predictions corrected by running them.** The dispatch flip — moving the guide arm below the
`match` — bites at the *"Guide"* assertion and **not** at the FILL one, because a selected guide comes
with an *empty* layer selection, so the wrong order falls through to the `0 =>` arm and paints the
**canvas** panel rather than a layer's. And `inspector_multi` over an empty selection draws a *full*
inspector — "0 layers", the whole ALIGN row, three `Mixed` fields — not "almost nothing", so only
naming the canvas card tells those two arms apart. Both are the same lesson: **the arm a wrong
dispatch falls into is not the arm you were testing against.**

⚠️ **`remove_all_guides` had no test caller anywhere in the workspace**, while `remove_selected_guides`
— the verb beside it in the same row — has two in `rulers.rs`. They are asserted **against each
other**, because a version that removed only the selection satisfies every assertion either verb
could make on its own.

⚠️ **Two named decisions stay unreached and the module says which.** `points_transform`'s increment
form needs a *selected anchor* before the field is even enabled, which is a second fixture.
`guide_actions`' `remove_all` / `remove` precedence is **not reachable from a pointer at all**: the
two buttons sit side by side in one `horizontal`, and one primary click at one position cannot make
both report `clicked()`, so the ordering is defensive. **An unreachable branch is a finding about the
branch, not about the tests**, and it is worth writing down at the site so the next coverage pass
does not spend an afternoon on it.

*(`roadmap.md` is unchanged by this entry and `architecture.md` too — §9.4 describes the guide
inspector's three cards and the empty inspector's canvas panel exactly as they behave, and the
point-editing takeover with them.)*

**D628 — The multi-selection Transform card's X, Y and angle halves get their first assertions.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Keep — five tests, and two of the finding's three claims about the code
had expired.***

The card had three test callers when `[S14.2-L6-04]` counted, and all three passed `W` or `H` with
`Absolute`. **D519** and **D520** then added the typed and scrubbed paths — again over `W` — plus the
zero-nudge guard over all six fields. What none of them reaches is the *direction* of the X and Y arms
and the whole of `multi_angle_tx`: which axis a move goes along, whether a nudge adds or lands,
whether the skew clamp exists, whether a layer's scale survives a rotation, and where `shared_angle`
stops calling a set `Mixed`. Five tests, every one flip-checked at a named site.

**The X and Y arms decide one thing — which component of the `Vec2` the delta goes in — and nothing
looked.** D520's control asserts the transaction has two ops and not where they put anything, which
is why the finding's flip 2 (the X arm moving the selection *vertically*) was green for the whole
workspace and, re-run, is green still. The Y arm is asserted separately rather than by symmetry:
it is a second literal, and transposing one of them is exactly the slip.

The angle tests take the distinction `multi_angle_tx`'s own doc is mostly about — a set at 0° and 40°
nudged by 5 comes out at 5° and 45°, and the same set given `Absolute(30)` comes out 30°/30° — and
the rebuild it does *not* do: the target is `translate * orientation * scale_non_uniform(split.scale)`,
and dropping the scale factor makes a quarter turn of a 40 × 60 layer measure 20 × 20 instead of
60 × 40.

🚨 **The finding's flip 1 was green for the review and is red today, and only re-running it says so.**
Deleting `multi_angle_tx`'s `unchanged` filter now fails
`multi_valve_tests::a_zero_nudge_builds_no_transaction_at_all` — D520's test, written two sessions
*after* the finding was ranked. **A finding's flip list is a claim about the tree at the moment it was
ranked**, and the cheapest way to find that out is to run it rather than to read it.

🚨 **The finding's sketch (iii) asks for `None` from two layers 0.002° apart, and it is wrong by
twenty-five times.** `shared_angle`'s `const EPS: f64 = 0.000_87` is in **radians** — 0.0498°, which
is what the constant's own doc means by *"half a tenth of a degree"* — so a 0.002° pair is deep
inside the agreement window and answers `Some`. **The units are the trap**: the field is in degrees,
the constant is in radians, and reading `0.000_87` as a degree figure makes 0.002 look like a
comfortable margin. The test brackets the real window at 0.04° (agreeing) and 0.06° (mixed), and it
is recorded here as well as at the test because **the sketch is the thing a later reader re-runs**.

⚠️ **And the `MAX_SKEW` flip's failure message corrected the prediction, which is the quieter finding
of the three.** An unclamped `Absolute(200)` was predicted to lean the layer back past the vertical.
What comes back is `0.349` radians — **20°** — because `Orientation::to_affine` puts the lean through
`tan`, whose period is π, so 200° and 20° are *the same matrix*. The clamp does not prevent a
blow-up; it prevents a layer silently leaning a fifth of the way while the field says 200. **The
failure a guard prevents can be quieter than the guard's doc implies**, and it is the quiet one that
survives review. The clamp is `multi_angle_tx`'s only guard on its input and had had no caller of any
kind; asserted through a round trip, so it also says the clamped matrix survives
`build::local_for_world`.

*(`roadmap.md`'s *Now · Inspector* bullet naming this as the open half of `[S14.2-L6-04]` is struck —
it listed the relative nudge, `shared_angle`'s `Mixed` and the `MAX_SKEW` clamp, and all three are
pinned now. `architecture.md` is unchanged: §9.4's *"dragging rotation or skew nudges relatively …
while typing sets absolutely"* and *"skew clamps to `tools::MAX_SKEW`"* were exact all along, and
were the sentences nothing was checking.)*

**D627 — Invariant 7's GPU verification test reads the pixel it promises.
*Fixed 2026-09-09; Fix — a one-pixel readback, at the CPU test's own tolerance.***

§4's invariant 7 says *"a pin-time verification test asserts a known sRGB fill produces the expected
output pixel **through each backend**"*. Only one did. `ondin-export/tests/png.rs`'s
`color_boundary_produces_expected_pixel` reads a pixel out of the **CPU** backend;
`ondin-render/tests/gpu_device.rs`'s `gpu_renders_fixture_on_device` built the same 220/30/40
fixture, rendered it to an `Rgba8Unorm` target, and asserted `.expect("gpu render should succeed")` —
it never mapped the buffer. A colour or alpha regression in the GPU handoff would not have been
caught. `[A1-L6-05]`.

⚠️ **The module doc's excuse covers the *walk* and not the *handoff*, and every clause of it is
true.** It reads *"pixel-level correctness is covered deterministically by the CPU tests, which share
`scene.rs`"*. The scene walk **is** shared — genuinely one function, and that is the whole point of
invariant 11 — so the sentence is accurate about the thing it names. What it does not name is the
colour path, which is not shared and is precisely where the two backends differ: **D339** records,
measured, that vello's GPU output is **straight** alpha where `vello_cpu`'s `Pixmap` is
**premultiplied**. A solid fill is exactly what pins that axis, and a solid fill is what this test
draws.

🚨 **An excuse that covers the shared half of a seam reads as covering the seam.** That is why this
survived a review pass that was looking for it: nothing in the paragraph is false, and the reader
supplies the leap. It is the same shape as **D622**'s third correction one entry away — a record
that argues a check away — with the difference that this one argues it away by being *true about
something else*.

**The fix is the finding's own prescription**: a one-pixel readback at the centre, asserted to ±2 per
channel — the tolerance `color_boundary_produces_expected_pixel` already uses, because the quantity
under test is *which colour arrived*, not the last bit of a rasterizer's rounding.
`read_centre_pixel` is `gpu_effects.rs`'s `readback` narrowed to one pixel and deliberately **not**
shared with it: that one is built around its own file's `Gpu` harness and its `SIDE` constant, and
threading a loose `device`/`queue` through it would be a refactor of a file this change has no
business touching. ⚠️ What *is* worth copying carefully is the **256-byte row alignment** — it is what
makes a naive `bytes_per_row` read the wrong row, and it is the one part of a readback that is easy
to get wrong and impossible to notice.

⚠️ **Still `#[ignore]`d.** It needs `--ignored` on hardware and the default suite is unchanged, which
is the same trade as before and is why invariant 7 is verified *at pin time* rather than
continuously. What changed is that running it now asserts something.

🚨 **Not flip-checked, and this entry says so rather than leaving it to be assumed.** No GPU adapter
is available on the machine this was written on — the same reason the codebase review's four open
Highs are unverifiable here. The assertion and the tolerance are both taken from tests that already
exist rather than invented, and **the first person to run this on hardware is the flip**. If it is
red on a real adapter, the interesting reading is not that the test is wrong: it is D339's axis, and
the entry to read beside it is that one.

*(Neither `architecture.md` nor `roadmap.md` changed. The invariant's text was correct all along —
it says "through each backend" and means it — and the test was the half not keeping it, which is the
`[A5]` shape of an invariant-enforcing test that no longer enforces.)*

---

**D626 — The export panel's decisions were fused to a dialog and a filesystem write, so none of
them could be observed. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Fix — two lifts, and the writer tested
against a temp folder.***

`panels/export.rs` was the largest genuinely under-covered module in the workspace — `facts.md` §7
puts it at **20.81 % over 1,432 lines** — and **none of the 27 `OndinApp` methods in it had a test
caller anywhere**. ⚠️ **The export walk that *is* tested is the wrong one**: `main.rs`'s
`export_all_runs_the_documents_own_settings` drives `run_export_all`, which **re-implements** the
same walk for the CLI, while `exportable_layers` is the door a user reaches. `[A5-L6-03]` and
`[S8.3-L6-04]`, taken together because they are the lift and the test it made possible, in one pass
over one file.

**The decision that matters most was fused to a dialog.** `export_all`'s own doc states the rule —
*"a modal appearing on `Ctrl+S` because a preference is set is the thing that would make the switch
not worth having"* — and the three-arm table carrying it sat next to
`rfd::FileDialog::pick_folder()`. Collapse the `(None, Quietly)` arm into the `Asking` one, or drop
the `.filter(|d| d.is_dir())` so a folder the user has since deleted falls through, and **every
`Ctrl+S` with the preference on pops a native folder dialog**, with nothing in the workspace
failing.

🚨 **`OndinApp::headless` does not dissolve this, and D303 says so in terms**: *"a headless app makes
the method callable without making the call site observable … this is a door, not a licence."*
**Worse here** — even a headless call would open a *real dialog* and write *real files*, so the
decision could not be observed at all until it was separated from the acting. D269's prescribed
lift, and the fourth time this session has applied it. `export_destination(Option<PathBuf>,
ExportAll) -> ExportRoute { Write | SayNoDestination | AskForFolder }` and `export_dialog(bool,
usize) -> DialogKind { Archive | SaveFile | PickFolder }`; `export_all` and `run_export` become the
callers that act on the answers.

⚠️ **The remembered-folder arm is asserted for both `how` values**, because *whoever asked* is the
arm's actual claim and a table checked one row per input passes against a version that only writes
for `Asking`. The `files.len() == 1` boundary is asserted from both sides, and `zip` at each of
three counts — an archive of one file is still an archive, which is the one place the two tables
disagree and the case a reordered `match` gets wrong.

**Then `write_export`, which needs no dialog at all.** `Destination` is constructed directly, so the
whole `(failed, skipped)` reporting table becomes assertable against a temp folder. Three separate
claims: the bytes reach disk under the planned names; the `skipped` counter reaches the sentence,
which is exactly what `[S8.3-L1-02]` found *missing* for a different loss; and `prefs.export_dir` is
remembered, which is what makes the *next* export silent and is therefore `export_destination`'s own
input. ⚠️ **The empty group is the fixture's point** — export settings and no extent, so
`plan::render` refuses it, and it is the only way to reach the `(None, n)` arm. Two ordinary rects
would assert the `(None, 0)` arm twice and call it coverage.

⚠️ **The flip is sharper than predicted.** Counting the refusal as a success — `rendered.push` with
empty bytes instead of `skipped += 1` — was predicted to fail the *sentence* and fails **two
assertions earlier, on the files**: `["Icon.png", "Nothing.png"]`, 2 against 1. The wrong version
does not merely mis-report; it writes a **zero-byte PNG** for a layer that has nothing in it. *A
miscount here is a file on the user's disk, not a wording.*

🚨 **One cross-reference, because the shape already exists in this codebase and one module has it
while one does not.** `write_export` calls `prefs.save()`, and this test touches no `prefs.json`,
because `OndinApp::headless` sets `Prefs::ephemeral` and `save` reads that flag on its **first
line**, before anything touches the filesystem. **That is exactly the injection point
`library::cache::LocalIndex` still lacks** — D619 records the suite editing the person's own *Recent
searches* for want of it — and `save`'s own comment gives the reason in the words D619 needed: *"the
damage is silent and permanent — the file it writes outlives the test by however long it takes
somebody to notice."* `roadmap.md`'s open bullet now names `Prefs::ephemeral` as the model, which
gives its *"where does the path come from"* question a fourth and cheapest answer.

**What is left is named in the code rather than papered over**: `run_export`'s
`.filter(|d| d.is_dir())` at the `export_all` call site is a filesystem test rather than a decision,
it lives outside the lifted table, and the test says so instead of pretending to reach it.

`architecture.md` is unchanged. §7's *"the destination follows the file count"* and *"no dialog
after the first time"*, and §9.4's Export panel, are exact — nothing about the behaviour moved, only
about what can be observed.

**D625 — The identity row's refusals had no test caller, and the flip that fixed that corrected the
finding. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Fix — asserted on the sentence each refusal gives.***

`inspector::identity_boolean_row` has three production call sites and no test caller; nor do
`group_actions`, `booleanable_selection`, `selected_boolean`, `apply_boolean` or
`flatten_selection`. The one helper beside them that *is* covered, the free `mask_card_targets`, has
a whole module to itself — which is the contrast that makes this a gap rather than a policy, since
the argument for lifting that rule out of the panel was made and won on the card one row below.
Both of the review's flips were **green**. `[S14.2-L6-05]`.

**Asserted on the sentence, not on `is_err()`.** `mask_action`'s own doc says it returns *"a
`Result` rather than an `Option` because every refusal here has a different thing to fix"* — so the
sentences **are** the feature, and a refusal-only test would pass against a version giving one
sentence for all five, which is precisely the defect `[S14.2-L3-06]` records in the boolean dropdown
one row away. ⚠️ **The order is asserted with them**: the same-group test runs before the
boolean-parent one, so a selection failing both must say *"in the same group"*. A version that
reordered them would still refuse and would tell the user to fix the wrong thing. The
two-shapes-in-one-group case is the control that stops all four refusals being satisfied by a
function that refuses everything.

`group_actions` returns a **pair**, and both halves are asserted in every row: a test reading only
`can_group` would pass against a version that had swapped them. Four rows — a lone group, a group
beside a layer, two plain layers, and a lone *shape*, which still groups because the rule is about
containers and not about count.

🚨 **The flip corrects the finding, and this is the entry's most important paragraph.** Disabling
the boolean-parent refusal fails at the predicted site **with a different sentence rather than with
`Ok`**: `left: "These layers cannot be wrapped in a group, so they cannot be masked"`. So
`build::mask`'s dry run at the bottom of `mask_action` **does** refuse a boolean's operands, and the
review's description — *"Use as mask goes live inside a boolean where `Document::governing_mask`
answers `None` and nothing can clip"* — is **wrong**. The control stays disabled either way.

⚠️ **Which makes that refusal earn its place for the reason the function's own doc gives, and only
that reason**: not to prevent the operation, which the builder already does, but to say *which thing
to fix*. **A refusal that is redundant for correctness and load-bearing for the message is a real
thing, and a test that asserts `is_err()` cannot tell it from a dead guard.** A prediction of `Ok`
here was the same mistake in reverse — assuming a guard that exists must be the one doing the work.

⚠️ **The shipped test's own preamble overstates the gap, and it is corrected here rather than
repeated.** It reads *"none of them had a test caller"* and lists `mask_action` and `toggle_mask`
among them; both are called by `releasing_a_mask_releases_every_one_the_card_reports`, fifty lines
above it in the same module, written for D513. The six names above are the ones that check out.

§9.4's mask paragraph is amended. It described the boolean guard as the button being *"stricter than
the operation"*, which is true of `op_set_mask` and reads as though the guard were what prevents the
operation — the reading this flip disproves.

**D624 — Six documented typography decisions were broken at once and the whole suite stayed green.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-09; Fix — three pinned, two of them lifted first, and three named as
still open. **The other three landed in D804**, which is where the queue closes.***

**G9.** **37 of 38** production items in the Type panel's write half had **zero test callers** —
`char_valve`, the panel's central write seam with fifteen occurrences in production, among them; the
one exception is `valve_paragraph`, at a single mention. The review broke **six documented decisions
simultaneously** and ran the whole `ondin-app` suite: **975 passed / 0 failed.** ⚠️ **A control flip
did bite at its predicted assertion** — constant-folding `next_line_height`'s Auto seed fails
`leaving_auto_seeds_the_line_height_the_font_was_giving` — so the harness is live, and the six
greens mean *nothing reaches these decisions* rather than *the flips were harmless*.
`[S6.2-L6-07]`.

**Three of the six are now pinned, and two had to be lifted first** (D269's move). The
`(under, strike)` → cell mapping comes out of `decoration_section` as `decoration_cell` /
`decoration_write`; the `weight >= 600` reading and the 400/700 a click writes come out of
`type_weight_toggles` as `bold_toggle`, returned as a pair because they are one rule read in two
directions. `matches_variant` was already a free function and simply had no caller — its
axis-agreement tolerance `< 0.05` had become `< 1000.0` in the flip, so every variant matched.

🚨 **The decoration pair is the sharpest of the six, and the reason is instructive.**
`decoration_section` is one of the few functions in this file that *does* have a test module —
`skip_ink_tests`, which drives it on a headless app through real frames — and that module exercises
the `under.is_some()` branch and the toggle beside it, never the cell. So **which cell lights was
unpinned even inside the coverage**, which is why a count of tested functions says nothing here.

**What the tests assert, and why that shape.** The decoration test asserts the read and write halves
**against each other**: whatever cell a state lights, picking that cell must produce that state
again. That is what has teeth rather than a table of literals, because *a mapping swapped in both
halves would satisfy a table of expected numbers and still light the wrong glyph*; cell 1's meaning
is pinned to `Underline` by name as well, and the both-at-once case is pinned to underline because
the model can reach it through a paste and the strip has no fourth cell. The bold test asserts at
**599 against 600**, a threshold being wrong only at its ends, and pins the *written* weight beside
the lit state. `matches_variant` is flipped in **both** directions — the tolerance widened, and
narrowed to `== 0.0` — because the second is what says the tolerance is not decoration.

⚠️ **Three of the six remained unreached, and the test module said which rather than letting itself
be read as coverage of the six**: `list_section`'s gutter default, `wrap_section`'s
`!= WrapMode::NoWrap` gate and `write_axis`'s `clear_at_default` all sat inside `&mut self` bodies
that need a live text session and a laid-out panel to enter. That was called a **fixture** rather
than a lift, and offered as the reason they did not travel with the other three. 🚨 **All three are
reached now and that reason was wrong for two of them** (D804): the gutter default and
`clear_at_default` read nothing but their parameters, so what needed the panel was their *callers*,
and both lifted. Only the wrap gate wanted the fixture. ⚠️ **`write_axis`'s guard was the one not to
confuse with a covered one** — `axis_valve` carried the same `clear_at_default` and *was* pinned
(D569), so a grep for the name read as though the decision were reached. **It was the same eight
lines twice**, which is the half this paragraph warned about and did not see; there is one copy now.

⚠️ **And a fixture finding.** The first draft's `find_map` over
`CharAttr::Underline(Option<Decoration>)` yields `Option<Option<_>>`, so the outer `is_some()` meant
*"the attribute was written"* — true of `Underline(None)` too — and asserted nothing. It failed on
**cell 0**, the one arm where the two readings differ, which is this project's *"its fixture never
reached the state"* shape caught by an assertion rather than by reading.

⚠️ **The claim that `architecture.md` states none of the three was wrong, and D804 corrects it**:
§9.4's wrap paragraph states the `NoWrap` gate in full, including the *dimmed and not reset* half and
the boundary the gate stops at. What was true is that the coverage was the whole of the gap.

**D804 — The last three of D624's six are reached, and two of them were a lift after all.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-19; Resolved — the fixture-or-lift split D624 drew was wrong for two of
the three.***

D624 pinned three of the six decisions `[S6.2-L6-07]` broke simultaneously and named the other three
— `list_section`'s gutter default, `wrap_section`'s `!= WrapMode::NoWrap` gate and `write_axis`'s

same breath.** Both arms call the one function now, so one assertion covers both, and there is no

**The wrap gate genuinely needed the fixture and has one.** `wrap_gate_tests` drives the real

constants the other way round and the failure was the honest one — a click on the cell already
current changes nothing, and *"the mode switched"* caught it.

**Three tests, every flip run, and no two of them landing on one assertion.**
`a_default_axis_value_is_dropped_except_on_opsz` carries four assertions because three flips need

🚨 **In `nowrap_kills_word_break_and_long_words_and_nothing_else` the control is the whole test.**
Every `NoWrap` assertion is that a click changed *nothing*, which a section nobody drew and a
coordinate that missed both produce, so the same fixture clicks the Wrap strip itself — the one

🚨 **And a doc-comment theft, committed and repaired inside this change.** Inserting `marker_attrs`
above `agreed_zero` anchored on that `fn` line rather than on the line above its doc block moved all

had run the neighbour grep correctly on every earlier insertion; what caught it was **running that
