clamping would make the file *draw* something it does not *say* — the panel would read 1000 and the
canvas would show the picture at 1. Refusing draws the unadjusted picture, which is the one honest
answer available to a reader that has been handed a number the model forbids.

⚠️ **The operation door was already shut against the other half of this, and the brief said
otherwise.** `op_set_fills` does not *"validate nothing"*: since D452 it asks
`build::image_ref_is_finite`, which weighs the crop rectangle, the tile scale and all seven
adjustment sliders, so a `NaN` exposure never reaches the model at all. That is precisely why both
witnesses above are **finite** — the only values that can still get in are the in-range guard's own.
So this is **D492's class at a third field**: *a number that is finite is not thereby a usable one*,
after `exports` and after `geometry::measurable`'s derived-value case at D495. §3's invariant list
says so now.

New arms on `image::adjust_tests::an_impossible_value_is_refused_at_both_doors` — the test named for
this guard, which had probed `NaN` only — plus in-range controls at −1.0, 1.0 and ±0.5, because a
predicate written `(-1.0..1.0)` or `(0.0..=1.0)` would pass every other assertion in the file and
silently refuse half the sliders the panel can produce. **Both flips bite, including the clamping
one**: reverting to bare `is_finite()` fails at the `exposure: 1000` arm, the predicted site, and
clamping each value through `Adjustment::set` before building fails at the *same* assertion. That is
why the claim is written on `pipeline().is_none()` and on `is_default()` together rather than on a
pixel — a clamping version draws a perfectly good picture that the file does not describe, and only
an assertion about the **refusal** can tell the two apart. §5.5a amended.

**D537 — A zero length keeps its unit across a save. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — the elision
predicate asks about the default, not about the number.***

The **save half** of `[S6.1-L1-03]`, Medium. `Length::is_zero` answers `true` for `Em(0.0)` as
readily as for `Px(0.0)`, and it was the `skip_serializing_if` predicate on all seven optional
lengths in `typography.rs` — `letter_spacing`, `word_spacing` and `baseline_shift` on `TextStyle`,
`spacing`, `indent`, `indent_start` and `indent_end` on `ParagraphStyle`. `Length::default()` is
`Px(0.0)`, so a field holding `Em(0.0)` was **absent from the file** and deserialized as `Px(0.0)`. A
designer who sets the letter-spacing field to `%` and leaves it at 0 reopens the file with the suffix
on `px`. Measured: `Em(0) reload = Px(0.0) unit=Px`.

**Zero is the only value this can go wrong at, and that is what hid it.** `resolve` gives `0.0` for
both variants, so nothing rendered ever disagrees — the unit is unobservable in the drawing and still
observable in the panel. And the producer is a pure model call: `Length::in_unit` maps `Px(0.0)`
straight to `Em(0.0)`, which is exactly what the panel's `px`/`%` suffix toggle calls, so the state
is one click away and leaves no other trace.

**`Length::is_default_zero` is the predicate now** — `matches!(self, Length::Px(v) if *v == 0.0)`, on
all seven sites. It costs four bytes and only where the unit is `Em`; the common case, a field never
touched and sitting at the `Px(0.0)` default, is elided exactly as before, so no existing file grows.
`Length::is_zero` stays: it has two real callers in `ondin-export/src/svg.rs` asking a genuinely
different question.

⚠️ **No schema bump, and this entry says so rather than leaving it to be worked out.** The change
only ever *adds* a key an older reader already understands: the fields are `#[serde(default)]` and
`Em` is not a new variant, so a file written here loads in an older build as `Em(0.0)` and one
written there loads here as `Px(0.0)` — which is what it always meant. It is invisible to
`io::MIGRATIONS`.

⚠️ **The other half of the finding is deliberately left open, and the two halves pull opposite
ways.** A zero-valued `Em` span is still kept by `normalize`, which compares structurally, and so
still reports *Mixed* through `shared_in` for text whose letter spacing is zero everywhere.
Preserving the unit **requires** keeping the span, so making `Em(0.0)` and `Px(0.0)` compare equal
would fix the readout by throwing away the very thing this predicate exists to keep. The readout is a
comparison on the **resolved** value and belongs at the reader; it is left open rather than guessed
at, and `roadmap.md`'s *Now · Text* carries it.

`typography::tests::a_zero_length_keeps_its_unit_across_a_save`, asserting on the **JSON text**
rather than on the round-tripped value, because a value that round-trips says nothing about whether
the key was written — and covering a `ParagraphStyle` field as well, because the predicate is named
seven times across two types and a test pinning only `letter_spacing` would be green against a fix
applied to one of them. Both flips bite: `is_zero` put back on `letter_spacing` fails on the first
assertion, the key absent, which is the predicted site; `is_default_zero` made to return `false`
unconditionally fails on the **control**, which is the assertion that keeps the fix from becoming
"write every field always". §5.4 amended.

**D536 — A `Boolean` belongs on the subtree cull's kind list. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — one
variant added to a `matches!`, and the only kind the list was ever observable for.***

`[S11.1-L4-05]`, Medium. `scene::paint_node`'s `bounds_cover_subtree` binding read
`node.children().is_empty() || node.clip() || matches!(node.kind(), NodeKind::Group | NodeKind::Root)`.
A boolean has children, does not clip, and is neither — so it came out `false` and the `if` below
short-circuited before ever consulting `res.ink_bounds(id)`. **Every boolean in the document was
walked, `paint_shape`d and encoded on every frame, wherever the view was.**

Measured in release against a counting painter, viewport at `(-1000,-1000)..(-500,-500)` and the
containers parked at x ≥ 10,000: 800 booleans issued **801** fills at **0.106 ms** of walk alone,
where 800 groups issued **1** at 0.0116 ms. The 0.106 ms is the walk; each of those 801 fills also
clones a whole `BezPath` at `paint_shape`, sized by the boolean's own segment count — which is why a
page of converted icon artwork is the worst case rather than a contrived one.

**A boolean is the *strongest* member of that list, not a doubtful one.** The binding's criterion is
that the bounds cover everything below, and the walk stops dead at a boolean — its children are its
operands, not artwork — so its cached ink bounds cover its whole subtree *exactly*, where a group's
merely happen to. The fix is `| NodeKind::Boolean { .. }` on the `matches!`.

**This is CLAUDE.md's named hazard, one crate over from where it was last swept**: *"adding a
`NodeKind` is a sweep the compiler only half-finds — grep the `matches!(kind` predicates after it
goes quiet."* `[S2.1-MATRIX]` built that matrix for `ondin-core`'s six `_`-armed predicates and
`ondin-render` was not in its scope.

⚠️ **The flip that removes `NodeKind::Group` from the list changes nothing, and that is the sentence
that explains why this survived so long.** Both arms stay green. With `Group` off the list a parked
group is no longer culled *as a subtree* — but the walk descends to its children, which are leaves,
`children().is_empty()` makes the predicate true for each of them, and every one is culled
individually. Same fill count, more walking. **So a group's descendants get culled leaf by leaf
whatever the list says, and the list has never been observable in a fill count for a group.** A
boolean is the one kind where it is, because the walk stops dead there. *The kind that was missing
from the list is the only kind whose absence the list can be caught by* — and the group arm is a
control for the **harness** (that the containers are reachable, that the viewport is genuinely empty,
that a fill count of 1 is the on-screen rect rather than a walk that stopped early), not a control
for the list. The test's own prose said otherwise until the flip was run.

Two tests in `crates/ondin-render/tests/render.rs`:
`an_off_screen_boolean_is_culled_like_an_off_screen_group`, and
`the_boolean_cull_does_not_grow_with_the_number_parked`, which pins the *shape* at 1 and at 40 rather
than asserting a time — a timing assertion in that suite would be a flake, and the two measurements
live in the doc comment and in the finding where nothing has to re-run them. Removing
`NodeKind::Boolean` is red at **4 against 1**, the predicted site. §6.3 amended.

**D535 — A cancelled opacity digit does not commit itself 600 ms later. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08;
Fix — one line on the cancel's clearing list, and the third way the window shuts.***

`[S16.2-L1-01]`, Medium. Press `4` with a layer selected: the canvas previews 40% and the document
correctly still holds 1.0, because the first digit is a preview by design (**D210**). Press `Escape`
and the preview visibly reverts. **600 ms later the layer becomes 40% anyway**, one undo step is
pushed, and the status line re-reads *Opacity 40%*. The right-click cancel — the other door onto
`app::cancel_gesture` — had it identically.

**The cancel fired and did its job.** `set_opacity_pct_on` previews through
`EditorSession::set_preview`, which sets `preview_holds_session = false`, so the opacity preview *is*
a gesture preview, `has_gesture_preview()` is true, and `cancel_gesture` is the rung `escape` stops
on. It cleared the preview correctly. What it never touched was `self.opacity_entry`, absent from its
whole clearing list — which names `drag`, `guide_previews`, `layer_drag`, `paint_drag`, `alt_clone`,
`autopan_total`, `session_scrub`, `settings_scrub`, `grid_scrub`, `grid_paint` and `chrome_hold`. So
`fold_opacity_entry`, which runs unconditionally on every editor frame, still found the entry and
still ran the commit arm on the deadline.

The fix is one line, `self.opacity_entry = None;`, beside `self.grid_paint = None;`. **It belongs in
`cancel_gesture` and not on the `escape` ladder**, because the right-click is the other door — and
the digit window is a gesture even though nothing is held down, which is what puts it on this list at
all.

⚠️ **This round's first instance against a *Resolved* entry, and D210's own sentence is what made it
look covered.** *"The commit happens when the window shuts, whichever way it shuts"* is a phrase a
reader takes as covering `Escape` — but D210 and `docs/shortcuts.md` §2 both enumerate exactly **two**
ways it shuts, a second digit or the deadline, and neither mentions a cancel of either kind. A
cancelled gesture owes zero transactions (§9.3). So this is the third way, and it shuts the window
without committing; D210 is amended to name it rather than left to be read charitably. ⚠️
**`shortcuts.md` §2 carries the same two-way enumeration and is still short**, which is stated here
because that file is outside this register's remit and the sentence is now incomplete rather than
merely terse.

`app::cancelled_opacity_digit_tests`, two. **Flip A**, the line removed, bites at the predicted site
— the post-deadline opacity, `0.4` against `1.0` — and the prediction was easy for once because the
two earlier assertions are *identical* in both versions, so there is only one site it can bite at.
**Flip B is the plausible wrong fix**: deleting `fold_opacity_entry`'s commit, since "stop the
deadline committing" closes the finding and removes the feature in one line. The main test stays
**green** under it and the control goes red at `1.0` against `0.4`. The pair is what says the fix
shut the window rather than nailing it shut. §9.3 amended, and D210 with it.

**D534 — A bare click no longer flattens a mixed corner radius. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix —
the field compares against its own seed, which is `paint_row`'s rule at a second site.***

`[S14.3-L1-01]`, Medium. `inspector::inspector_appearance`'s single corner-radius `value_field` shows
`uniform(corners)` or, when the four disagree, `largest(corners)` — so that **dragging** it starts
from the shape's own scale rather than from 0. It then handed `GeometryPatch::CornerRadius(r)`, which
sets **all four**, to `edit_valve` unconditionally. `edit_valve` commits on the engaged→released
transition a click produces and compares no value against the document, so a rect with corners
`(10, 0, 0, 0)`, clicked into and clicked away from with nothing typed and nothing dragged, became
`(10, 10, 10, 10)` with `undo_depth 0 → 1`. Three corners the user never touched, gone.

⚠️ **The no-op family could not see it, which is why only the *mixed* case was ever visible.**
`Transaction::changes_nothing` (D428) is asked at `commit_inner`. Over an *agreeing* set the write is
a genuine no-op and D428 has absorbed it since it was written; over a disagreeing one the transaction
really does change the document, so D428 is right to let it through and **the guard has to be at the
field**. The fix is `if shared.is_some() || r != seed`, where `shared` is `uniform(corners)` and
`seed` is the number the field was seeded with.

**This is `paint_row`'s `!hazy || moved` at a second field** — the guard written for
`[S14.4-L1-01]` at **D465**, the same accident for the same reason: a readout has to hand its control
*some* number while the set disagrees, and `edit_valve` commits on a transition without comparing
anything. `largest`'s own doc says what the seed is for — *"so **dragging it** starts from the
shape's own scale"* — and a click is not a drag.

⚠️ **And it widens D465 rather than repeating it.** That entry's survey concludes *"every other
`Mixed` numeric field in the inspector was safe"*, which is true and is the wrong population: this
field prints a **number**, not the word, and is on the *single-node* panel rather than the
multi-selection one. What marks the family is not the word `Mixed` but **being seeded from one member
of a disagreeing set** — so the question to ask of any numeric field is where its value came from,
not what it says. D465 amended.

**What it gives up, on purpose**: typing the shown number over a mixed set, which reads as "flatten
them all to this", now does nothing. The per-corner disclosure button one place to the right is that
edit's door, and `paint_row` makes the identical trade at the identical seam. §5.3 already says the
flatten is a real edit — *"its inverse is a `CornerRadii`, because flattening four values into one is
not undoable any other way"* — which is the argument for making it be asked for.

**A gap rather than a contradiction.** D53 names this field only for the *readout*, and §5.7a's
no-op promise is D428's, which is correct about this write; nothing in the design said a seeded
number may not be committed by a click.

`panels::inspector::mixed_corner_radius_tests`, two tests. The aim point `(200, 60)` was found by
sweeping and is written down, because this row's other claimants are **silent** rather than
destructive — unlike `mixed_opacity_tests`, where a mis-aim clears every fill and fails loudly, a
mis-aimed press here writes nothing and the test goes green for the wrong reason. In a 320-wide card
the row is y = 46…74, the opacity field's focusable box is x = 47…134, the radius field's is
x = 178…265 and the per-corner button's hit area is x = 272…310, identical at 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0
`pixels_per_point`.

⚠️ **The harness must feed the panel from `session.display_node`, not `session.doc`.** A live drag
lives in the *preview*, so a `corners0` re-read from the committed document re-seeds `r` on every
frame, the release then commits `r == seed`, and the guard under test blocks a write that was never
made — measured, and the file passes with the fix deleted. `inspector_single` reads through
`display_node` for exactly this reason.

**Double-flipped.** The guard removed fails at `(10,10,10,10)` against `(10,0,0,0)`, the predicted
site. The guard removed *and* the three claim assertions disabled leaves the drag control **green**,
which is what says the control is a control — "the aim point is the radius field and the guard has
not turned it off" — rather than a second copy of the claim that would go red for the same reason.
Run, not reasoned: the first assertion aborts the test, so a single flip says nothing about anything
after it. §5.3 and §9.4 amended, and D465 with them.

**D533 — The popover lane is six things, and two hand-written lists each knew four of them. *Fixed
and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — one named query for the lane, a spelled-out list for the clear, and a
test on the single member by which they differ.***

`[S16.4-L1-05]` and `[S15.2-L1-03]`, both Medium. They are one entry because they are one defect
written twice: **a hand-maintained set of "the floating things", short in two functions that never
look at each other.**

**(a) The lane.** `app::picker_lane_right` reserved on four states — `type_menu`, `stroke_menu`,
`effect_menu` and `edited_image` — where **six** popovers hang in it. The two missing are the Export
card's: `export::export_settings_popup`, gated on `export_row_open`, and
`export::export_menu_popup`, gated on `export_menu`, both anchored through `popover_anchor` at
`POPOVER_W`, *the same width the lane is computed from*. So opening either and then clicking a Fill
chip opened the colour picker **underneath it**: the popover is `Order::Foreground` where the picker
is `Order::Middle`, and from the measured column rect the arithmetic puts **236 of the picker's 240
points** inside the popover's span. `picker_lane_right` is consulted only on the frame the picker is
created, so a popover opened *first* — the ordinary order — is the whole of the exposure.

**(b) The clear.** `menu::open_context_menu` cleared four of the seven floating things R4 covers,
and the two Export popovers were two of the three it missed. `effect_menu` and `export_menu` both
survived a context-menu open — measured — leaving **two `Order::Foreground` `Area`s over the canvas
the menu was aimed at**, which is the state R4 exists to make unreachable. Neither dismisses itself
on the way, because both read `PointerButton::Primary` only, deliberately, so the secondary click
that opened the menu is invisible to them.

⚠️ **The second consequence is the sharper one, and it is R3 broken by a route R3's own guard cannot
reach.** One `Escape` then closed the context menu *and* the effects popover, because
`inspector_panel` runs before `context_menu_ui` and `effect_menu_popup` reads the same unconsumed
key — *"the press that closes a menu closes only the menu"* failing in a region where the guard at
the top of the frame cannot help, since the second thing dismissed is not a menu. It goes away with
the clear, and **that half is closed as a consequence rather than directly**: nothing asserts the
two-things-on-one-press case, because with the clear in place the state it needs is unreachable. If
the clear is ever narrowed, this is what comes back.

**The counts, stated once, because nothing else states them.** Six popovers hang in the lane:
typography, stroke, effects, the Export card's row settings, the Export panel's own menu, and the
image-editing card. R4's clear is **seven** floating things — the top-bar dropdown slot and the
colour picker, plus five of those six. ⚠️ **The odd one out is the image-editing card, and it is the
reason the two lists are deliberately not one.** R4 clears *the floating things somebody opened*;
that card is what the mode looks like, so clearing it would leave a right-click having silently
half-left a mode — gestures still armed, outline still drawn, controls gone. A shared list would have
to carry an exception, which is exactly how a member comes to be quietly excluded from one of the
two. So: two lists, differing by one member, each naming the other, and **a test that asserts the
difference** rather than leaving it to be re-derived. ⚠️ **Three lists since 2026-09-19** (D801):
`OndinApp::a_popover_owns_escape` is the lane's six minus the same image card, excluded for the same
reason running in the same direction — the key that *leaves* image editing is the ladder's own rung,
so a popover gate that held it would swallow the way out. **Two of the three exclude the card on one
argument**, which is what to check before any of them is folded into another.

**The shape of the fix is the argument.** (a) becomes one named query, `OndinApp::a_popover_is_open`,
so a seventh popover joins one list or does not work and there is one place to look. (b) stays
spelled out, for the reason above. `app::popover_lane_tests::every_popover_in_the_lane_reserves_it`
drives all five settable states as a table plus a `None` control — ⚠️ **the control is load-bearing**:
it fails a `picker_lane_right` that reserves unconditionally, which is the plausible wrong fix
because it looks like it can only help. `menu::tests::opening_a_context_menu_clears_every_floating_thing`
asserts every clear **and** that `Tool::ImageEdit` survives, which is the assertion that stops the two
lists being "simplified" into one. Flips: dropping `export_menu` and `export_row_open` from
`a_popover_is_open` is red on those two rows and green on the other four and on the control; dropping
the three new clears from `open_context_menu` is red at **`effect_menu`**, the first of them checked
— `export_row_open` is asserted last and would not have fired, which is the second time this session
that the *order* of assertions decided which one reports.

⚠️ **Both comments named the wrong count in prose, and so does the design.**
`open_context_menu`'s said *"All five of these"* over a list of four; `context-menus.md` §0 R4 says
*"the View and Snap dropdowns, the colour picker and the **four** inspector popovers"* and then names
the six clears `openCanvasMenu` makes in the design export, which is where the four came from — the
app has grown three popovers since and neither half of the sentence followed. **A set nobody owns
gets miscounted by everyone who counts it.** §0 R4 is corrected and says it was wrong rather than
being quietly made right, and `context-menus.md` §9.6 carries it as item 15.

⚠️ **And the count was got wrong again in the fixing, which is this entry's own point turned on
itself.** `open_context_menu`'s new comment reads *"It cleared four of six"* and the test's doc
comment repeats it, where the clear is **seven** fields; six is the design export's number, not this
app's. `a_popover_is_open`'s own doc has the lane's four-of-six right. *Fix with the two comments in
`menu.rs` corrected to seven — the numbers in this entry are the measured ones.*

⚠️ **D107 asked exactly this question and nobody answered it for the third and fourth surface.** Its
closing line is *"any third floating surface owes the same question: which lane is it in, and what is
already there"*, written when the lane was invented; both Export popovers were put in the lane
without it being asked. D107 amended to say so. §9.4 amended: R4's clear is enumerated there and was
enumerated as four.

**D532 — A multi-row drop that lands the rows where they already are planned an undo step. *Fixed and
tested 2026-09-08; Fix — the composition tested once, against the simulation the planner already
keeps.***

`[S15.1-L1-03]`, Medium. `layers::plan_layer_move`'s no-op test is **per row**, and it compares each
row's landing index with the position that row held *before* the rows ahead of it were lifted out of
the list. So a run of rows dropped at the boundary immediately after itself gives every one of them
an `at` that differs from its own `at_from`, while the **net permutation is the identity**. Measured
over `[k0, k1, k2]` moving `[k0, k1]`: index 2 plans **two** `Reorder`s over a byte-identical child
list — `undo_depth 0 → 1`, the document dirtied so an autosave and a crash snapshot fire, and a
status line claiming *"Reordered 2 layers"*. The **single-row** version of the same drop is correctly
`ops = 0`. It scales: n rows give n net-zero ops.

⚠️ **The result was never wrong.** This is a non-minimal op list and not a wrong move, which is why
it survived: everything on screen is right.

⚠️ **D428's `changes_nothing` cannot absorb it, and the reason is this entry's most useful
sentence.** `Operation::Reorder`'s arm asks `child_index(doc, id) == Some(index)` of the document
**as it stands**, and each of the n ops moves its row to an index it is not at *yet*. Not one of them
is a no-op, so `Transaction::changes_nothing` is `false` and the transaction commits. **A composition
of real operations that returns to where it started is invisible to any per-operation guard.** That
is the third distinct shape this session found that D428 misses — D520's transaction that is never
*built*, D528's mode flip that is a genuine change nobody asked for, and this one — and the three
are worth stating as a class: `changes_nothing` answers *"is each write a write of what is already
there"*, which is a narrower question than *"did the user's gesture change anything"* in three
different directions. §9.3 says so now, in one bullet, with the never-built case cross-referenced to
§9.4 where D520 left it.

⚠️ **And D428 named this very gesture as one of the routes it closed.** Its own text read *"So does a
multi-row layers drop that lands rows where they already are, which emits one net-zero `Reorder` per
row"* — true about the net and false about the operations, so the route was never covered, and §9.3
repeated it. Both are corrected rather than dropped: a reader who has just measured n live `Reorder`s
deserves to find out where the claim came from.

**The fix is in the planner, against the simulation it already keeps**, not at the commit: after the
loop, if nothing was reparented and every touched parent's simulated child list equals the
document's, the ops are cleared. **Only when nothing was reparented**, because a reparent's
`SetTransform` ops are not modelled by `sim`, so a child-list comparison would be answering about
half the transaction. `finish_layer_drag`'s existing `Ok(plan) if plan.ops.is_empty()` guard then
does the rest, and the status line stops lying.

⚠️ **A test of that name already existed and moved one row**, which is what hid this.
`a_drop_that_moves_nothing_plans_nothing` dropped a **single** row at index 0 and stopped — the
assertion existed, carried exactly the right name, and covered the arm that worked. It is replaced by
a version that walks all three boundaries which leave a two-row run where it is, keeps the single-row
case as a control, and asserts that a real move still plans both rows. **A suite of one-row drops
would find nothing wrong here**, and the finding had to name the index it did for the same reason:
the flip that removes the composition test is red at **index 2 with two rows** and green at indices 0
and 1 either way.

⚠️ **And the way this one was nearly missed belongs in the entry.** It was written up in this
session's own log as *"very probably closed by D428 already — not verified"*, in the paragraph that
was writing up the lesson *"a finding's symptom can be closed by an unrelated fix; let the flip say
which part"*. Checking it took four minutes and found it wide open. **An open finding is cheaper to
check than to reason about**, and a dismissal reasoned from the mechanism is worth exactly what a
flip prediction reasoned from the mechanism is worth — which this session got wrong three times out
of six.

**D531 — `ondin export --all` exited 0 having written nothing. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix —
one gate on the files produced rather than on the layers collected.***

`[S16.5-L1-01]`. `main::run_export_all`'s only failure gate was `subjects.is_empty()`, which fires on
the set of **layers**, not on the set of **files produced**. A document whose only exporting layer has
no ink — an empty group, a fully hidden layer, a zero-size shape — carrying a **raster** spec wrote
nothing, did not even create the output directory, said *"skipped …"* on **stderr** where a build step
does not read it, and returned `Ok(())`.

⚠️ **Which is the failure this function's own doc says the exit-1 path exists to prevent, three
paragraphs above the code that did it**: *"Exit code 1 when a document has no export settings at all,
rather than a cheerful zero over nothing written. A build step that silently succeeds without producing
its output is the failure that gets noticed three commits later."* §7 stated the same rule and scoped
it the same way — *"nothing in the document is set up to export"* — and no §15 entry covered the
every-file-skipped case, so this is **a gap rather than a violated verdict**. §7 is widened, and says
it was narrower rather than reading as though it had always covered this.

The fix is one `if written.is_empty()` after the render loop, naming the skipped count in its message.
⚠️ **The raster arm is the only one that reaches it**: `png::raster_of` opens with
`extent(res, origins)?`, while `plan::render`'s SVG branch always answers `Some` — so an empty group
carrying an *SVG* spec writes a file and exits 0, correctly, and **a version of the test built on the
default spec would have passed under the defect.** The test says so rather than leaving the next reader
to find it by changing the fixture.
`main::tests::an_export_all_that_skips_every_file_fails_rather_than_exiting_zero` asserts the error
**and** that the output directory was never created — the half stderr could not say, and the half a
build step actually trips over. Flip: removing the branch is red at `expect_err`, with the `Ok(())` the
finding measured.

**D530 — The three text-sizing rows were offered over a multi-selection, and the test named for the
rule proved nothing. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — the `one` every neighbouring push already
had.***

`[S15.2-L1-02]`. `menu::head_rows` pushed the three `Item::TextSizing` rows on `all_are(Kind::Text)`
with **no `one`**, where every one of the eight neighbouring pushes in the same function is inside an
`if one`. Measured: two text layers in *different* sizing states, both selected, right-click one — all
three rows appear, the hit layer's state is ticked as though it were the selection's, and taking a row
writes **only** the hit layer, while the other's tick was never shown. D261 rules that out in as many
words: *"'Every member qualifies' is satisfied by a pair of text layers — both are text — but the tick
is a fact about one node."* `docs/context-menus.md` §5.6 says the same in its table. ⚠️ **And so did the
code comment three lines above the push** — *"only over one layer: the tick says which state this node
is in, and a selection of two text nodes in different states has no honest answer to put there"* — so
the rule was written down three times and enforced nowhere.

⚠️ **The `Option` was doing the work the `one` was supposed to do, and it cannot.** The guard reads
`if let Some(cell) = st.text_sizing`, and `layer_menu_state` reads `text_sizing` off the **hit** node
alone, so it can never be `None` while the hit is text. `LayerState::text_sizing`'s own doc is right
that an `Option` makes the unanswerable state unspellable — but the state it makes unspellable is *not
text*, and the state this row needed guarding against is *several nodes*. **A fact about one node
cannot answer a question about a set**, however carefully it is typed.

⚠️ **The test named for the rule closed on a state the app cannot be in.**
`the_three_sizing_rows_tick_one_and_only_over_a_single_text_layer` ended with `menu(2, None)` — and
`None` there is the fixture's *own hand-set* `LayerState::text_sizing`, not what `layer_menu_state`
returns; nothing in the suite calls that function. *What would also pass it*: exactly the code that
shipped. It closes with `menu(2, Some(0))` now, the state a real two-layer selection produces, and the
flip that removes `one` is red on it. **This is `CLAUDE.md`'s third vacuity shape — a fixture that
never reaches the state it names — met in a test whose *name* is the rule**, which is the version of it
hardest to distrust. `context-menus.md` §9.6 carries this as item 14.

**D529 — *Rename* was the one row a lock dimmed that the spec lists as staying live. *Fixed and tested
2026-09-08; Fix — the dim goes, the design having decided this one the other way.***

`[S15.2-L1-01]`. `menu::layer_menu` pushed
`Row::new(Item::Rename).dim_if(!one, …).dim_if(locked, why)`. `docs/context-menus.md` §5.9 names the
five rows that stay live over a locked layer — *"every editing row is dimmed while **Unlock**,
**Show**, **Rename**, **Copy** and **Zoom to selection** stay live"* — and *Rename* is one of them: a
name is not the layer's artwork, which is the argument that already keeps *Copy* and *Copy properties*
live two groups up.

**The row was the only one of the verb's three doors that refused.** `Ctrl+R`, `F2` and the layers
panel's double-click all renamed a locked layer without complaint, which is the failure D261 states 380
lines below this very push, in the *Edit image* row: *"a menu refusing where a key allows is the
failure, and a menu agreeing with one is not."* **D320 brought *Edit image* into line by adding the
refusal to the verb; here the design says the other way, so the dim goes rather than the chords
growing one.** D320 and D321 both enumerate the rows they touch and neither names *Rename*; D216 is its
only other appearance in §15 and is about where the caret lands.

⚠️ **The test named for the rule asserted four live rows where §5.9 names five**, which is how this
survived a section that has been read several times: `Item::Rename` and `Item::ToggleHidden` were
live-by-spec and asserted by nothing, and one of the two was wrong.
`menu::tests::a_locked_layer_dims_the_editing_rows_and_keeps_the_way_back`'s live list is now §5.9's
sentence entire, plus *Copy properties* for the reason its own comment gives, and the flip — restoring
`.dim_if(locked, why)` — is red on it. **A list that quotes a spec should be the whole sentence, or it
is a filter nobody chose.** `context-menus.md` §9.6 carries this as item 13.

**D528 — A click in image-edit mode committed, and silently changed the picture's mode. *Fixed and
tested 2026-09-08; Fix — the commit is gated on travel and the preview deliberately is not.***

`[S12.3-L1-04]`. A press and a release with no movement — the ordinary way of dismissing a mode or
checking where you are — committed. `canvas::image_edit_input`'s `Drag::CropPan` arm builds its
transaction for a delta of zero, and `crop_tx` writes `fit = ImageFit::Crop` **unconditionally**, so a
`Fill` picture became a `Crop` one and the click left an undo step behind it.

⚠️ **The pixels do not move, which is why it could ship.** A `Fill` picture's seed crop *is*
`cover_crop`, so nothing on screen changes and the whole consequence arrives later: the *Fit* control
reads Crop, and resizing the layer stops re-framing the picture — which is exactly the difference
`ImageFit`'s own doc draws between the two derived modes and the two stored ones.

⚠️ **The guard exists in the same file for the same hazard, 900 lines away, and neither crop door
consulted it.** `canvas::gesture_travelled`'s doc *is* this finding's argument, written for the node
tool: *"`node_input` runs its drag arms on the press frame and on the release frame of a plain click,
where the delta is nothing … leaves an undo step behind a press that was only ever a selection."*

**The fix.** Both `Drag::CropPan` and `Drag::CropResize` carry a new `grab_world: Point`, and the
commit — **not the preview** — is gated on `gesture_travelled(world_at - grab_world)`. World rather
than the node's local space, deliberately: the threshold is a screen distance, and a layer scaled 10×
would otherwise need a tenth of the hand movement to count as a drag. `Drag::PointBox` already carries
exactly this field for exactly this reason and says so in its own doc; these are the second and third
instance. **Gating the preview instead would break `image_ghost_live`'s promise** that the ghost
arrives with the first travelled frame rather than a gesture late, and the preview costs nothing
because it commits nothing. An untravelled release clears the preview a commit would have cleared —
`clear_gesture_preview` per D109 — because otherwise the click would go on *showing* the flip it did
not make: the inspector reads the preview through `display_node`, so the *Fit* control would say Crop
until something unrelated cleared it.

⚠️ **A generic no-op guard at the commit would not have caught this**, which is worth stating because
`[S13.1-L1-08]` and `[S12.1-L1-05]` proposed one for the same family. The transaction is genuinely not
a no-op — it writes a mode the picture did not have — and D428's `changes_nothing` is exact, so it
answers `false` for it and is right to. **The mode flip needed the travel guard specifically**, which
is the general shape: *a write that changes nothing visible is still a write, and only the gesture
knows it was never asked for.*

⚠️ **The first version of the test passed while measuring nothing, and only the control said so.** The
fixture left the camera at its default, which puts the layer's world origin off a 400×300 canvas
entirely — a click in the middle of the canvas probed at world `(599.5, 449.5)` against a frame of
`0..100` — so every press missed the picture, `Drag::CropPan` was never armed, and *"a click commits
nothing"* was a true statement about a gesture that did not happen. The travelled control failed, which
is the only reason it was found. **A headless canvas test must aim the camera**, and the module doc now
says so at the fixture. `canvas::crop_click_tests::a_click_in_image_edit_mode_commits_nothing` asserts
the **mode** before the count, because that is what a no-op guard would miss, and
`a_travelled_crop_pan_still_commits` asserts `Drag::CropPan` is armed before anything else. Flip:
committing unconditionally is red at the mode, `Crop` for `Fill`.

§9.3 and §9.4 amended — §9.3's no-undo-step paragraph now names travel as the third mechanism beside
the empty transaction and `changes_nothing`, and §9.4's image-editing section says which of the two
crop gestures is gated on it.

**D527 — One `Escape` closed a top-bar dropdown *and* paid out a rung of the ladder. *Fixed and
tested 2026-09-08; Fix — one match arm, the mirror of the context menu's.***

`[S16.4-L1-04]`. With the Rect tool armed, opening the top bar's Zoom (or View, or Snap) menu and
pressing `Escape` closed the menu **and** dropped the tool to Select. ⚠️ **The context menu has an
explicit rule against exactly this and `TopMenu` was not covered by it.** `<OndinApp as
eframe::App>::ui`'s context-menu arm states it in as many words — *"the press that closes a menu closes
**only** the menu. `escape` is a ladder that pays out one rung per press, and a version that closed the
menu and then fell through would deselect, or leave the group, or drop back to Select, in the same
keystroke that dismissed a menu opened by accident — eating the very state the menu was aimed at"* — and
makes it structural by **returning**, so there is no path from that arm to the ladder. `TopMenu` had no
arm at all.

**The principle covered it while no verdict did**, which is where this sits in the design rather than
in the code. `docs/context-menus.md` §0 **R3** is written generally — *"a menu"* — and **R4 explicitly
names the top-bar dropdowns** in the one-slot rule, so the dropdowns are inside R4 and outside R3's
keyboard clause, which was only ever justified in the context menu's own three regions. No passage
anywhere extended press-consumption to `TopMenu`. R3 says so now.

⚠️ **`input::resolve`'s `egui_wants_keyboard_input` guard does not stand in for it**, and that is
measured rather than reasoned: opening a dropdown by clicking its head leaves `focused() == None`, so
egui does not think anything wants the keyboard and the action resolves as usual. It is D464's
observation about the modals met on a second surface — that check is `focused().is_some()`, not "a
widget is taking characters", and a floating thing with no text field in it never trips it.

⚠️ **Flipped, and the failure *site* is the finding.** Removing the
`Action::Escape if self.open_menu != TopMenu::None` arm is red at the **tool**, not at the menu — the
menu closes either way, because `dropdown` reads the key itself as well. So the assertion that names
the defect is the one about the state that was *eaten*, and **a test asserting only "the menu closed"
would have been green under the defect**. Anywhere two mechanisms can produce the same visible
dismissal, assert on the thing that was supposed to survive.
`app::library_wiring_tests::escape_over_a_top_bar_dropdown_closes_only_the_dropdown`.

⚠️ **Amended 2026-09-08: the comment above that arm had landed on top of itself, twenty-four lines
twice, with every gate green.** The cause is new and is the reason it is recorded here rather than
merely fixed — it came from a **flip-and-restore** rather than from an edit. The flip removed only the
`Action::Escape if …` line; the restore put back the line *plus* its comment block, so the block ended
up stacked on the copy that had never left. That is D451's `op_create` duplication arriving by a second
road, and the first instance this project has had caused by flip-checking rather than by inserting. It
is also the exact case `CLAUDE.md` says the rule covers and that a reader will assume it does not: **a
flip is an edit, and the revert is an edit too**, so take out and put back precisely the same text.
Found by `arch-scribe` reading the change; fixed at `714d8f4`.

§9.4 amended — the one-press-one-rung paragraph now states the rule for every floating thing and names
the four doors and the different mechanism at each — and `context-menus.md` §0 R3 with it.

⚠️ **Amended 2026-09-19: the four doors named above are nine.** They were the four that *read* the
key — the context menu, the top-bar dropdowns, the three modals and the colour picker — and the five
inspector and Export popovers were outside the enumeration because nobody had measured them. **All
five were breaking the rule**, three by reading the key without stopping the ladder and two by not
reading it at all. See **D801**, which is this rule applied to them; the enumeration above is of the
mechanisms found on 2026-09-08 and is left as written rather than rewritten, since it is what the
audit of that day saw.

**D801 — Every popover answers `Escape`, and none of them pays out a rung any more. *Fixed and
tested 2026-09-19; Resolved — `roadmap.md`'s measure-first bullet is spent, and both shapes it
predicted were real.***

That bullet carried this as a question with an instruction attached — *"measure before writing
anything down"* — because D527's own dropdown case was red at the **tool** and green at the **menu**,
so the assertion has to be on the state that was supposed to survive. Measured first, on a headless
app with the tool set to `Tool::Rect` so the ladder's last rung is the observable one, one `Escape`
driven through `RawInput`:

| popover | closed on `Escape`? | ladder paid out? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none — the control | — | **yes**, `Rect` → `Select` |
| `stroke_menu` | yes | **yes** |
| `effect_menu` | yes | **yes** |
| `type_menu` | yes | **yes** |
| `export_menu` | **no** | **yes** |
| `export_row_open` | **no** | **yes** |

**Both shapes the bullet predicted were real** — three popovers of the first and two of the second,
which is every popover it named. The three inspector popovers read `key_pressed`, which does not
consume, so each closed itself *and* let the press through to `input::resolve` —
D533's second consequence with no menu in it, one press taking two things. The Export card's two read
no key at all, so `Escape` did the one thing it should not, dropping a rung, and none of the thing it
should.

🚨 **The fixture nearly made the measurement wrong, and that is the half worth carrying forward.** On
a *rect*, `type_menu` measured as still up after the press — looking exactly like the Export card's
failure — because a shape draws no Typography panel, so nothing ever ran the handler and the flag
merely survived untouched. On a text node it measures the opposite. **A popover that nothing is
drawing answers every key the same way, which is indistinguishable from ignoring them.** The
instruction was to measure before writing anything down; the lesson on top of it is that **a
measurement needs its fixture asserted**, because this one would have been written down backwards.

**The fix is two parts.** `OndinApp::a_popover_owns_escape`, and a new arm in
`<OndinApp as eframe::App>::update` between the modal arm and the `else` that runs `input::resolve`:
while one of the five is open, an `Escape` press reaches no ladder. **The arm's body is empty on
purpose** — the popovers close themselves later in the same frame on the same `key_pressed`, so what
the arm removes is only the *second* thing the press was doing, which is dropping the tool, leaving
the group or clearing the selection behind a popover the user was looking straight at. And
`panels/export.rs` gained the `key_pressed(Escape)` block its two popovers never had, clearing both.

🚨 **`a_popover_owns_escape` is `a_popover_is_open` minus the image-edit card, and the one-member
difference is load-bearing rather than tidy.** Image editing is a `Tool::ImageEdit`, so *leaving* it
is the ladder's own `tool != Select` rung — gating `Escape` on it would strand the user in the mode
with the key that exits it swallowed. **It is D533's exclusion, for the same reason and in the same
direction**: that entry keeps the card out of R4's clear because R4 clears the floating things
somebody opened and *"that card is what the mode looks like"*, and this is the same sentence applied
to a key instead of to a right-click. So the lane now has **three** lists rather than two, and the
two that exclude the card exclude it on one argument — which is the thing to check before any of
them is "simplified" into another.

⚠️ **`Escape` only, not the keyboard.** A modal owns every key because the document behind it cannot
be seen; a popover sits over a canvas the user is still looking at, and nothing about it earns
`Delete` or an arrow. That is the narrow claim D527 actually makes, and it is why this arm gates one
key rather than standing `input::resolve` down the way D464's modals do.

**Test** — `app::context_menu_rule_tests::escape_over_a_popover_closes_it_and_pays_out_no_rung`, five
cases plus the control. Each case asserts its fixture is in the state it is about *before* the key,
for the `type_menu` reason above. ⚠️ **The control carries the whole test**: every other assertion is
that the tool did *not* change, which a completely broken ladder also produces, so without a case
proving `Escape` still pays out when nothing is up, the five would pass against an `escape` that had
stopped working.

**Three flips, all run.** Removing the arm from `update` is red on `stroke_menu`'s tool assertion,
the first popover case. Narrowing `a_popover_owns_escape` to drop `type_menu` is red on that case
alone, `Select` against `Rect` — **the gate is per-popover and nothing else covers any one of the
five**. Removing the Export card's new `key_pressed` block is red on `export_menu`'s *closed*
assertion; ⚠️ **whether its tool assertion also goes red is reasoned and not measured**, the closed
assertion panicking first so the tool one is never reached, and the reasoning is that `export_menu`
is still `true` under that flip and the gate therefore still fires. **The two halves are
independent** — one arm stops the rung, one block closes the popover — which is the argument for
asserting both per case rather than once at the end.

§9.4's one-press-one-rung paragraph is amended, its four doors now nine and its closing *"what is
still unmeasured"* clause spent; §9.4's two-lists sentence and §7's Export-popover paragraph say
three; `shortcuts.md`'s ladder paragraph gains the rung a popover takes ahead of it;
`context-menus.md` §0 R3 gains a fourth site found the way it predicts sites are found; and D527 and
D533 are amended. **The whole *Now · Keyboard* `Escape` bullet is struck from `roadmap.md`**, its
already-struck D558/D578 sub-clause with it — that section keeps D466's `Mode::TextInsert` question
and two others, so it does not join that file's *"sections with nothing open"* line.

**D526 — The close interception was structurally unreachable from the library screen, and the flag it
sets was cleared by nothing on the way out. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — two calls lifted above
the view branch and one line added to a clear list.***

`[S16.1-L2-04]`, and it is two defects that only look like one because they share a flag.

**(a) The ✕ was not intercepted on the library screen.** `handle_close_request` — whose own doc says
*"intercept the window close so unsaved work is never lost silently"*, a claim about the **window** —
sat below `<OndinApp as eframe::App>::ui`'s `View::Dashboard` return, so on the library screen it never
ran whatever the session held. **Reachable, and by ordinary means**: `go_to_dashboard` autosaves on the
way out only for a document that *has a path*, and `save_file` returns early after `session.fail` on
any write error — a read-only file, a full disk, a stale `.writing` another process holds. What stopped
it being outright loss is the `.recovery/` snapshot, which is up to `SNAPSHOT_SECS` behind. Both
`handle_close_request` and `close_confirmation` are above the return now, beside `recovery_modal`,
which has been there since D377 for exactly this reason and says so.

⚠️ **The comment at that return claimed the font poll was *"the one thing given up by returning this
early"*, and it was wrong by four**: these two, `disk_results` and the two ticks were all below it.
Exactly one of the five had been compensated by hand — `go_to_dashboard` clears the snapshot and says
*"the tick is an editor frame's job"* — and the same argument was never made for the close. Two of the
five are lifted; the comment now names the three that stay and why each is deliberate. ⚠️ **D365 and
§9.5 both quote the ordering verbatim** — *"before the font poll, before `input::resolve`, before
`handle_close_request`"* — with the argument *no tool, no selection, no canvas*, **which is an argument
about the editor's own machinery and never was one about the window.** Both are amended: the ordering
is unchanged for everything except the close, and the close is above it.

**(b) `confirming_close` was written `true` in one place and cleared in three, none of them on the way
out of the editor.** The three are the card's own Save, Discard and Cancel arms. Not `go_to_dashboard`
— which clears `picker`, `context_menu`, `open_menu` and `rename_entry` — not `reset_transient_state`,
not `open_path`. Measured: `Ctrl+O` under the card walked to the dashboard with
`confirming_close == true`, where the card is not drawn, so the question could no longer be answered
and the next ✕ closed the window uninterrupted; and coming back into the editor it was still `true`
with `is_dirty()` **false**, so the *"has changes that have not been saved"* card returned over a
document that had none. **Cleared rather than answered**: the question was *"are you closing this
document?"* and the user has stopped closing it.

⚠️ **That clear list is the second hand-written one of its class to be found short**, the first being
`reset_transient_state` and `per_corner_radius` at D447 — §9.4 now names both together, because nothing
checks either and a new piece of editor chrome joins neither by construction.

Two tests. `the_close_card_is_reachable_from_the_library` drives a `ViewportEvent::Close` through
`eframe::App::ui` with `view == Dashboard` and asserts the card rises **and** that a `CancelClose` is
emitted — the second half mattering because raising a card while the window goes down anyway is not an
interception. `walking_to_the_library_clears_the_close_card` is the other. Flips: putting both calls
back below the return is red at `confirming_close`, with the `CancelClose` assertion never reached;
making the clear a no-op is red at **the only assertion in the workspace that can see it**, nothing
else reading the flag outside the card.

§9.4 and §9.5 amended, and D365 with them.

**D525 — `Escape` over the *Unsaved changes* card did not answer it, and did not stop there. *Fixed
and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — the card reads the `ModalResponse` it was already being handed.***

`[S16.1-L1-03]`. `app::close_confirmation` called `egui::Modal::new(…).show(ctx, …)` and read only its
three buttons, dropping the returned `ModalResponse` on the floor. So `Escape` — the universal way out
of a dialog — was **unhandled**: the card stayed up, and the key fell through
`<OndinApp as eframe::App>::ui`'s ungated `else` into `OndinApp::escape`, which paid out a rung of the
editor's escape ladder underneath it. Measured before the fix at `tool` `Rect → Select` with
`confirming_close` still `true`; held down it kept going — present mode off, picker dismissed, text
session finished, gesture cancelled, points cleared, pivot off, group exited, selection cleared — with
the card still asking. The control is one modal away: `Escape` over Settings closes it and leaves the
tool alone.

**Both sibling modals already did this**, which is what makes it an omission rather than a question.
`settings::settings_ui` maps `should_close()` to `Cancel`; `recovery_modal` maps it to *Later*
**deliberately** rather than to *Discard*, with a test named for it and a ⚠️ saying that collapsing a
reflex key into the destructive arm *"would delete somebody's only copy of an hour's drawing because
they tapped a key"*. So the fix is one `if modal.should_close() { decision = Some(CloseChoice::Cancel) }`
— and **`Cancel` is D377's argument reaching the second modal it applies to**: the safe arm, which here
also means the ✕ that opened the card is simply called off.

⚠️ **§9.5 enumerates the modals sharing this convention and this card was not among them.** That list
is eight, every one drawn on `settings::card_modal`, where the *Unsaved changes* card is a bare
`egui::Modal` with three buttons and no `modal_title` ✕ — which is how it came to sit outside a
convention §9.5 describes as holding everywhere. It is nine now and §9.5 **says so** rather than quietly
gaining a row: the convention is wider than the card it was written about, and the one modal not drawn
on the shared card is the one that stopped keeping it. D368 is amended to say the same, because that is
the entry the universality claim descends from and it is an entry about the *card*.

⚠️ **Half of this finding was closed before the fix was written, by a change made for another reason,
and the test says so in its own doc.** D464 had already stopped the key reaching `input::resolve` while
any of the three modals is up, so the ladder no longer pays out; what was left was a card that would
not go away. The flip bears it out — dropping the `should_close()` arm is red at `confirming_close` and
**green at the tool** — so the tool assertion is a regression guard rather than this fix's doing.
*That is D520's shape a second time and it has now happened twice in two sessions:* **when a fix closes
a finding older than the last round of work, expect part of it to be already closed, and let the flip
say which part.** A test written to a stale finding's own measurement is vacuous the day it is written,
with every gate green.

`app::library_wiring_tests::escape_over_the_close_card_cancels_it_and_leaves_the_tool_alone`.
⚠️ **It needs a settling frame before the key**: `ModalResponse::should_close` gates Escape on
`is_top_modal`, which egui derives from the stack the *previous* pass built, so a probe that delivered
the key on the frame the card was born measured a card that ignored it — which reads exactly like the
defect it was written for. D377 records the same trap for
`escape_defers_a_recovery_and_never_deletes_it`; this is the second test to pay for it.

§9.5 amended, and D368 with it.

**D524 — A line predicting what the valve would do was the expression the valve had stopped using.
*Fixed and tested 2026-09-08; Fix — the valve reports, and a gate for the expression itself.***

**Not a review finding either, and the fourth accident in a row** — found by grepping `crates/` for
the literal while writing D523's entry, which is why the gate below exists. `inspector::valve_slot`
computed, immediately *before* calling `edit_valve`:

```rust
// Decided before the valve runs, because the valve is what makes it true.
let committing =
    !resp.dragged() && (resp.drag_stopped() || resp.lost_focus() || resp.changed());
self.edit_valve(resp, tx);
```

⚠️ **The comment is the whole finding.** It says the valve is what makes the predicate true, and the
predicate is the expression D316 took *out* of the valve — so it had not been true since. **Two
retargets read it**, both of them in the ten lines under it: the Group Colors one, which moves a
row's key onto the colour it just became and whose own paragraph says what happens when it is wrong —
*"the picker finds nothing to edit on the next frame and closes itself in the user's hand"* — and
`retarget_mixed_paint`, which is that failure arrived at from the other direction, a mixed row's slot
ceasing to exist the moment the edit makes its targets agree. **The line above them was causing the
failure the paragraphs below it exist to prevent.**

**Measured**, by driving a `DragValue` through `edit_valve` and recording per frame what the
prediction answered against what the valve did. A typed edit: the prediction answers `true` on
**four** frames — both keystrokes, and *both* of the two frames a `DragValue` reports `lost_focus()`
on — where the valve commits **once**. An **abandoned** edit (`Escape`): the prediction answers
`true` **twice** where the valve commits **nothing**, so a cancelled colour retargeted the row
anyway.

**The fix removes the mirror rather than correcting it.** `OndinApp::edit_valve` returns `bool` —
whether this frame committed — and `valve_slot` asks it. ⚠️ **A predicate that predicts what another
function will do is a copy of that function**, and this one drifted because copies do. The general
form is worth stating rather than leaving as this site's detail, because it is what D519 and D523
were one abstraction level down: a valve that *re-implements* a valve rather than one that predicts
it.

⚠️ **What the return value means, exactly, and it is not "the document changed".** It is
`EditorSession::commit`'s own answer — *"the commit took"* — which is `true` even when D428's
`changes_nothing` drops the transaction underneath it, because that is what `commit_edit` has always
documented. That is the right question for both readers: `valve_slot` asks *"has the edit ended?"*
and then compares the colour itself.

Two tests in `app.rs · mod edit_valve_report_tests`:
`the_valve_reports_true_on_one_frame_and_it_is_not_a_keystroke` and `an_escaped_edit_reports_nothing`.
The flip that restores the prediction is red in both, with the numbers above.

⚠️ **Two measured facts are recorded in that module so a later reader does not take either for a
bug.** Its probe widget is a bare `egui::DragValue` and it does **not** land the typed number — the
committing frame carries the value the field started with, which is D519's one-frame-late write-back
— which is also why there is no assertion on `undo_depth` there. The real controls do not have that
problem, and that was **checked rather than assumed**:
`inspector::scale_row_tests::a_typed_value_lands_when_the_field_is_clicked_away_from` drives
`scale_row` — a `value_field`, which every production caller uses — through the identical events and
lands 50. ⚠️ **That test also fills a real hole**: the only existing typed-value test finishes with
`Enter`, where egui applies the value and drops focus on the *same* frame, so the case where those
two frames are separated — clicking away, the ordinary way out of a field — had never been driven on
the shared valve at all.

**And the gate, which is the other half of this.**
`app.rs · valve_condition_gate::nothing_commits_on_the_expression_d316_removed` reads every `.rs`
file under `crates/`, blanks `//` comments so the prose that explains the expression does not trip
it, and fails on any `lost_focus()` with a `changed()` within 160 characters, unless a
`valve-gate-not-a-commit` marker appears in a window of sixteen lines back and four forward — the
window being that wide because a `cargo fmt`-wrapped condition puts the matched term seven to eleven
lines below the comment excusing it, measured on the five sites in the tree.

- ⚠️ **Windowed rather than line-matched, because `cargo fmt` wraps.** A condition long enough to
  matter is long enough to be split, and a line-by-line grep would have found **none of the four** —
  which is D523's own point about no single-line pattern matching all three valves, met from the
  other side.
- The exemption is a **marker in a comment beside the line**, not a path in a list, for
  `deps_forbidden`'s lesson: a list of locations rots the moment a function moves, where a marker
  travels with the line and has to be re-justified by whoever writes the next one.
- ⚠️ **Broken on purpose and it goes red**, which is `CLAUDE.md`'s move for a gate and the one that
  found two of this project's known holes: a fourth valve on the superseded expression was added to
  `inspector.rs`, `cargo fmt` wrapped it across four lines, and the gate named the file and the line.
- ⚠️ **Its first run found five lines and not one was a bug** — `inspector::interacting`, an inline
  copy of it in `canvas.rs`, the Type panel's opacity gate, `CharWrite::Valve`'s gate, and a
  `TextEdit` whose two terms sit in two *different* conditions (a text field genuinely does end on
  losing focus; D316's rule is about numeric ones). All five are marked with a sentence saying why.
  **That is this gate's whole cost and it is paid once**; what it buys is that the sixth such line
  has to be justified by whoever writes it.

§9.3 amended — its D523 bullet asked for a grep and now names the test, and the mirrored-predicate
rule sits beside it — and §9.4's *"so there is one valve again"*, three bullets from a bullet saying
there are three, now says which one it means.

**D523 — Typing a font size wrote every intermediate size to the document. *Fixed and tested
2026-09-08; Fix — the engagement latch in the third and last hand-rolled valve.***

**Not a review finding.** `panels::typography::char_valve` committed on `resp.drag_stopped() ||
resp.lost_focus() || resp.changed()` — the expression §15 D316 removed from `OndinApp::edit_valve`
and D519 removed from `inspector::multi_valve`, alive in a **third** valve. What found it was
*writing down that it existed*: D519's closing notes recommended a sentence for `edit_valve`'s doc
naming the other hand-rolled valves, and writing *"the remaining hand-rolled valve is `char_valve`"*
was enough to make somebody go and read it, and it had the same defect. **Three valves, one
expression, three separate discoveries** — D316's from a photographed undo history, D519's from a
review sweep, this one from a doc comment about D519 — **and not one of them by a gate.** The tell
was always the same literal string, and nothing in this project greps for it.

**Measured, frame by frame, before the fix.** Typing `40` into the Type panel's size field over a
20pt text node took `undo_depth` from **0 to 2**, one commit per keystroke. ⚠️ **And it is worse
than the multi card's version of the same defect, because the intermediate values are written to the
document**: the probe printed `size=4` after the first keystroke and `size=40` after the second,
both of them committed states. A size typed as `100` therefore puts a one-point line through the
artwork, then a ten-point one, each of them a real undo entry, an autosave and a crash-snapshot
write. D316's five commits all wrote the *same* final number, which is why that report needed five
undo presses photographed to see it at all; this one is on screen.

**The fix is D519's, spelled a third time.** `engaged = resp.dragged() || resp.has_focus()`, stored
under `resp.id.with("char-valve-engaged")` in `Context::data`, **read before the `gesture_cancelled`
bail**, which is D317's ordering; the commit moves to the falling edge; and `key_pressed(Escape)`
refuses it. This valve had **no refusal of any kind**, so `Escape` over a typed font size applied
the number — D315's rule reaching the last of the three.

⚠️ **And a third arm the other two valves do not have, which is the part worth reading twice.**
Several of the picker's controls reach `char_valve` through `CharWrite::Valve` as **raw sensed
regions** — the hue slider, the alpha strip — and the comment on that route already said why they
are special: *"a raw sensed region reports neither `changed` nor `lost_focus`"*. Such a control has
no focus to hold and, on a click that never becomes a drag, nothing to latch: `engaged` is false on
every frame it exists, so a falling-edge-only valve would never commit it **at all**. So a
`changed()` frame on a control that was **never engaged** still commits at once, exactly as before.

🚨 **The paragraph above is right about what the arm *does* and wrong about who reaches it, and D802
measured that rather than leaving it standing.** A click on the hue slider or the alpha strip never
enters this valve: `picker::pointer_slot` answers `if resp.clicked() { self.write_slot(…); return; }`
before it would reach `valve_slot`, so the colour commits one call earlier and *"would never commit
it at all"* was never the alternative. A drag enters the valve as the engaged arm and its release as
the falling edge — arms the other two valves already have — and on the frames this route does enter
it, `changed()` is **false**, a raw sensed region being written through `write_stop_colour` and marked
changed by nothing. **This entry's own verdict stands**: the commit condition is fixed and tested, and
that is what the entry is titled for. What does not stand is the reason the third arm was kept.

🚨 **And the arm itself is gone as of 2026-09-19 (D812).** D803 found its one real user — egui's own
clamp of a stored value outside a *ranged* field, committing an edit nobody made — and the read that
settled it is that all seven call sites are engagement-bearing while both `DragValue` helpers opt out
of that clamp (D425, D552), so it had no live user at all. **The two paragraphs above are kept as the
record of what was believed and why**, which is the whole shape of this entry: an arm kept for a
route that did not exist, deleted eleven days later once somebody wrote the test.

⚠️ **The `&& !resp.lost_focus()` argument below went with the arm and is kept for one reason** — it
is the clearest statement in this file of how a `DragValue` reports `lost_focus()` on **two**
consecutive frames, which the surviving two arms still depend on.

⚠️ **That arm needed `&& !resp.lost_focus()`, and the test measured why.** A `DragValue` reports
`lost_focus()` on **two** consecutive frames and writes its parsed edit string back on the *second*
of them. Without the guard the falling edge refuses an `Escape` on the first frame and the third arm
commits the abandoned number on the next one — `escape_abandons_a_typed_font_size` read **40** where
it asked for 20. A raw sensed region never takes focus, so it never reports losing it, and the guard
costs the arm nothing — *which was the argument when the arm was believed to be for those controls,
and it survives D802 because it is about the guard rather than about the users.*

Two tests in `typography::char_valve_tests`, driving real pointer and key events over a headless app
holding one 20pt text node: `typing_a_font_size_is_one_step_and_writes_no_size_on_the_way` and
`escape_abandons_a_typed_font_size`. `type_size_field` returns its `egui::Response` now, for the
reason `multi_number` and `scale_row` do: a widget's rect is not predictable from outside, so the
test draws the field once and finds it rather than guessing at it.

**Four flips were run, and two of them are findings about where the teeth are not:**

1. Restoring the old condition is red at the assertion taken *during* typing — and **reading 40, not
   4**, because that assertion runs after both keystrokes, so what it catches is that the document
   was written to at all; the `4` is visible only frame by frame. The count assertion below it is
   never reached.
2. Dropping the `Escape` refusal is red at the size, 40 for 20, and **green at the count** —
   abandoning and committing both spend the engagement exactly once, so a count cannot tell them
   apart.
3. ⚠️ Dropping the **remembered attribute** — the `pending` arm that holds the in-flight `CharAttr`
   across the frames between the last keystroke and the commit — **does not bite**, where the
   identical flip in `multi_valve` is red (D519's second flip). This field's widget has written `40`
   back by the frame the commit lands on, so the held value is never the one used. *Why the two
   widgets differ has not been established*, and that is the argument for keeping the memory rather
   than against it: the valve must not depend on which frame egui happens to choose, and it has
   **seven call sites** of which the tests drive one. Recorded as insurance, in the code comment and
   here.
4. ⚠️ Removing the third arm entirely: **nothing goes red in 1,042 tests.** Its users are the
   picker's raw sensed regions, and reaching one headlessly means driving the whole picker, so the
   arm is carried on the strength of `CharWrite::Valve`'s own gate comment rather than on coverage —
   *writable now and unwritten*, said in the code where the test would go and open in `roadmap.md`.
   🚨 **Re-run on 2026-09-19 and now explained: it does not bite because the named users do not
   reach the arm** (D802). The flip was read here as a coverage gap and is a reachability one — *a
   flip that does not bite says where the teeth are not, and that is sometimes because there is
   nothing there to bite.*

⚠️ **§9.2's D425 passage said `char_valve` carries no engagement latch, and it is amended rather
than quietly made true.** The latch is there now — but the third arm commits a `changed()` frame on
a control that was never engaged, which is exactly the shape of an egui-initiated rewrite, so
`clamp_existing_to_range = false` is still *the whole* of what stops the library writing a
range-clamped value to the document there. **And the durable defence against a fourth valve is the
grep, not the rule**: the same superseded expression survived in three hand-rolled valves for two
hundred entries and was found three times by three unrelated accidents, so §9.3 now asks for one.
⚠️ **For `lost_focus`, not for the expression** — it is line-wrapped in the doc comments of two of
the three valves and wrapped at a *different* point in each, so no single-line pattern matches all
three, which is the same defence failing one step down. §9.2 and §9.3 amended.

**D802 — `char_valve`'s third arm cannot be reached by the controls it was kept for. *Measured
2026-09-19; Fix — its real user is named the same day (D803) and is a hazard, so *delete the arm* is
a live proposal and the ruling is the maintainer's. The reason D523 kept it on is false and is
amended there.***

**This started as the roadmap's "writable now and unwritten" item and ended as a different
finding.** D523 kept an arm no other valve has — a `changed()` frame on a control that was **never
engaged** — for the picker's raw sensed regions, and `roadmap.md`'s *Now · Inspector* has carried the
missing test ever since, the fixture half of the excuse having gone when three modules in `picker.rs`
started driving `picker_ui` headlessly with real pointer events at measured coordinates (D540, D552,
D553). So the errand was a probe for the two sensed strips. **The test was written, and it found the
route does not exist.**

The picker's raw sensed regions — the hue slider and the alpha strip, both through `slider_track`,
and the saturation/value plane, which allocates its own `Sense::click_and_drag()` rect rather than
sharing that helper — write by `picker::write_stop_colour` →
`picker::pointer_slot`, and the first thing `pointer_slot` does after its `gesture_cancelled` bail is
`if resp.clicked() { self.write_slot(node, slot, brush); return; }`. **A click never reaches
`valve_slot`**, so it never reaches `write_char_slot`, so it never reaches `char_valve`. A *drag*
does reach it, as the engaged arm, and its release reaches it as the falling edge — both of them arms
the other two valves have. And on every frame this route enters the valve, `resp.changed()` is
**false**: a raw sensed region is written through `write_stop_colour` and is marked changed by
nothing, which is the same property the route's own gate comment states from the other side — *"a raw
sensed region reports neither `changed` nor `lost_focus`"* — and which D523 read as the argument
**for** the arm rather than against it.

**Measured, not reasoned.** All three arms instrumented with `eprintln!` and the click driven through
a real picker over a real text layer: every entry printed `changed=false dragged=false focus=false
lost_focus=false engaged=false was=false` — **no arm taken** — while the colour committed anyway, one
call earlier, in `write_slot`. Flipping the third arm out entirely leaves the new test green **and the
whole suite green** — 1,301 tests on 2026-09-19 against the 1,042 D523 measured on 2026-09-08, two
readings of a suite that grew in between rather than one number restated. That is D523's own fourth
flip re-run, with the same answer and now with a reason for it.

**So what is owed is not a test but a question.** *Does anything reach this arm at all?* `char_valve`
has **seven** call sites and this measures one of them, so the honest state is that the only users
anybody had written down are ruled out and the rest are unexamined. ⚠️ **§9.2's argument for
`clamp_existing_to_range(false)` is a different question and does not fall with this one**: that
passage turns on the arm's *predicate* — a `changed()` frame on a control holding no focus is exactly
the shape of an egui-initiated rewrite — where this entry is about who arrives at it, and an idle
rewrite of a valved `DragValue` is a candidate nobody has measured either. **Delete the arm, or find
and document its real user.** Nothing was changed to pre-empt that ruling.

🚨 **That candidate was measured hours later and it is the arm's user** (§15 **D803**). Removing
`ui::value_field_f64`'s `clamp_existing_to_range(false)` and instrumenting the three arms again on the
Type panel's tracking field, **the third arm fires**: egui's own per-frame clamp of a stored value
outside a *ranged* field marks the response changed on a control holding no focus, so it walks past
`engaged` and `was_engaged` into `commit_edit`. The picker half of this entry stands untouched — what
it was missing is that the arm's user is not a control at all but the library. ⚠️ **And it is a hazard
rather than a feature**: that rewrite is `[S6.2-L1-01]`'s idle-frame clamp, and this arm is the
mechanism by which it became a committed document change and an undo step. D425's one line is the
whole of what keeps the user from existing in the shipped tree. **The ruling above is better informed,
not answered**: *delete the arm* is now a specific proposal — a second defence against a bug D425
already closes — and *keep it* is keeping a route whose only known user something else has to hold
shut. ⚠️ Two of the seven call sites are measured now, so *only known user* is still the honest
phrase. **Still the maintainer's ruling, and still nothing changed to pre-empt it.**

🚨 **Ruled 2026-09-19: the arm is deleted (D812).** What decided it was neither of the two
measurements but a **read** of the remaining five call sites — all seven are engagement-bearing, and
both `DragValue` helpers opt out of egui's clamp (D425, **D552**), so the arm had no live user of any
kind. *"Seven call sites, two measured"* is seven read, and the *only known user* hedge above is
discharged. The argument that settled it is the asymmetry: a caller that needed the arm fails loudly,
keeping it fails silently.

⚠️ **Two fixture facts, both found the hard way, and the first is why this took a sweep.** A text node
selected is not enough: `PaintSlot::TextColor` **orphans the picker** unless `type_menu` is on the
Character tab, because the slot is only *shown* there and `picker_ui`'s orphan match is doing exactly
what it is for. Without that line `app.picker` is `None` by the second frame and every click in a
5 × 66 position sweep lands on nothing — **which reads exactly like "the click does not work"** and is
the fixture not being in the state the test is about, so the test asserts the picker is still open
before it clicks. And the coordinate is measured rather than derived: with the picker spawned at
(400, 300), (500, 344) is on the **saturation/value plane**. The same sweep says what is *not* there —
no column in x ∈ {420…600} over y ∈ [280, 800] ever moved the hue off red — so **the hue strip's own
band is still unlocated**, recorded here so the next person does not re-run that sweep to learn it.

What landed is `picker::text_colour_route_tests::a_click_on_the_picker_writes_a_text_layers_colour`,
an end-to-end test of the route that *is* taken and had no test either: a click at the measured
coordinate on a real picker writes the text layer's colour, and it is **one** undo step rather than a
preview left on the floor. D523's third-arm paragraphs and its index row are amended rather than left
standing, and §9.3's copy of them with it. `roadmap.md`'s bullet was **re-scoped rather than struck**
— the test it asked for is written; the question under it was open — and the *Now · Inspector* table
row that called this *"the one the picker's raw sensed regions need"* is corrected with it. **Both
are struck outright on 2026-09-19 by D812**, which takes the ruling.

**D522 — One drop of N image files was N undo steps. *Fixed and tested 2026-09-07; Fix — a
transaction-returning half of `create_image_at`, and a document advanced as the batch is built.***

`[S16.3-L2-02]`, Medium. `app::drop_images_at` called `canvas::create_image_at` per file, and that
commits its own transaction. Three PNGs dragged in together placed three layers, said *"Placed 3
images"* **once**, and left `undo_depth` at **3**: one `Ctrl+Z` removed the last picture and left the
other two, and only the last was selected, so there was not even a selection to delete the rest with.
§9.3's invariant 5 is one gesture, one transaction, one undo step, and a drop is one gesture —
`take_dropped_images` reads one frame's `raw.dropped_files` and hands the whole batch over. The
function's own doc already called it *"N files arrive at one point"* on the way to committing N
times.

⚠️ **`commit_run` cannot merge these either**, for D521's reason with a different operation:
`CreateNode.overwrites()` is `None`, so `shape` is `None` and the merge is refused. That is the
second structural verb outside `dispatch` the run mechanism cannot reach, and it is reported here
rather than left as an aside because the two together are what make the general rule in D521 a rule.

`canvas::image_tx(over, image, world)` is the transaction-returning half `create_image_at` now calls.
**`over` is the document to read *structure* from** — the child count that becomes the new node's
index, the sibling names a free name is chosen against, and whether the blob is already embedded — so
